AGENCY:
Coast Guard, Department of Homeland Security.
ACTION:
Temporary final rule.
SUMMARY:
The Coast Guard is establishing a temporary safety zone for navigable waters on the Monongahela River from Mile Marker 15 to Mile Marker 16. This safety zone is necessary to protect personnel and vessels from potential hazards on navigable waters during an operation to install aerial transverse wirelines. Entry of vessels or persons into this zone is prohibited unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Marine Safety Unit Pittsburgh or their designated representative or their designated representative.
DATES:
This rule is effective without actual notice from November 17, 2026 through November 19, 2026. For the purposes of enforcement, actual notice will be used from November 16, 2026, through November 17, 2026. The temporary safety zone will be enforced from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day during this period.
ADDRESSES:
To view available documents go to
https://www.regulations.gov
and search for USCG-2026-1407.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
If you have questions about this rule, contact LT Lionel Babin, MSU Pittsburgh Waterways Management Division, U.S. Coast Guard; telephone 206-815-6224, or email
lionel.t.babin@uscg.mil
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:

II. Background and Authority
On October 19, 2026 an organization notified the Coast Guard that it will be installing aerial transverse wirelines over the Monongahela River from Mile Marker 15 to Mile Marker 16 from
(
printed page 73671)
November 16, 2026 until November 19, 2026. The installation will take place from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day with periods of time to allow traffic to transit. Hazards associated with this work include the use of heavy equipment which will obstruct vessel traffic. The Captain of the Port (COTP) Pittsburgh has determined that potential hazards associated with this work are a safety concern for anyone in this area of the Monongahela River. The COTP is issuing this rule under the authority in
46 U.S.C. 70034
, which is needed to protect personnel and vessels in the navigable waters within the safety zone.
Because of these potential hazards, the Coast Guard is issuing this rule without prior notice and comment. As is authorized by
5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)
, the Coast Guard finds that good cause exists for not publishing a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) with respect to this rule because it is impracticable. The Coast Guard was notified of this event on October 19, 2026, but we must establish this safety zone by November 16, 2026, to protect personnel and vessels. Therefore, we do not have enough time to solicit and respond to comments.
For the same reason, the Coast Guard finds that under
5 U.S.C. 553(d)(3)
, good cause exists for making this rule effective less than 30 days after publication in the
Federal Register
.
III. Discussion of the Rule
This rule establishes a safety zone that will be enforced from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. on each day from November 16, 2026 through November 19, 2026. The safety zone will cover the navigable water in the Monongahela River at Mile Marker 15 to Mile Marker 16. Vessels and persons will not be allowed to enter the zone during this time, unless authorized by the Captain of the Port.
IV. Regulatory Analyses
We developed this rule after considering numerous statutes and Executive orders related to rulemaking. Below we summarize our analyses based on a number of these statutes and Executive orders.
A. Impact on Small Entities
The regulatory flexibility analysis provisions of the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980,
5 U.S.C. 601-612
, do not apply to rules that are not subject to notice and comment. Because the Coast Guard has, for good cause, waived the notice and comment requirement that would otherwise apply to this rulemaking, the Regulatory Flexibility Act's flexibility analysis provisions do not apply here.
Under section 213(a) of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996 (
Pub. L. 104-121
), if this rule will affect your small business, organization, or governmental jurisdiction and you have questions, contact the person listed in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section.
The National Ombudsman resolves concerns of uneven or excessive federal regulatory enforcement. Reviews are confidential and do not waive the right to pursue administrative appeals or any other legal action. Contact 1-888-REG-FAIR (1-888-734-3247) or
Ombudsman@SBA.gov
.
B. Collection of Information
This rule will not call for a new collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3520
).
C. Federalism and Indian Tribal Governments
We have analyzed this rule under
Executive Order 13132
, Federalism, and have determined that it is consistent with the fundamental federalism principles and preemption requirements described in that Order.
Also, this rule does not have tribal implications under
Executive Order 13175
, Consultation and Coordination with Indian Tribal Governments, because it does not have a substantial direct effect on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal Government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes.
D. Unfunded Mandates Reform Act
As required by The Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (
2 U.S.C. 1531-1538
), the Coast Guard certifies that this rule will not result in an annual expenditure of $100,000,000 or more (adjusted for inflation) by a State, local, or tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector.
E. Environment
We have analyzed this rule under Department of Homeland Security Directive 023-01, Rev. 1, associated implementing instructions, and Environmental Planning COMDTINST 5090.1 (series), which guide the Coast Guard in complying with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (
42 U.S.C. 4321
et seq.
), and have determined that this action is one of a category of actions that do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment.
This rule is a safety zone. It is categorically excluded from further review under paragraph L60(a) of Appendix A, Table 1 of DHS Instruction Manual 023-01-001-01, Rev. 1. A Record of Environmental Consideration supporting this determination is available in the docket.

§ 165.T08-1407
Safety Zone; Monongahela River, Pittsburgh, PA.
(a)
Location.
The following area is a temporary safety zone: All waters of the Monongahela River from Mile Marker 15 to Mile Marker 16, near Pittsburgh, PA.
(b)
Definitions.
As used in this section,
designated representative
means a Coast Guard Patrol Commander, including a Coast Guard coxswain, petty officer, or other officer operating a Coast Guard vessel and a Federal, State, and local officer designated by or assisting the Captain of the Port Pittsburgh (COTP) in the enforcement of the safety zone.
(c)
Regulations.
(1) Under the general safety zone regulations in subpart C of this part, you may not enter the safety zone described in paragraph (a) of this section unless authorized by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative.
(2) To seek permission to enter, contact the COTP or the COTP's representative on VHF-FM channel 16. Those in the safety zone must comply with all lawful orders or directions given to them by the COTP or the COTP's designated representative.
(d)
Enforcement period.
This section will be enforced from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. each day from November 16, 2026, to November 19, 2026.

As provided in section 782(i) of the Act, in the

Analysis of Comments Received

see
Appendix I to this notice.
Changes Since the Preliminary Results
Based on review of the record and comments received from interested parties, we made changes to the
Preliminary Results.
Because Hongjia and Nanping Huatai refused to allow verification of their information submitted in this segment of the proceeding, we determine that Hongjia's and Nanping Huatai's data could not be verified pursuant to section 776(a)(2)(D) of the Act. Further, due to Hongjia's and Nanping Huatai's failure to cooperate by not acting to the best of their ability to comply with a request for information, we find that the application of facts available with an adverse inference (AFA) is warranted, pursuant to sections 776(a) and 776(b)(1)(A) of the Act. Accordingly, as Commerce determines that Hongjia's and Nanping Huatai's responses in this proceeding are unverifiable, and the application of AFA is appropriate, we conclude that the respondents did not demonstrate eligibility for a separate rate in this review and, thus, are considered part of the China-wide entity for these final results. For further details on the changes since the
Preliminary Results, see
the Issues and Decision Memorandum.
In the
Preliminary Results,
Commerce also assigned a weighted-average of the mandatory respondents' rates to the non-selected separate rate companies. For these final results, because the information provided by the mandatory companies has not been verified and we are applying AFA, we are assigning a separate rate calculated in the most recently completed review of the
Order. See
the Issues and Decision Memorandum for further discussion.
Separate Rates
In the
Preliminary Results,
we preliminarily granted a separate rate to both mandatory respondents. However, because we were unable to verify information submitted by the two mandatory respondents, Hongjia and Nanping Huatai, regarding their eligibility for a separate rate, we find this information unreliable. Therefore, we determine that Hongjia and Nanping Huatai are not eligible for a separate rate and find them to be part of the China-Wide entity.
For the companies eligible for a separate rate in this review, we relied on the weighted-average dumping margin calculated for non-examined separate rate companies in the previous administrative review of the
Order

ad valorem

Disclosure
Normally, Commerce discloses to interested parties the calculations performed in connection with the final results of review within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the date of publication of the notice of final results in the
Federal Register
, in accordance with
19 CFR 351.224(b)
. However, because we determine that Hongjia and Nanping Huatai to be part of the China-Wide entity and subject to the China-wide entity rate which is not subject to change, there are no calculations to disclose.
Assessment Rates
Pursuant to section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act and
19 CFR 351.212(b)(1)
, Commerce has determined, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) shall assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries of subject merchandise in accordance with the final results of this review. For the companies listed above, which have been assigned a weighted-average dumping margin that is not zero or
de minimis
(
i.e.,
less than 0.5 percent), Commerce will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries of subject merchandise at a rate equal to the weighted-average dumping margin assigned to the companies. The companies eligible for a separate rate have been assigned a rate of 37.24 percent, which is the non-selected separate rate from
Millworks AR3.
[
14
]
Additionally, we will instruct CBP to apply the China-wide entity rate of 220.87 percent to all POR entries of subject merchandise exported by the China-wide entity.
Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication in the
Federal Register
of these final results. If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (
i.e.,
within 90 days of publication).
Cash Deposit Requirements
The following cash deposit requirements will be effective upon publication of these final results for all shipments of the subject merchandise from China entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the publication date of these final results, as provided by section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act: (1) for the companies eligible for a separate rate identified in the table above, the cash deposit rate will be equal to the weighted-average dumping margin listed in the table above; (2) for all Chinese exporters of subject merchandise that have not been found to be entitled to a separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate for the China-wide entity (
i.e.,
220.87 percent); and (3) for all non-Chinese exporters of subject merchandise which have not received their own separate rate, the cash deposit rate will be the rate applicable to the Chinese exporter that supplied that non-Chinese exporter. These cash deposit requirements, when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.
Notification to Importers Regarding the Reimbursement of Duties
This notice also serves as a final reminder to importers of their responsibility under
19 CFR 351.402(f)(2)
to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this POR. Failure to comply with this requirement could result in Commerce's presumption that reimbursement of antidumping and/or countervailing duties has occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties and/or an increase in the amount of antidumping duties by the amount of the countervailing duties.
Administrative Protective Order (APO)
This notice also serves as a reminder to parties subject to an APO of their responsibility concerning the return or destruction of proprietary information disclosed under APO in accordance with
19 CFR 351.305(a)(3)
, which continues to govern business proprietary information in this segment of the proceeding. Timely written notification of the return or destruction of APO materials, or conversion to judicial protective order, is hereby requested. Failure to comply with the regulations and terms of an APO is a violation which is subject to sanction.
Notification to Interested Parties
We are issuing and publishing these final results of administrative review and notice in accordance with sections 751(a)(1) and 777(i) of the Act.

On the basis of the record
[
1
]
developed in the subject investigations, the United States International Trade Commission (“Commission”) determines, pursuant to the Tariff Act of 1930 (“the Act”), that there is a reasonable indication that an industry in the United States is materially injured by reason of imports of corrugated die-cut cardboard boxes from China, Malaysia, and Turkey, provided for in subheading 4819.10.00 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States, that are alleged to be sold in the United States at less than fair value (“LTFV”) and alleged to be subsidized by the Government of Turkey.
[
2 3
]
Commencement of Final Phase Investigations
Pursuant to section 207.18 of the Commission's rules, the Commission also gives notice of the commencement of the final phase of its investigations. The Commission will issue a final phase notice of scheduling, which will be published in the
Federal Register
as provided in § 207.21 of the Commission's rules, upon notice from the U.S. Department of Commerce (“Commerce”) of affirmative preliminary determinations in the investigations under §§ 703(b) or 733(b) of the Act, or, if the preliminary determinations are negative, upon notice of affirmative final determinations in those investigations under §§ 705(a) or 735(a) of the Act. Parties that filed entries of appearance in the preliminary phase of the investigations need not enter a separate appearance for the final phase of the investigations. Industrial users, and, if the merchandise under investigation is sold at the retail level, representative consumer organizations have the right to appear as parties in Commission antidumping and countervailing duty investigations. The Secretary will prepare a public service list containing the names and addresses of all persons, or their representatives, who are parties to the investigations. As provided in section 207.20 of the Commission's rules, the Director of the Office of Investigations will circulate draft questionnaires for the final phase of the investigations to parties to the investigations, placing copies on the Commission's Electronic Document Information System (EDIS,
https://edis.usitc.gov
), for comment.
Background
On September 9, 2026, the American Pizza Boxes Manufacturers Coalition
[
4
]
and the United Steel, Paper and Forestry, Rubber, Manufacturing, Energy, Allied Industrial and Service Workers International Union filed petitions with the Commission and Commerce, alleging that an industry in the United States is materially injured or threatened with material injury by reason of subsidized imports of corrugated die-cut cardboard boxes from Turkey and LTFV imports of corrugated die-cut cardboard boxes from China, Malaysia, and Turkey. Accordingly, effective September 9, 2026, the Commission instituted countervailing and antidumping duty investigation Nos. 701-TA-806 and 731-TA-1805-1807 (Preliminary).
Notice of the institution of the Commission's investigations and of a public conference to be held in connection therewith was given by posting copies of the notice in the Office of the Secretary, U.S. International Trade Commission, Washington, DC, and by publishing the notice in the
Federal Register
of September 14, 2026 (
91 FR 58174
), as revised on October 8, 2026 (
91 FR 64401
). The Commission conducted its conference on September 30, 2026. All persons who requested the opportunity were permitted to participate.
The Commission made these determinations pursuant to §§ 703(a) and 733(a) of the Act (
19 U.S.C. 1671b(a)
and
1673b(a)
). It completed and filed its determinations in these investigations on November 13, 2026. The views of the Commission are contained in USITC Publication 5810 (November 2026), entitled
Corrugated Die-Cut Cardboard Boxes from China, Malaysia, and Turkey: Investigation Nos. 701-TA-806 and 731-TA-1805-1807 (Preliminary).
By order of the Commission.
Issued: November 13, 2026.

Needs and Uses:
Section 222 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended,
47 U.S.C. 222
, establishes the duty of telecommunications carriers to protect the confidentiality of its customers' proprietary information. This proprietary information (CPNI) includes personally identifiable information derived from a customer's relationship with a provider of telecommunications services. This information collection implements the statutory obligations of Section 222. These regulations impose safeguards to protect Customer Proprietary Network Information (CPNI) and other customer proprietary information against unauthorized access and disclosure.
On November 16, 2023, the FCC released the
SIM Swap and Port-Out Fraud Order
(
88 FR 85794
(December 8, 2023)), which adopted a baseline framework to combat SIM swap fraud by amending section 64.2010 of the CPNI rules to add paragraph (h) on Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) changes and adds new information collection requirements in paragraphs (h)(2) through (6) and (h)(8) of that rule. A SIM swap involves the fraudulent transfer (or “swap”) of an account from a device associated with one SIM to a device associated with a different SIM, allowing a bad actor to control the victim's mobile account and access the victim's CPNI. The new rules establish a uniform framework that gives wireless providers flexibility to implement customer authentication and security methods to address SIM swap fraud. The
SIM Swap and Port-Out Fraud Order
modifies the existing CPNI collection requirements to require wireless providers to: (1) adopt processes for responding to failed authentication attempts in connection with a SIM change request; (2) immediately notify customers of any requests for a SIM change associated with the customer's account before the SIM change is completed; (3) offer all customers, at no cost, the option to lock or freeze their account to stop SIM change requests; (4) provide customers with advance notice of any account protection measures offered; (5) maintain a clear process for customers to report SIM fraud, promptly investigate and remediate fraud, and promptly provide customers with documentation of fraud involving their accounts; and (6) track and maintain for three years a record of SIM change requests and authentication measures used.

SUMMARY:
The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSM) announce that a draft environmental assessment (EA) is available for public review for the Falkirk Mining Company's Federal coal lease-by-application (LBA) for Falkirk Mine, serial number NDMT 106782389, and mining plan for the proposed NDMT 106782389. The BLM also announces that a public hearing will be held to receive comments on the Fair Market Value (FMV), Maximum Economic Recovery (MER), and on factors that may affect the FMV and MER determinations of the coal resources contained in the proposed LBA lease tracts. The BLM and OSM take these actions in compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, as amended; the Mineral Leasing Act, as amended; and the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976, as amended.

The draft EA will be available on November 17, 2026. To receive due consideration, written comments on the FMV and MER must be received by the BLM Montana/Dakotas State Office no later than December 17, 2026.
A public hearing will be held on December 16, 2026 from 3 p.m. until 5 p.m.
ADDRESSES:
The public hearing will be held at the Underwood City Hall, 88 Lincoln Ave., Underwood, ND 58576. Any updates to the public hearing will be provided through the ePlanning project website and a press release.
The draft EA and documents pertinent to this proposal are available for review on the BLM ePlanning project website at
https://eplanning.blm.gov/​Project-Home/​?id=​e52d7cb7-1509-f111-8406-001dd8029ed0

.

AGENCY:
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
SUMMARY:
FAA proposes to modernize its payment systems to require electronic payments and eliminate the option to pay by paper payment methods such as cash, money orders, and paper checks. This proposal complies with
Executive Order 14247
titled “Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account,” which seeks to increase the efficiency of the Federal Government by phasing out paper receipts and mandating electronic payments to and from agencies.
DATES:
Send comments on or before January 4, 2027.
ADDRESSES:
Send comments identified by docket number FAA-2026-3538 using any of the following methods:
Federal eRulemaking Portal:
Go to
www.regulations.gov
and follow the online instructions for sending your comments electronically.
Mail:
Send comments to Docket Operations, U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Room W58-213, West Building 5th Floor, Washington, DC 20590-0001.
Hand Delivery or Courier:
Take comments to Docket Operations in Room W58-213 of the West Building 5th Floor at 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
Fax:
Fax comments to Docket Operations at (202) 493-2251.
Docket:
Background documents or comments received may be read at
www.regulations.gov
at any time. Follow the online instructions for accessing the docket or go to the Docket Operations in Room W58-213 of the West Building 5th Floor at 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590 between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Sierra Elam, Office of Rulemaking, ARM-200, Federal Aviation Administration, 800 Independence Avenue SW, Washington, DC 20591; (202) 267-7627;
sierra.e.elam@faa.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Executive Summary
A. Overview of Proposed Rule
In accordance with Executive Order (E.O.) 14247 titled “Modernizing Payments To and From America's Bank Account”,
[
1
]
FAA proposes to amend its regulations to stop accepting paper payments, such as cash, money orders, and paper checks, and require electronic payments instead. FAA proposes to amend payment provisions located in
Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations
(14 CFR) parts 13, 47, 49, 61, 63, 65, 187, and 406. These payment provisions cover aviation and commercial space transportation-related civil penalties, aircraft registration fees, fees for aircraft recording, duplicate airmen and medical certificates, duplicate knowledge test reports, overflight fees, and FAA services performed outside of the United States.
Sections 47.17, 49.15, 61.29, 63.16, 65.16, and 406.9 only list the option to pay fees by paper payment methods. However, §§ 13.15, 13.16, 13.18, and 187.15 allow for both electronic and paper payment options. FAA proposes to amend these sections to require electronic payments and eliminate the use of paper payment methods.
E.O. 14247
directs the Secretary of the Treasury to review and revise procedures for granting limited exceptions where electronic methods are not feasible. Consistent with
E.O. 14247
, FAA proposes to allow another payment method in circumstances where another method is otherwise authorized by law.
FAA also proposes to revise the following guidance documents to remove references to paper payment methods: Advisory Circular (AC) Form 8050-1B; AC Form 8050-5; and AC Form 8060-56. FAA will post the drafts of these guidance document revisions to this NPRM's docket for public comment.
B. Statement of the Problem
FAA currently processes paper and electronic payment methods, where applicable. Section 3(c) of
E.O. 14247
requires all payments made to agencies to be processed electronically, eliminating the need for processing paper payments by phasing out paper disbursements and receipts.
Title 14 of the CFR
does not mention paper disbursements issued by FAA, and FAA generally does not issue them. In limited circumstances, however, FAA has issued paper checks, such as for witness fees during litigation, if the witness requests a paper payment. In current practice, FAA requests customers use the United States Treasury Department's website,
Pay.gov,
to pay the fees and penalties listed in §§ 13.15, 13.16, 13.18, 47.17, 49.15, 61.29, 63.16, 65.16, 187.15, and 406.9. Although FAA requests customers use
Pay.gov
for the fees and penalties described in this NPRM, the regulatory text in 14 CFR diverges from this current practice.
(
printed page 73706)
As a result, FAA proposes to amend its regulations to accept and process electronic payment methods only for all fees and penalties under 14 CFR. FAA also proposes to revise its guidance documents to direct the use of electronic payment methods rather than paper payment methods. These amendments and revisions would standardize FAA's regulations with current practice and guidance. Consistent with
E.O. 14247
, this proposal is intended to increase government efficiency and reduce the burdens of processing paper payments for the regulatory community.
C. Summary of the Costs and Benefits
The proposed rule would result in annual cost savings of $99,815 for FAA by eliminating the need to process paper payments. Over five years, these savings sum to $457,125 at three percent discounting, or $409,262 at seven percent discounting, or annualized value of $99,815 (regardless of discounting). The proposed rule would result in $1,425,933 in cost savings in perpetuity.
FAA expects the costs to customers to be de minimis to transition from paper to electronic payments.
II. Authority for This Rulemaking
FAA's authority to issue rules regarding aviation safety, including those governing charging and receiving fees for certain services provided by FAA, is found in title 49 of the United States Code. Subtitle I, Chapter 1, Section 106 describes the authority of the FAA Administrator. Subtitle VII, Aviation Programs, describes in more detail the scope of the agency's authority.
This rulemaking is issued under the authority described in Subtitle VII, Part A—Air Commerce and Safety, Chapter 441—Registration and Recordation of Aircraft, Sections 44101—44106, Section 44107, Recordation of conveyances, leases, and security instruments, Chapter 445—Facilities, Personnel, and Research, Section 44506, Air traffic controllers, Chapter 447—Safety Regulation, Section 44702, Issuance of certificates, Section 44703, Airman Certificates, Section 44728, Flight attendant certification, Section 44748, Aircraft dispatching, Chapter 453—Fees, and Chapter 463—Penalties, Section 46301, Civil penalties. Under those statutory provisions, FAA is charged with prescribing regulations to promote safety in civil air commerce, issuing certificates, charging and receiving fees for such services, and assessing civil penalties. This regulation addresses matters within the scope of that authority.
The Commercial Space Launch Act of 1984, as amended and codified at
51 U.S.C. 50901-50924
(the Act), authorizes the Secretary of Transportation (Secretary) to oversee, license, and regulate commercial launch and reentry activities, and the operation of launch and reentry sites within the U.S. or as carried out by U.S. citizens. Section 50905 directs the Secretary to exercise this responsibility consistent with public health and safety, safety of property, and the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States. In addition, section 50903 requires the Secretary to encourage, facilitate, and promote commercial space launches and reentries by the private sector. Section 50917 provides the Secretary with civil penalty authority for violations falling under Section 50917(a). As codified in
49 CFR 1.83(b)
, the Secretary has delegated authority to the Administrator to carry out these functions.
III. Background
A. History of Payments to FAA
FAA has collected payments for a variety of services since its inception. Historically, these payments have been made by paper methods to FAA. In 1997, FAA began accepting payments electronically for air traffic services for certain flights operating through the National Airspace System (NAS),
[
2
]
by amending § 187.15(d). Since 1997, FAA's regulations have only been amended twice to accept electronic payments. In 2007, FAA amended § 187.15(a) to allow the use of credit card to pay fees for certification services performed outside the United States.
[
3
]
This action standardized the authorized payment methods for services in part 187. In 2021, FAA amended §§ 13.15(c), 13.16(l), and 13.18(j) to accept electronic payments for civil penalties.
[
4
]
In current practice, FAA accepts payments for these services and penalties through
Pay.gov
. FAA also accepts electronic payments for fees listed in §§ 47.17, 49.15, 61.29, 63.16, 65.16, and 406.9, even though the regulatory language for each section does not mention the ability to pay by electronic methods.
IV. Discussion of the Proposal
This rulemaking proposes to conform FAA's regulations to the directive in
E.O. 14247
to phase out paper check disbursements and receipts. FAA regulations do not include paper check disbursements, so this rule updates regulations related to paper receipts. The proposed amendments described in this section would require payments made to FAA to be collected and processed electronically
[
5
]
and eliminate the use of paper payment methods unless an exception applies as specified in section 4 of
E.O. 14247
. This section of the NPRM also describes the proposed revisions to guidance documents associated with the proposed regulatory amendments.
A. Proposed Amendments to Investigative and Enforcement Procedures in Part 13
Part 13 contains procedures for compromising some civil penalties before referring them to the United States Attorney General for prosecution, as well as for assessing other civil penalties administratively, depending on the amount of the civil penalty. FAA currently collects payments for these civil penalties through electronic and paper payment methods. The methods for paying civil penalties are located in §§ 13.15(c)(2)(i), 13.16(l)(1)(i) and (ii), and 13.18(j)(1)(i) and (ii). FAA proposes to streamline these conditions by requiring electronic payments and eliminating the option to pay by paper methods, unless another payment method is otherwise authorized by law.
1. Proposed § 13.15, Civil Penalties Other Than by Administrative Assessment
Civil penalties under § 13.15 pertain to those FAA may settle before referring them to the United States Attorney General for prosecution. These civil penalties are in an amount that exceeds FAA's statutory authority to assess (see
49 U.S.C. 46301(d)(4)
). Section 13.15(c)(2)(i) states that persons cited with an alleged violation may respond to a proposed civil penalty by submitting an electronic payment, certified check, or money order. The person who paid the civil penalty will then be sent a letter from an FAA
(
printed page 73707)
attorney stating the payment settles the action the person was cited with.
FAA proposes to amend § 13.15(c)(2)(i) to remove the option to pay by certified check or money order. Proposed paragraph (2)(i) would require persons to pay civil penalties under this section by electronic payment unless another payment method is otherwise authorized by law.
2. Proposed § 13.16, Civil Penalties Against Miscellaneous Persons and All Persons for Hazardous Materials Violations
Section 13.16 pertains to civil penalties for all violations, including hazardous materials violations, assessed to persons other than individuals acting as a pilot, flight engineer, mechanic, or repairman. Section 13.16(l)(1)(i) and (ii) describe the options for how to pay these civil penalties. Paragraph (l)(1)(i) lists the option to pay penalties by paper payment and paragraph (l)(1)(ii) lists the option to pay by electronic payment. Both paragraphs direct persons paying a civil penalty under § 13.16 to follow the directions listed in the notice of proposed civil penalty, final notice of proposed civil penalty, or the order assessing civil penalty.
FAA proposes to remove paragraphs (l)(1)(i) and (ii) from § 13.16 and revise paragraph (l)(1) to require electronic payments when a person pays a civil penalty unless another payment method is otherwise authorized by law. This proposed change would eliminate the option to pay civil penalties under § 13.16 by paper payment. FAA also proposes to add “compromise order” to the regulatory text in proposed § 13.16(l)(1) because compromise orders are another type of document that involve a civil penalty payment under § 13.16. In addition, the proposed § 13.16(l)(1) text would replace the word “in” with “for” when referencing the directions specified for the notice of proposed civil penalty, final notice of proposed civil penalty, order assessing civil penalty, or compromise order. Civil penalty payment instructions are not necessarily in these documents and might be provided separately by FAA.
3. Proposed § 13.18, Civil Penalties Against Pilots, Flight Engineers, Mechanics, or Repairmen
Civil penalties under § 13.18 pertain to those assessed for violations listed under
49 U.S.C. 46301(d)(2)
made by individuals acting as pilots, flight engineers, mechanics, or repairmen. Section 13.18(j)(1)(i) and (ii) contain the details on how to pay these civil penalties. Both paragraphs refer the cited person to the order of assessment for details and directions on how to pay the penalty. Section 13.18(j)(1)(i) lists the option to pay via paper payment and § 13.18(j)(1)(ii) lists the option to pay by electronic payment. Similar to the proposed changes in § 13.16, FAA proposes to remove § 13.18(j)(1)(i) and (ii) and revise § 13.18(j)(1) to require electronic payments to be made based on the directions specified in the notice of proposed assessment, the order of assessment, or the compromise order, unless another payment method is otherwise authorized by law. FAA proposes to add “notice of proposed assessment” and “compromise order” to the regulatory text in § 13.18(j)(1) because these documents can also involve civil penalty payments under § 13.18. In addition, proposed § 13.18(j)(1) would replace the word “in” with “for” when referencing the directions specified for the notice of proposed assessment, order of assessment, or compromise order. Civil penalty payment instructions are not necessarily in these documents and might be provided separately by FAA. This proposed change would eliminate the option to pay § 13.18 civil penalties by paper payment.
B. Proposed § 47.17, Aircraft Registration Fees
The FAA Registry (Registry) collects fees for a variety of services in § 47.17(a). These services include applications for: certificate of aircraft registration; dealer's aircraft registration certificate; additional dealer's aircraft registration certificate issued to the same dealer; special registration number; changing, reassigning, or reserving a special registration number; replacement certificate of aircraft registration; and renewal certificate of aircraft registration. Section 47.17(b) requires applications for any of the previously listed services be accompanied by a check or money order. Despite the regulatory text at § 47.17, the Registry currently accepts electronic payments for aircraft registration services through its online portal, Civil Aircraft Registry Electronic Services (CARES), and
Pay.gov
.
FAA proposes to remove the phrase “check and money order” in § 47.17(b) and insert the phrase “electronic payment” in its place. This revision would eliminate the requirement to pay aircraft registration fees by paper payment unless such payment methods are otherwise authorized by law and would codify current electronic payment practices into 14 CFR.
C. Proposed § 49.15, Fees for Recording Aircraft Titles and Security Documents
FAA collects fees for recording conveyances of aircraft, aircraft engines, and propellers under part 49. Depending on the conveyance, FAA requests persons send in FAA Form AC 8050-98 or their original claim of lien, accompanied by check or money order. Similar to the current practice for § 47.17, the Registry instructs persons pay § 49.15 fees by electronic methods by navigating to the CARES portal, which then directs them to
Pay.gov
. FAA proposes to revise § 49.15 to require electronic payments for fees for recording aircraft conveyances unless another payment method is otherwise authorized by law. This revision would eliminate the requirement to pay by paper methods.

The Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (Pub. L. 96-39), as amended by the Uruguay Round Agreements Act (Pub. B. Confidential Business Information
Confidential Business Information (CBI) is commercial or financial information that is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of Information Act
(
printed page 73712)
(FOIA) (
5 U.S.C. 552
), CBI is exempt from public disclosure. If your comments responsive to this NPRM contain commercial or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that you actually treat as private, and is relevant or responsive to this NPRM, it is important you clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission containing CBI as “PROPIN.” FAA will treat such marked submissions as confidential under the FOIA, and they will not be placed in the public docket of this NPRM. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to the person in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section of this document. Any commentary FAA receives which is not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket for this rulemaking.

Abstract:
Sections 460 and 428J of the Higher Education Act of 1965, as amended (HEA) provide for teacher loan forgiveness in William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (Direct Loan) Program and the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) Program. Borrowers who teach for five consecutive years at schools or educational service agencies serving low-income families and meet certain other requirements may receive up to $17,500 in loan forgiveness. The teacher loan forgiveness regulations at
34 CFR 685.217
(for the Direct Loan Program) and
34 CFR 682.216
(for the FFEL Program) require borrowers to provide their loan holders with documentation establishing their eligibility for teacher loan forgiveness and for teacher loan forgiveness forbearance. The U.S. Department of Education (ED) is requesting no substantive changes but is making revisions to better align the forms with other similar forms and improve the borrower experience.

SUMMARY:
The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a Confirmatory Order to TRISO-X, LLC (the licensee), as a result of a successful Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mediation. On June 9, 2026, the NRC notified the licensee of an apparent violation being considered for escalated enforcement. The apparent violation involved the implementation of management measures to ensure the design basis supporting the structural stability function of the TX-1 process building's main force resisting system (MFRS) was maintained during construction. The NRC provided the licensee with the opportunity to respond through a written response, a Pre-decisional Enforcement Conference (PEC), or ADR. The licensee elected to participate in ADR, and mediation sessions were held on July 29 and August 20, 2026, during which the parties reached an Agreement in Principle. As part of the agreement, the licensee committed to taking certain corrective actions and consented to the issuance of a Confirmatory Order to make those commitments legally binding and resolve the apparent violation without further enforcement action by the NRC. The Confirmatory Order is effective upon issuance.
DATES:
The Confirmatory Order was issued on October 21, 2026.

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION
In the Matter of:
TRISO-X, LLC, TRISO-X Facility, Docket No. 07007027, License No. SNM-7007, EAF-RII-2026-0052
CONFIRMATORY ORDER MODIFYING LICENSE (EFFECTIVE UPON ISSUANCE)
I
TRISO-X, LLC (TRISO-X) is the holder of Special Nuclear Material License No. SNM-7007, issued on February 13, 2026, by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC or Commission) pursuant to Part 70 of
Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations
(10 CFR). The license authorizes TRISO-X to receive, acquire, possess, transfer, and use byproduct, source, and special nuclear material in accordance with conditions specified therein. The facility is located on the licensee's site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.
This Confirmatory Order is the result of an agreement reached during Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mediation sessions conducted on July 29, 2026, and August 20, 2026.
II
From March 9 through 12, 2026, the NRC conducted an inspection of construction activities at the TRISO-X site. As discussed in NRC Inspection Report 07007027/2026-006, dated June 9, 2026, the NRC identified an apparent violation associated with TRISO-X's failure to apply effective management measures, specifically, design control measures, to ensure the design basis supporting the structural stability function of the TX-1 process building's main force resisting system (MFRS) was maintained during construction.
In accordance with the NRC Enforcement Policy, the apparent violation was considered for escalated enforcement action on the basis of the information available to the NRC at the time of the inspection, including the following:
1. On or before January 19, 2026, the licensee approved (and later implemented) welding processes that could not meet the design specifications for the special concentrically braced frames (SCBF) forming part of the MFRS. Specifically, the licensee implemented welding processes for the construction of SCBF diagonal braces that did not achieve the qualified weld size necessary to meet the requirements of the construction code specified in the licensing basis of the facility. Consequently, multiple SCBF welds were constructed such that their available design strength was less than the strength required to meet the applicable construction code.
2. From approximately January 28, 2026, to February 16, 2026, and from February 20, 2026, to March 10, 2026, the licensee failed to conduct visual weld inspections of the structural steel in the MFRS of the TX-1 process building as required by the applicable construction code. Specifically, the field welded connections of the SCBF diagonal braces were not inspected by an authorized special inspector prior to and during welding on a random daily basis as required by the construction code. As a result, the quality of the welding operations performed over the period identified above was not verified to be in conformance with the design basis and quality requirements.
By letter dated June 9, 2026, the NRC notified TRISO-X of the results of the inspection with an opportunity to: (1) attend a Pre-decisional Enforcement Conference, (2) provide a written response to the NRC, or (3) participate in an ADR mediation session in an effort to resolve these concerns.
In response to the NRC's offer, TRISO-X requested the use of the NRC's ADR process to achieve resolution of the apparent violation. On July 29, 2026, and August 20, 2026, the NRC and TRISO-X participated in ADR mediation sessions conducted by a professional mediator, arranged through Cornell University's Institute on Conflict Resolution. The ADR process uses a neutral mediator, who has no decision-making authority, to assist the parties in resolving disputes. The ADR mediation sessions resulted in an Agreement in Principle concerning resolution of the apparent violation. This Confirmatory Order reflects the terms agreed upon through the ADR process and makes TRISO-X's commitments legally binding.
III
During the ADR sessions, TRISO-X and the NRC reached a preliminary settlement agreement called an Agreement in Principle.
The elements of the agreement include the following:
A. Definitions
1.
Braced-frame intersection welds,
as used in the Agreement in Principle and this Confirmatory Order, refers to the existing flare bevel groove field welds on the TX-1 process building that connect the diagonal braces of the special concentrically braced frames (SCBF) at their intersection, which form part of the building's Main Force Resisting System (MFRS). These are the welds characterized by the NRC as nonconforming with the original design with respect to their effective throat size and the welding process selected for their installation, as discussed in NRC Inspection Report 07007027/2026-006, dated June 9, 2026.
B. Pre-ADR Corrective Actions
Prior to the ADR sessions, TRISO-X completed the corrective actions and enhancements listed below to address the noncompliance and preclude recurrence of the apparent violation. The NRC agreed to give TRISO-X credit for these corrective actions, subject to verification through NRC inspection.
1. TRISO-X completed an apparent cause analysis for the braced-frame intersection welds using the 5-Why Cause & Effect Method to identify the cause of the potential weld nonconformance. The analysis identified the apparent cause as a shop drawing detail error which resulted in braced-frame intersection welds that did not meet the original design requirements.
2. TRISO-X conducted an extent of condition review which revealed that the issue described in Item III.A.1 of this Confirmatory Order included ten (10) SCBF in the MFRS of the TX-1 process building.
3. On April 3, 2026, TRISO-X issued a verbal Stop Work to the construction contractor for structural welding (referred to in the contractor documentation as `x-bracing' welding operations) to prevent any further potential nonconforming welds, followed by a formal confirmation of Stop Work via letter, dated April 5, 2026.
4. TRISO-X performed an analysis and calculation of the braced-frame intersection welds which determined that a 
                        7/16
                        -inch effective throat meets the design requirements (
i.e.,
demand-to-capacity ratios less than 1). TRISO-X updated the applicable design drawings to specify the use of 
                        7/16
                        -inch effective throat instead of the original 
                        5/8
                        -inch to ensure compliance with revised design requirements.
5. TRISO-X developed a Performance Qualification Record (PQR) for the Weld Procedure Specification (WPS) used in the installation of the braced-frame intersection welds to validate the WPS welding parameters, specifically to support an
(
printed page 73820)
effective throat larger than that specified in American Institute of Steel Construction (AISC) Standard 360-16, “
Specification for Structural Steel Buildings,”
Table J2.2, for the welding processes used to make the welds.
6. TRISO-X developed and implemented a qualified Ultrasonic Testing (UT) procedure for the braced-frame intersection welds to measure the as-built effective throats. TRISO-X performed UT on 100% of the braced-frame intersection welds under Nonconformance Report NCR-15. The UT results indicated that the effective throats of all braced-frame intersection welds measured equal to or greater than a 
                        7/16
                        -inch, meeting the updated design requirements.
7. TRISO-X completed an extent of condition review for all partial penetration groove welds in the TX-1 process building design drawings to identify other structural welding locations where incorrect design parameters were specified. TRISO-X identified some design drawings for pipe support welds that potentially could have led to a similar issue with the shop drawing detailing process. These design drawings were revised to clarify the design intent.
8. The Engineer of Record conducted an extent of condition review of TX-1 design and shop drawings issued at the time of discovery of the vendor shop drawing error that led to the braced-frame intersection welds nonconformance. The extent of condition review concluded that this issue was localized and did not extend to other areas of the project. TRISO-X and the Engineer of Record addressed the shop drawing review process and communicated to personnel the application of internal review standards and the lessons learned related to this event.
9. TRISO-X directed the construction contractor to revise vendor shop drawings applicable to the braced-frame intersection welds to update weld size and remove incorrect joint designation. Additionally, TRISO-X directed the construction contractor to revise vendor shop drawings for the shop welds at the intersection of the SCBF and confirmed that the WPS used for their installation met the original design requirements.
10. TRISO-X revised the construction contractor Site Specific Quality Plan to implement enhancements to the Nonconformance Report (NCR)/Corrective Action Process; integration of work planning documentation and proper identification of required inspections; and protocols for ensuring consistency of reviews of sub-suppliers.
11. TRISO-X revised the structural steel Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) to include additional witness and hold points and clear notification requirements for TRISO-X to ensure code-required special inspections are conducted prior to, during, and after welding activities.
12. Effective May 21, 2026, TRISO-X implemented a periodic Quality Control (QC) coordination meeting between TRISO-X and the appropriate TX-1 construction project contractors/subcontractors.
13. On July 7, 2026, TRISO-X held a meeting with the construction contractor and the Engineer of Record to confirm the roles and responsibilities of Special Inspectors under the 2018 Edition of the International Building Code (IBC-2018), Chapter 17. A follow-up letter documenting these responsibilities was issued on July 13, 2026, and signed by all parties.
14. TRISO-X developed a weld tracking mechanism to clearly communicate the status of the braced-frame intersection welds to internal stakeholders including Engineering, Regulatory, and Construction groups.
15. On July 15, 2026, TRISO-X performed a walkdown and visual inspection of SCBF components located on the first level of the TX-1 process building. The status of the as-built welds and open NCRs was reviewed and the results documented in a report.
16. On July 22, 2026, TRISO-X provided training to the Quality Assurance (QA) Special Inspectors to reinforce expectations for inspections, documentation, and escalation of field issues to management. This training is documented in TRISO-X CR-2026-0022-CA04.
17. On June 11, 2026, TRISO-X issued a letter to the construction contractor requiring replacement of the Quality Control subcontractor due to unacceptable performance of assigned duties for QC inspection of construction activities.
18. TRISO-X implemented a new procedure, TX0-PRO-QAS-0171, “
Construction Surveillance Program,”
to formalize the QA requirements for surveillance and oversight of contractors performing construction activities. The procedure includes two forms, Construction Surveillance Report and ITP Review Checklist, to improve consistency of documentation.
19. TRISO-X developed specific work packages for SCBF welding to incorporate the updated ITPs.
20. TRISO-X revised TXF-QAS-PLN-0016, “
Construction Quality Plan,”
to include references to additional oversight requirements and execution expectations that are implemented through new procedure TX0-PRO-QAS-0171, “
Construction Surveillance Program.”
C. Corrective Actions Agreed to in ADR
1. TRISO-X shall demonstrate, with respect to the structural stability safety function for natural phenomena hazards (NPH), that the existing braced-frame intersection welds meet the performance objectives and quality requirements of the structural codes and standards documented in TRISO-X materials license SNM-7007 and the license application incorporated by reference therein. The forces, limit states, material strengths, and resistance factors used in the design of the welded connections shall be consistent with the intended performance of the connection and the assumptions used in the design of the structure. This demonstration shall be made available to the NRC for inspection within 30 days of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order. If TRISO-X chooses to rework or replace individual components of the braced-frame or the entire braced-frame, including welded connections, then this corrective action item (Item III.C.1) does not apply to those components. The demonstration for existing conditions shall include, at a minimum, the following:
a. Technical justification demonstrating that the braced-frame intersection welds meet all applicable design requirements with the revised 
                        7/16
                        -inch effective throat
b. The WPS and associated PQRs that support the use of an effective throat larger than specified in AISC 360-16, Table J2.2, for the braced-frame intersection welds
c. Qualification records (performance demonstration) of the UT procedure used for measuring the as-built effective throat of the braced-frame intersection welds
d. Training and qualification records of the personnel who performed the UT examination of the braced-frame intersection welds
e. Examination reports for the UT performed on the braced-frame intersection welds in accordance with the qualified UT procedure
f. Training and qualification records of individuals performing QA oversight of the WPS qualification and UT examinations
g. QA oversight records of WPS qualification and the UT examination performed on the braced-frame intersection welds
2. If the NRC's review of the information provided for Item III.C.1 above concludes that TRISO-X did not successfully demonstrate that the structural stability safety function of the TX-1 process building and its braced-frame intersection welds is maintained, TRISO-X shall repair, replace, or redesign all braced-frame intersection welds to restore such function in accordance with TRISO-X materials license SNM-7007 and the license application incorporated by reference therein. TRISO-X agrees to complete this item within 6 months of the date of the NRC correspondence documenting the conclusions about Item III.C.1 of this Confirmatory Order.
3. For any future structural field welding, including rework or replace, of SCBF's flare bevel groove welds, TRISO-X will install the field welds using welding processes that conform with AISC 360-16 without exceeding the effective throat limitations in AISC 360-16, Table J2.2.
4. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will perform additional inspections (
e.g.
visual observation, non-destructive examination (NDE), or other methods as appropriate) of the completed SCBF fillet welds in the TX-1 process building which were not inspected by the welding Special Inspector before and during welding as required by AISC 341-16, “
Seismic Provisions for Structural Steel Buildings.”
TRISO-X will demonstrate that the inspection technique(s) and the results provide reasonable assurance that the fillet welds conform with the applicable design and installation requirements as specified in IBC-2018 and the applicable standards referenced therein. TRISO-X will correct any nonconforming fillet welds in accordance with the 2015 Edition of the American Welding Society (AWS) Code D1.1, “
Structural Welding Code—Steel.”
TRISO-X agrees to track implementation of the inspections and any necessary corrective
(
printed page 73821)
actions under its NCR process including a timeline for completion. If TRISO-X chooses to rework or replace any of the braced-frames or components of the SCBF, including fillet welded connections, then this corrective action item (Item III.C.4) does not apply to those components.
5. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will evaluate its existing corrective action program (CAP) against the guidance in NRC Regulatory Guide (RG) 3.75,
“Corrective Action Programs for Fuel Cycle Facilities,”
Section C, to identify and correct any gaps in its CAP with respect to the construction of the TX-1 process building. The evaluation will be formally documented, and the findings, if any, will be entered into TRISO-X's CAP for tracking and resolution, as determined to be appropriate by the licensee. The use of NRC RG 3.75 is intended to serve as a reference to help guide the evaluation and this provision is not intended to make compliance with NRC RG 3.75 a regulatory or licensing requirement.
6. Within 12 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will perform external benchmarking at another facility within the U.S. nuclear industry, either under construction or operating, to identify actionable best practices related to design control and contractor oversight activities and implement those actions for construction activities at the TRISO-X facility. TRISO-X will capture the results of this benchmarking activity in its CAP and assign action items to track their completion.
7. Within 12 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will conduct an effectiveness review of the corrective actions implemented to prevent issues similar to the design control errors leading to the issuance of this Confirmatory Order. The effectiveness review, its conclusions, and resulting follow-up actions will be entered into TRISO-X's CAP for tracking and resolution.
8. Within 3 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will revise its Contractor Management procedure to:
a. implement a sitewide construction surveillance plan to clearly describe the activities that TRISO-X construction oversight personnel shall perform and witness. With respect to oversight activities, and as applicable to the circumstances, the Contractor Management procedure will address the following:
i. assessments, surveillances, audits, and inspections
ii. identification of nonconformances
iii. development and monitoring of corrective actions
iv. review of design and field work records
v. witness points and hold points
vi. review of contractor procedures
vii. review of contractor qualifications
viii. verification that items or services conform to procurement requirements before acceptance
ix. verification of record retention to demonstrate compliance with project requirements
x. identification of organizational interfaces and division of responsibilities
b. correct issues with roles and responsibilities presented in the original revision, and
c. establish appropriate monitoring metrics for specific construction activities identified during work package review.
9. Within 2 months after placement of the second level concrete floor slabs, TRISO-X will conduct a walkdown and visually inspect the SCBF components located on the second level of the TX-1 process building. The status of the as-built welds and open NCRs will be reviewed and the results documented in a report. TRISO-X agrees to track any necessary corrective actions under its NCR process including a timeline for completion and to complete remediation work to ensure compliance with applicable codes and design requirements.
10. Within 3 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will perform an extent of condition review to identify other code-required special inspections (
e.g.,
welding, bolting, and protected zones) of the TX-1 process building MFRS and confirm that these were completed and documented in accordance with the applicable code requirements. TRISO-X agrees to track any necessary corrective actions under its NCR process including a timeline for completion and to complete remediation work to ensure compliance with applicable codes and design requirements.
11. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will provide Nuclear Safety Culture training to the TRISO-X Construction Oversight, Engineering, Regulatory, and Quality teams, including applicable construction contractor management personnel and QC/QA construction inspectors. The training will reinforce common expectations for quality, conservative decision-making, procedural compliance, questioning attitude, problem identification and resolution, Stop-Work authority, and raising safety concerns. TRISO-X agrees to maintain training materials and attendance records.
12. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will provide training for laborers and craft workers to reinforce that work execution must follow build-to-print practices using approved design documents, that work quality is essential, and that work should be stopped when there is uncertainty about the path forward. The training will be formalized and maintained as a requirement for onboarding of new laborers and craft workers involved in the construction of the TRISO-X process buildings.
13. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will conduct a lessons-learned presentation for the TRISO-X team (TRISO-X and applicable X-energy employees, contractors, and subcontractors) summarizing the apparent violation, contributing causes, corrective actions, and programmatic improvements. The presentation will provide formal internal lessons-learned to help ensure that personnel involved understand the circumstances that led to the apparent violation, reinforce expectations for future work, promote implementation of the corrective actions across the organization, and improve preparation and planning for installation of process equipment and items relied on for safety (IROFS). TRISO-X agrees to maintain presentation materials and attendance records.
14. Within 12 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will prepare a formal lessons-learned report summarizing the apparent violation, causes, corrective actions, and programmatic improvements; distribute the report to applicable TRISO-X and X-energy personnel; and present the lessons learned during an internal company briefing such as an All-Hands meeting. TRISO-X will maintain an official copy of the report in its records.
15. Within 12 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will develop a case study to highlight cross-cutting issues. This case study will be incorporated and maintained in training for new TRISO-X employees.
16. TRISO-X agrees to provide a lessons-learned presentation at the March 2027 NRC Regulatory Information Conference (RIC), or other mutually agreed forum if the RIC is not available, regarding its experience with construction of the TRISO-X facility, including the issues giving rise to this Confirmatory Order. The presentation will address, as appropriate, lessons learned regarding construction of a new fuel cycle facility; the selection, oversight, and management of contractors with limited or no prior nuclear industry experience; development and implementation of programs and processes as a new NRC licensee; and other regulatory, programmatic, and construction-related lessons learned during facility construction.
D. Agreement by Agency
Based on the completed corrective actions described in Section III.B above, and the commitments described in Section V below:
1. The NRC agrees not to issue a notice of violation for all matters discussed in the NRC's letter to TRISO-X, dated June 9, 2026 (NRC Inspection Report 07007027/2026-006, EAF-RII-2026-0052).
2. The NRC agrees not to impose a civil penalty for all matters discussed in the NRC's letter to TRISO-X, dated June 9, 2026 (NRC Inspection Report 07007027/2026-006, EAF-RII-2026-0052).
3. The NRC agrees not to consider this Confirmatory Order as an escalated enforcement action in the civil penalty assessment process for future enforcement cases involving the TRISO-X facility licensed under SNM-7007.
On October 5, 2026, TRISO-X consented to issuing this Confirmatory Order with the commitments, as described in Section V below. TRISO-X further agreed that this Confirmatory Order is to be effective upon issuance, the agreement memorialized in this Confirmatory Order settles the matter between the parties, and that TRISO-X has waived its right to a hearing.

Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will provide Nuclear Safety Culture training to the TRISO-X Construction Oversight, Engineering, Regulatory, and Quality teams, including applicable construction contractor management personnel and QC/QA construction inspectors. The training will reinforce common expectations for quality, conservative decision-making, procedural compliance, questioning attitude, problem identification and resolution, stop-work authority, and raising safety concerns. TRISO-X agrees to maintain training materials and attendance records.
12. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will provide training for laborers and craft workers to reinforce that work execution must follow build-to-print practices using approved design documents, that work quality is essential, and that work should be stopped when there is uncertainty about the path forward. The training will be formalized and maintained as a requirement for onboarding of new laborers and craft workers involved in the construction of the TRISO-X process buildings.
13. Within 6 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will conduct a lessons-learned presentation for the TRISO-X team (TRISO-X and applicable X-energy employees, contractors, and subcontractors) summarizing the apparent violation, contributing causes, corrective actions, and programmatic improvements. The presentation will provide formal internal lessons-learned to help ensure that personnel involved understand the circumstances that led to the apparent violation, reinforce expectations for future work, promote implementation of the corrective actions across the organization, and improve preparation and planning for installation of process equipment and IROFS. TRISO-X agrees to maintain presentation materials and attendance records.
14. Within 12 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will prepare a formal lessons-learned report summarizing the apparent violation, causes, corrective actions, and programmatic improvements; distribute the report to applicable TRISO-X and X-energy personnel; and present the lessons learned during an internal company briefing such as an All-Hands meeting. TRISO-X will maintain an official copy of the report in its records.
15. Within 12 months of the issuance date of this Confirmatory Order, TRISO-X will develop a case study to highlight cross-cutting issues. This case study will be incorporated and maintained in training for new TRISO-X employees.
16. TRISO-X will provide a lessons-learned presentation at the March 2027 NRC RIC, or other mutually agreed forum if the RIC is not available, regarding its experience with construction of the TRISO-X facility, including the issues giving rise to this Confirmatory Order. The presentation will address, as appropriate, lessons learned regarding construction of a new fuel cycle facility; the selection, oversight, and management of contractors with limited or no prior nuclear industry experience; development and implementation of programs and processes as a new NRC licensee; and other regulatory, programmatic, and construction-related lessons learned during facility construction.
This agreement is binding upon successors and assigns of TRISO-X, LLC. The Chief Nuclear Materials Inspector, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards, may, in writing, relax or rescind any of the above conditions upon demonstration by TRISO-X or its successors of good cause.
VI
In accordance with
10 CFR 2.202
and
10 CFR 2.309
, any person adversely affected by this Confirmatory Order, other than TRISO-X, may request a hearing within thirty (30) calendar days of the date of issuance of this Confirmatory Order. Where good cause is shown, consideration will be given to extending the time to request a hearing. A request for extension of time must be made in writing to the Chief Nuclear Materials Inspector, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards, U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, Washington, DC 20555, and include a statement of good cause for the extension.
All documents filed in NRC adjudicatory proceedings, including a request for hearing, a petition for leave to intervene, any motion or other document filed in the proceeding prior to the submission of a request for hearing or petition to intervene (hereinafter “petition”), and documents filed by interested governmental entities participating under
10 CFR 2.315(c)
, must be filed in accordance with the NRC's E-Filing rule (
72 FR 49139
; August 28, 2007, as amended at
77 FR 46562
, August 3, 2012). The E-Filing process requires participants to submit and serve all adjudicatory documents over the internet, or in some cases to mail copies on electronic storage media. Participants may not submit paper copies of their filings unless they seek an exemption in accordance with the procedures described below. Detailed guidance on making electronic submissions may be found in the Guidance for Electronic Submissions to the NRC and on the NRC website at
https://www.nrc.gov/​site-help/​e-submittals.html
.
To comply with the procedural requirements of E-Filing, at least 10 days prior to the filing deadline, the participant should contact the Office of the Secretary by email at
hearing.docket@nrc.gov
,
or by telephone at 301-415-1677, to (1) request a digital identification (ID) certificate, which allows the participant (or its counsel or representative) to digitally sign submissions and access the E-Filing system for any proceeding in which it is participating; and (2) advise the Secretary that the participant will be submitting a petition or other adjudicatory document (even in instances in which the participant, or its counsel or representative, already holds an NRC-issued digital ID certificate). Based upon this information, the Secretary will establish an electronic docket for the hearing in this proceeding if the Secretary has not already established an electronic docket.
Information about applying for a digital ID certificate is available on the NRC's public website at
https://www.nrc.gov/​site-help/​e-submittals/​getting-started.html
.
Once a participant has obtained a digital ID certificate and a docket has been created; the participant can then submit adjudicatory documents. Submissions must be in Portable Document Format (PDF). Additional guidance on PDF submissions is available on the NRC's public website at
https://www.nrc.gov/​site-help/​electronic-sub-ref-mat.html
.
A filing is considered complete at the time the document is submitted through the NRC's E-Filing system. To be timely, an electronic filing must be submitted to the E-Filing system no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the due date. Upon receipt of a transmission, the E-Filing system time-stamps the document and sends the submitter an email notice confirming receipt of the document. The E-Filing system also distributes an email notice that provides access to the document to the NRC's Office of the General Counsel and any others who have advised the Office of the Secretary that they wish to participate in the proceeding, so that the filer need not serve the document on those participants separately. Therefore, applicants and other participants (or their counsel or representative) must apply for and receive a digital ID certificate before adjudicatory documents are filed so that they can obtain access to the documents via the E-Filing system.
A person filing electronically using the NRC's adjudicatory E-Filing system may seek assistance by contacting the NRC's Electronic Filing Help Desk through the “Contact Us” link located on the NRC's public website at
(
printed page 73824)
https://www.nrc.gov/​site-help/​e-submittals.html
,
by email to
MSHD.Resource@nrc.gov
,
or by a toll-free call at 1-866-672-7640. The NRC Electronic Filing Help Desk is available between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m., Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays.
Participants who believe that they have a good cause for not submitting documents electronically must file an exemption request, in accordance with
10 CFR 2.302(g)
, with their initial paper filing stating why there is good cause for not filing electronically and requesting authorization to continue to submit documents in paper format. Such filings must be submitted in accordance with
10 CFR 2.302(b)-(d)
. Participants filing adjudicatory documents in this manner are responsible for serving the document on all other participants. Filing is considered complete by first-class mail as of the time of deposit in the mail, or by courier, express mail, or expedited delivery service upon depositing the document with the provider of the service. A presiding officer, having granted an exemption request from using E-Filing, may require a participant or party to use E-Filing if the presiding officer subsequently determines that the reason for granting the exemption from use of E-Filing no longer exists.
Documents submitted in adjudicatory proceedings will appear in the NRC's electronic hearing docket which is available to the public at
https://ehd.nrc.gov/​home
unless excluded pursuant to an order of the Commission or the presiding officer. If you do not have an NRC-issued digital ID certificate as described above, click “cancel” when the link requests certificates and you will be automatically directed to the NRC's electronic hearing dockets where you will be able to access any publicly available documents in a particular hearing docket. Participants are requested not to include personal privacy information, such as social security numbers, home addresses, or personal phone numbers in their filings, unless an NRC regulation or other law requires submission of such information. For example, in some instances, individuals provide home addresses in order to demonstrate proximity to a facility or site. With respect to copyrighted works, except for limited excerpts that serve the purpose of the adjudicatory filings and would constitute a Fair Use application, participants are requested not to include copyrighted materials in their submission.
The Commission will issue a notice or order granting or denying a hearing request or intervention petition, designating the issues for any hearing that will be held and designating the Presiding Officer. A notice granting a hearing will be published in the
Federal Register
and served on the parties to the hearing.
If a person other than TRISO-X or its successors requests a hearing, that person shall set forth with particularity the manner in which their interest is adversely affected by this Confirmatory Order and shall address the criteria set forth in
10 CFR 2.309(d)
and
(f)
.
If a hearing is requested by a person whose interest is adversely affected, the Commission will issue an order designating the time and place of any hearings. If a hearing is held, the issue to be considered at such hearing shall be whether this Confirmatory Order should be sustained.
In the absence of any request for hearing, or written approval of an extension of time in which to request a hearing, the provisions specified in Section V above shall be final 30 days from the date of this Confirmatory Order without further order or proceedings. If an extension of time for requesting a hearing has been approved, the provisions specified in Section V shall be final when the extension expires if a hearing request has not been received.
For the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

Deputy Office Director and Chief Nuclear Materials Inspector, Office of Nuclear Material Safety and Safeguards
.
