§ 656.14
Notice of filing.
(a) An employer who desires to hire an alien for permanent employment in the United States must post notice of the filing of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
and be able to document that notice was provided, as follows:
(1) If there is a bargaining representative(s) for the employer's employees in the occupational classification located at the place(s) of employment, the employer must provide written notice, electronically or by mail, by providing a copy of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
and maintaining documentation of where and when it was sent to the bargaining representative(s).
(2) If there is no bargaining representative(s), the employer must post notice in at least two conspicuous locations to all employees located at the place(s) of employment in which the work will be performed by the alien. Electronic posting, such as displaying the notice prominently on any internal or external website that is maintained by the employer, known and readily accessible to all employees, and customarily used by the employer for notices to employees about terms and conditions of employment, is sufficient to meet this posting requirement as long as it otherwise meets the requirements of this section. The notice must be of sufficient size, clearly visible, and unobstructed while posted and must be posted in conspicuous places where the employees of the employer would normally expect to see such employment-related notices and can readily read the posted notice on their way to or from their place of employment. The documentation requirement may be satisfied by providing a copy of the posted notice and stating where and when it was posted, and by providing copies of all the in-house media, whether electronic or print, that were used to distribute notice of the application in accordance with the procedures used for similar positions within the employer's organization.
(b) If the employer intends to employ the alien under the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
at a third-party worksite, the employer's obligation to provide notice under paragraph (a) of this section extends to the third-party worksite, regardless of whether the place(s) of employment is/are owned or operated by the employer or by some other person or entity.
(c) In the case of a private household, notice is required under this section only if the household employs one or more U.S. workers at the time the application for labor certification is filed. The documentation requirement may be satisfied by providing a copy of the posted notice to the CO.
(d) The notice of the filing of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
must:
(1) State that notice is being provided in connection with the filing of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
by the employer to sponsor an alien for permanent employment in the job opportunity;
(2) State any person may provide information or documentary evidence bearing on the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
to the OFLC Administrator of DOL; and
(3) Provide the physical address of the OFLC Administrator.
(e) The notice must contain the information required for advertisements by § 656.17(e) and contain the information required by paragraph (d) of this section.
(f) The notice of filing must be provided or posted within 10 business days before the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
is filed with the NPC and continue to be available or displayed through the date on which the Immigrant Petition is approved by USCIS or the date of determination if the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
or Immigrant Petition is denied or withdrawn, whichever is later.

(a)
Employer obligations.
Except for
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
involving college or university teachers or professional athletes or professional sports team coaches using the recruitment procedures set forth in § 656.18, an employer must attest to having conducted recruitment under this section prior to the filing of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
and comply with all advertising requirements set forth in paragraphs (b) through (e) of this section.
(b)
Required recruitment.
(1) Place a job order with the SWA(s) serving the place(s) of employment.
(2) Where the employer maintains one or more websites for its business operations, place an advertisement for the job opportunity on the web page the employer customarily uses to recruit for job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
If the employer does not customarily use its website(s) for its business operations to recruit for job opportunities that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
the employer must post the job opportunity that is the subject of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
on a web page on all of its business operations website(s) in a conspicuous location.
(3) Place an advertisement for the job opportunity on at least one job search website other than a website maintained by the employer or SWA(s). Where the employer customarily uses one or more job search websites to advertise the job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
the employer must place an advertisement for the job opportunity on all such websites using the same method(s) and location(s) that it uses for job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
(4) Where the employer customarily uses one or more social media platforms to advertise job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
the employer must place an advertisement for the job opportunity on all such social media platforms using the same method(s) and location(s) that it uses for job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
(5) During the period of time the job order placed with the SWA under paragraph (b)(1) of this section is actively circulating, place an advertisement for the job opportunity in the occupational classification through at least one job fair, on-campus recruiting event, or with a college, university, or trade school's placement office. Where the employer customarily engages in one or more job fairs or on-campus recruiting events or placement offices at different colleges, universities, or trade schools to advertise job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
the employer must place an advertisement for the job opportunity in the same occupational classification that is the subject of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
using the same method(s) and location(s) for all such job fairs, on-campus recruitment events, or placement offices that it uses for job opportunities in the same occupational classification that are not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
(c)
Length of active recruitment.
All advertisements placed in connection with the requirements set forth in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section must be active for a period of no less than 90 calendar days or the total number of days the employer has customarily advertised for the same or similar job opportunities during the most recent 12 months that were not the subject of an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
(d)
Completion of active recruitment.
Each of the advertisements placed in connection with the requirements set forth in paragraphs (b)(1) through (4) of this section must be completed no more than 60 calendar days and no less than 30 calendar days before the expected filing of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
(e)
Advertising requirements.
(1) All recruitment conducted under this subpart must contain terms and conditions of employment that are not less favorable than those offered to the alien and, at a minimum, must comply with the assurances applicable to the recruitment of U.S. workers set forth in § 656.13. In addition, employers must enable any and all information systems they use for collecting, maintaining, and tracking applicants for non-PERM related recruitment to capture all applications that U.S. workers submit for PERM-related recruitment, and enable all applicant records to remain searchable in the same manner as applicant records for non-PERM related recruitment.
(2) All advertising must contain the following information:
(i) The employer's name and contact information;
(ii) A description of the job opportunity with sufficient information to apprise U.S. workers of the services or labor to be performed, including the duties and actual minimum qualifications or requirements to perform the services or labor and the hours of work per week;
(iii) The place(s) of employment or geographic area of employment, including a statement as to whether the position offers remote work, full-time telework, or a hybrid combination of telework and on-site work, with enough specificity to apprise applicants of any travel requirements and where applicants will likely have to reside to perform the service or labor;
(iv) The wage offer or, in the event that there are multiple wage offers, the range of applicable wage offers, each of which must equal or exceed the highest of the prevailing wage or the Federal, State, or local minimum wage;
(v) If applicable, a statement that overtime will be available to the worker and the wage offer(s) for working any overtime hours; and
(vi) A statement that the job is a full-time position and, if the employer has more than one job opening, indicate the total number of job openings the employer intends to fill.
(3) An employer may recruit for multiple positions simultaneously through a single advertisement, provided that, with respect to each job opportunity for which certification is sought, the multi-position advertisement:
(i) Complies with the pre-filing recruitment timing requirements in paragraph (d) of this section;
(ii) Complies with the recruitment placement and duration requirements in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section;
(iii) Includes sufficient information to apprise U.S. workers of each job opportunity, including all information required by this paragraph (e).
(f)
Recruitment report.
(1)
Requirements of a recruitment report.
The employer must prepare, sign, and date a written recruitment report. The recruitment report must be completed before it is submitted concurrently with the filing of the
Application for Permanent Employment

Certification,
as set forth in § 656.10, or on a date specified by the CO as required by the procedures for supervised recruitment set forth in § 656.21 and contain the following information:

in the place(s) of intended employment, provide a detailed explanation of the method(s) used and date(s) on which the employer notified all potentially qualified laid off U.S. workers for the job opportunity;

Further recruitment guidance.

§ 656.19
Processing of an application.
(a)
NPC review.
The CO will assign for processing all
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification,
review such applications for compliance with the requirements set forth in this part, and make a decision to conduct an audit examination using the procedures set forth in § 656.20, order supervised recruitment using the procedures set forth in § 656.21, or issue a final determination set forth in § 656.24.
(b)
Correspondence during processing.
Any notice or request sent by the CO(s) under this subpart to an employer requiring a response will be sent electronically, unless the employer was permitted to file by mail as set forth in § 656.10(c). For employers permitted to file by mail, the CO will send any notice or request via traditional methods to assure next day delivery. The CO will use the address, including electronic mail address, provided on the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
to send such notices or requests. The employer's response to such a notice or request must be filed electronically, except that an employer permitted to file by mail as set forth in § 656.10(c), may use traditional methods to assure next day delivery. The employer's response must be sent by the due date or the next business day if the

due date falls on a Sunday or Federal holiday.
(c)
Response dates.
OFLC will determine the date of an employer's response to any notice or request sent to the employer during application processing as follows:
(1) For any
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
received using the electronic method(s) designated by the OFLC Administrator, response date(s) will be the date on which a response to a notice or request is submitted. Response date(s) will be based on the time of submission in the Eastern time zone of the United States.
(2) For any
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
received in accordance with § 656.10(c)(2) or (3), response date(s) will be the postmark date affixed to the employer's response submission.
(d)
Job duties and requirements.
(1) Job requirements specified in the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
unless adequately documented as arising from business necessity, must be those normally required for the occupation and must not exceed the SVP level assigned to the occupation as shown in the O*NET Job Zones. To establish a business necessity, an employer must demonstrate the job duties and requirements bear a reasonable relationship to the occupation in the context of the employer's business and are essential to perform the job in a reasonable manner.
(2) A foreign language requirement is prohibited, unless such a requirement is justified by business necessity. Demonstrating business necessity for a foreign language requirement may be based upon the following:
(i) The nature of the occupation and the specific duties to be performed in the job opportunity that normally requires regular use of a foreign language; or
(ii) The need to communicate with a large majority of the employer's customers, contractors, or employees who cannot communicate effectively in English, as documented by:
(A) The employer furnishing the number and proportion of its clients, contractors, or employees who cannot communicate effectively in English, and/or detailed executed contracts or agreements outlining plans to market products or deliver services in a foreign country; and
(B) A detailed explanation of why the duties of the job opportunity normally require frequent contact and communication with clients, contractors, or employees who cannot communicate effectively in English, including why the responsibilities of the position for which permanent labor certification is sought necessitate regular contact and communication with these individuals, and why it is reasonable to believe the foreign-language-speaking clients, contractors, and employees cannot communicate effectively in English.
(3) If the job opportunity involves a combination of occupations, the employer must document that it has normally employed workers for that combination of occupations, and/or workers customarily perform the combination of occupations in the place(s) of employment, and/or the combination job opportunity is based on a business necessity. Combination occupations can be documented by position descriptions, relevant payroll records, and/or letters from other employers stating their workers regularly perform the combination of occupations in the same AIE, and/or documentation that the combination occupation arises from a business necessity.
(4)(i) If the job opportunity contains alternative requirements, those requirements must be substantially equivalent to the primary requirements of the job opportunity for which permanent labor certification is sought; and
(ii) If the alien already is employed by the employer, and the alien does not meet the primary job requirements and only potentially qualifies for the job by virtue of the alternative requirements, the CO will deny permanent labor certification unless the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
states that any suitable combination of education, training, or experience is acceptable.

and there are not cost-effective alternatives to a live-in household requirement. Mere employer assertions do not constitute acceptable documentation. § 656.24
Labor certification determinations.
(a)
Determinations.
The OFLC Administrator is the Department's National CO. The OFLC Administrator and the CO(s), by virtue of delegation from the OFLC Administrator, have the authority to certify or deny
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification.
The OFLC Administrator has sole discretion to certify, deny, or suspend processing of
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
under 656.31(b) or for other appropriate reasons or to delegate authority to the CO to do so.
(b)
Criteria for certification.
The CO will grant certification only if:
(1) The employer has met all the requirements of this part.
(2) There are not sufficient U.S. workers to fill the job opportunity. In making a determination as to whether there are insufficient U.S. workers to fill the employer's job opportunity, the CO will count as able and available any U.S. worker referred by the SWA or any U.S. worker who applied (or on whose behalf an application is made) directly to the employer, whom the employer has not rejected for a lawful, job-related reason.
(i) The CO must consider a U.S. worker able and qualified for the job opportunity if the worker, by education, training, experience, or a combination thereof, is able to perform in the normally accepted manner the duties involved in the occupation as customarily performed by other U.S. workers similarly employed. For the purposes of this paragraph (b)(2)(i), a U.S. worker is able and qualified for the job opportunity if the worker can acquire the skills necessary to perform the duties involved in the occupation during a reasonable period of on the-job training.
(ii) If the job involves an alien who is a college or university teacher or has exceptional ability in the sciences or the arts, the U.S. worker must be at least as qualified as the alien.
(3) The employment of the alien will not have an adverse effect upon the wages and working conditions of U.S. workers similarly employed. In making this determination, the CO considers such things as: labor market information; the special circumstances of the industry, organization, and/or occupation; the prevailing wage in the place(s) of intended employment; and working conditions, such as hours, that are normal to the occupation and industry.
(c)
Approved certification.
If permanent labor certification is granted, the CO will send a final determination notice and a copy of the certified
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
to the employer and a copy, if applicable, to the employer's agent or attorney using an electronic method(s) designated by the OFLC Administrator. For employers permitted to file by mail as set forth in § 656.10(c), the CO will send the final determination notice and a copy of the certified
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
using the mailing address for the employer identified on the application. The CO will send the certified
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
directly to USCIS using an electronic method(s) designated by the OFLC Administrator.
(d)
Denied certification.
If the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
is denied, the CO will send a Notice of Denial to the employer and a copy, if appropriate, to the employer's agent or attorney using an electronic method(s) designated by the OFLC Administrator. For employers permitted to file by mail as set forth in § 656.10(c), the CO will send the Notice of Denial by means normally assuring next day delivery. The Notice of Denial will:
(1) State the reason(s) certification is denied, citing the relevant regulatory standards;
(2) Offer the employer an opportunity to request reconsideration by the CO of the denial under § 656.26(a) or request review by BALCA under § 656.26(b);
(3) State that if the employer does not request reconsideration by the CO or review by BALCA within 30 calendar days of the date of the determination, as specified in § 656.26(a) or (b), the denial is final, and the Department will not accept any request for reconsideration or review on that
Application for Permanent Employment Certification;
(4) State that if the employer does not request reconsideration or review of the denial under § 656.26(a) or (b), a new
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
may be filed at any time; and
(5) State that the employer is prohibited from filing a new
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
in the same occupation for the same alien while a request for reconsideration or review is pending under the procedures set forth in § 656.26 or § 656.27.
§ 656.26
Review of denials of permanent labor certification.
(a)
Request for reconsideration by the CO.
(1) The employer may request reconsideration by the CO within 30 calendar days from the date of issuance of the Notice of Denial.
(2) A request for reconsideration may include only:
(i) Documentation that the Department actually received from the employer in response to a request from the CO to the employer; or
(ii) Documentation that the employer did not have an opportunity to present previously to the CO, but that existed at the time the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
was filed and maintained by the employer to support the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
in compliance with the requirements of § 656.10(h).
(3) Paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) of this section notwithstanding, the CO will not grant any request for reconsideration
(
printed page 74017)
where the deficiency that caused denial resulted from the applicant's disregard of a system prompt or other direct instruction.
(4) The employer's request must clearly state whether it is seeking a request for review by BALCA or a request for reconsideration by the CO. If it is not clearly stated whether the employer is requesting reconsideration by the CO or requesting review by BALCA, the CO will reconsider the determination.
(5) If the employer requests reconsideration, the CO will reconsider the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
If the reconsideration is denied, the Notice of Reconsideration Denial will:
(i) State the reasons for the Notice of Reconsideration Denial;
(ii) Quote the request for review procedures at paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section;
(iii) Advise that failure to request review by BALCA of the Notice of Reconsideration Denial within 30 calendar days of the date of determination constitutes a failure to exhaust administrative remedies;
(iv) Advise that, if a request for review is not made within 30 calendar days of the determination, the Notice of Reconsideration Denial will become the final determination of the Secretary;
(v) Advise that if the reconsideration is denied, and a request for review is not made in accordance with the procedures at paragraph (b) of this section, a new application may be filed at any time; and
(vi) Advise that a new application in the same occupation for the same alien cannot be filed while a request for review is pending with BALCA.
(b)
Request for review by BALCA.
(1) If a permanent labor certification is denied under § 656.24(d), if a request for reconsideration is denied under paragraph (a) of this section, if a permanent labor certification is revoked pursuant to § 656.32, or if a debarment is issued under § 656.31(f), a request for review of the denial of certification, denial on reconsideration, revocation, or debarment may be made to BALCA by the employer or debarred person or entity by making a request for such an administrative review in accordance with the procedures provided in this paragraph (b). In the case of a finding of debarment, receipt by the Department of a request for review, if made in accordance with this section, will stay the debarment until such time as the review has been completed and a decision rendered thereon.
(2) A request for review of a denial of certification, denial on reconsideration, or revocation:
(i) Must be sent within 30 calendar days of the date of the determination to the CO who denied the application, denied the request for reconsideration, or revoked the certification;
(ii) Must clearly identify the particular labor certification determination for which review is sought;
(iii) Must set forth the particular grounds for the request; and
(iv) Must include a copy of the final determination.
(3) A request for review of debarment:
(i) Must be sent to the OFLC Administrator within 30 calendar days of the date of the debarment determination;
(ii) Must clearly identify the particular debarment determination for which review is sought;
(iii) Must set forth the particular grounds for the request; and
(iv) Must include a copy of the Notice of Debarment.
(4)(i) With respect to a request for review of either a Notice of Denial or a Notice of Reconsideration Denial, statements, briefs, and other submissions of the parties and amicus curiae must contain only legal argument and only such evidence as was actually before the CO at the time of the CO's decision, even if such evidence is in the administrative file.
(ii) With respect to a revocation or a debarment determination, BALCA proceeding may be de novo.
(c)
Denial of certification, denial on reconsideration, or revocation Appeal File.
Upon the receipt of a request for review, the CO immediately must assemble an indexed Appeal File:
(1) The Appeal File must be in chronological order, must have the index on top followed by the most recent document, and must have consecutively numbered pages. The Appeal File must contain the request for review, the complete application file, and copies of all the written material, such as pertinent parts and pages of surveys and/or reports upon which the denial was based.
(2) The CO must send the Appeal File to BALCA, Office of Administrative Law Judges, the employer, the employer's attorney or agent (if applicable), and the Associate Solicitor for Employment and Training Legal Services, Office of the Solicitor, U.S. DOL (counsel), as soon as practicable.
(3) The employer may furnish or suggest directly to BALCA the addition of any documentation that is not in the Appeal File, but was actually before the CO at the time of the CO's decision. The employer must submit such documentation in writing, and must send a copy to the Associate Solicitor for Employment and Training Legal Services, Office of the Solicitor, U.S. Department of Labor, Washington, DC 20210.
(d)
Debarment Appeal File.
Upon the receipt of a request for review of debarment, the OFLC Administrator, immediately must assemble an indexed Appeal File:
(1) The Appeal File must be in chronological order, must have the index on top followed by the most recent document, and must have consecutively numbered pages. The Appeal File must contain the request for review, the complete application file, and copies of all the written material, such as pertinent parts and pages of surveys and/or reports upon which the denial was based.
(2) The OFLC Administrator must send the Appeal File to BALCA, Office of Administrative Law Judges, the employer, the employer's attorney or agent (if applicable), and the Associate Solicitor for Employment and Training Legal Services, Office of the Solicitor, U.S. DOL (counsel), by means normally assuring next-day delivery.
(3) The debarred person or entity may furnish or suggest directly to BALCA the addition of any documentation in writing that is not in the Appeal File. The debarred person or entity must submit such documentation in writing, and must send a copy to the Associate Solicitor for Employment and Training Legal Services, Office of the Solicitor, U.S. Department of Labor.

§ 656.30
Validity of labor certifications.
(a)
Validity period.

Application for Permanent Employment Certification
is certified.

Scope of validity.

§ 656.31
Applications involving fraud, willful misrepresentation, or violations of this part.
(a)
Denial.
The CO will deny any
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
under § 656.24 where the CO determines that the application contains false statements of material fact, is fraudulent, contains willful misrepresentations, or was otherwise submitted in violation of the requirements of this part.
(b)
Possible fraud or willful misrepresentation.
(1) If the Department learns an employer, attorney, or agent is involved in possible fraud or willful misrepresentation in connection with the permanent labor certification program, the Department will refer the matter to DOJ, DHS, or other government entity, as appropriate, for investigation, and send a copy of the referral to the DOL-OIG. If the Department learns an employer, attorney, or agent is involved in possible discrimination because of national origin, the Department will also refer the matter to the EEOC; where it indicates possible discrimination because of citizenship status, or because of national origin by an employer not covered by Title VII, the Department will also refer the matter to DOJ. In these cases, or if the Department learns an employer, attorney, or agent is under investigation by DOJ, DHS, or other government entity for possible fraud or willful misrepresentation in connection with the permanent labor certification program, the Department may suspend processing of any
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
involving such employer, attorney, or agent until completion of any investigation and/or judicial proceedings. Unless the investigatory agency, in writing, requests the Department to do otherwise, the Department will provide written notification to the employer and a copy, if appropriate, to the employer's agent or attorney of the suspension in processing.
(2) A suspension pursuant to paragraph (b)(1) of this section may last initially for up to 180 calendar days. No later than 180 calendar days after the suspension began, if no criminal indictment or information has been issued, or judicial proceedings have not been concluded, the CO may resume processing any of the
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification,
or may extend the suspension in processing until completion of any investigation and/or judicial proceedings.
(c)
Criminal indictment or information.
If the Department learns that an employer, attorney, or agent is named in a criminal indictment or information in connection with the permanent labor certification program, the processing of any of the
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
related to that employer, attorney, or agent may be suspended until the judicial process is completed. Unless the investigatory or prosecutorial agency, in writing, requests the Department to do otherwise, the Department will provide written notification to the employer and a copy, if appropriate, to the employer's agent or attorney of the suspension in processing.
(d)
No finding of fraud or willful misrepresentation.
If an employer, attorney, or agent is acquitted of fraud or willful misrepresentation charges, or if such criminal charges are withdrawn or otherwise fail to result in a finding of fraud or willful misrepresentation, the CO will resume processing of the
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
in accordance with the requirements of this part based on the merits of the application.
(e)
Finding of fraud or willful misrepresentation.
If an employer, attorney, or agent is found to have committed fraud or willful misrepresentation involving the permanent labor certification program, whether by a court, the Department of State or DHS, as referenced in § 656.32(c), by the OFLC Administrator under paragraph (f)(3) of this section, or through other proceedings:
(1) Any suspension of processing of pending
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
related to that employer, attorney, or agent will terminate.
(
printed page 74019)
(2) The CO will decide each such
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
on its merits and may deny any such
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
under § 656.24 and paragraph (a) of this section.
(3) In the case of a pending
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
involving an attorney or agent found to have committed fraud or willful misrepresentation, the Department will notify the employer associated with that
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
of the finding and require the employer to notify the Department in writing, within 30 calendar days of the notification, whether the employer will withdraw the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
designate a new attorney or agent, or continue the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
without representation. Failure of the employer to respond within 30 calendar days of the notification will result in a denial under § 656.24. If the employer elects to continue representation by the attorney or agent, DOL will suspend processing of any affected
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
while debarment proceedings are conducted under paragraph (f) of this section.
(f)
Debarment.
(1) No later than 6 years after the date of filing of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
that is the basis for the finding, or, if such basis requires a pattern or practice as provided in paragraphs (f)(1)(iii) through (viii) of this section, no later than 6 years after the date of filing of the last
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
which constitutes a part of the pattern or practice, the OFLC Administrator may issue to an employer, attorney, agent, or any combination thereof a Notice of Debarment for not more than 3 years, based upon any action that was prohibited at the time the action occurred, upon determining the employer, attorney, or agent has participated in or facilitated one or more of the following:
(i) The sale, barter, or purchase of any
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
or any other action prohibited under § 656.12;
(ii) The willful provision or willful assistance in the provision of false or inaccurate information in applying for permanent labor certification;
(iii) A pattern or practice of a failure to comply with the terms of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification;
(iv) A pattern or practice of failure to comply in the audit process pursuant to § 656.20;
(v) A pattern or practice of failure to comply in the supervised recruitment process pursuant to § 656.21;
(vi) Conduct resulting in a determination by a court, DHS, DOS, or the OFLC Administrator under paragraph (f)(3) of this section of fraud or willful misrepresentation involving an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification,
as referenced in paragraph (e) of this section;
(vii) A pattern or practice, by an attorney or agent, of preparing or submitting
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
on behalf of two or more unrelated employers that contain materially the same job duties, requirements, or recruitment procedures where the CO has determined that those requirements were not the employers' actual minimum requirements or that the recruitment was not conducted in good faith; or
(viii) Failure to pay the alien or a U.S. worker hired for the job opportunity the offered wage stated in the certified
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
(2) The Notice of Debarment will be in writing; will state the reason for the debarment finding, including a detailed explanation of how the employer, attorney or agent has participated in or facilitated one or more of the actions listed in paragraphs (f)(1)(i) through (viii) of this section; will state the start date and term of the debarment; will state that the employer, attorney, or agent will be debarred from all foreign labor certification programs (
i.e.,
disqualified from filing any labor certification applications or labor condition applications or receiving approvals from OFLC) for the term of the debarment; and will identify appeal opportunities under § 656.26. The debarment will take effect on the start date identified in the Notice of Debarment unless a request for review is filed within the time permitted by § 656.26. DOL will notify DHS and the Department of State regarding any Notice of Debarment.
(3)
Independent Department finding.
The OFLC Administrator may determine that an employer, attorney, or agent has committed fraud or willful misrepresentation, as defined in 656.3, in connection with an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification.
Such a determination does not require, and is not contingent upon, any determination by a court, DHS, or the Department of State, and does not preclude a referral under paragraph (b) of this section. A Notice of Debarment issued on the basis of such a determination will set forth the evidence relied upon, and the employer, attorney, or agent may seek review under 656.26.
(g)
False statements.
To knowingly and willfully furnish any false information in the preparation of the
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
and any supporting documentation, or to aid, abet, or counsel another to do so is a Federal offense, punishable by fine or imprisonment up to five years, or both under
18 U.S.C. 2
and
1001
. Other penalties apply as well to fraud or misuse of DOL immigration-related documents and to perjury with respect to such documents under
18 U.S.C. 1546
and
1621
.
§ 656.32
Revocation and invalidation of permanent labor certifications.
(a)
Basis for DOL revocation.
The OFLC Administrator may revoke a permanent labor certification issued under this part, if the certification was not justified.
(b)
DOL procedures for revocation.
(1) The OFLC Administrator sends to the employer and a copy, if appropriate, to the employer's agent or attorney a
Notice of Intent to Revoke
an approved permanent labor certification which contains a detailed statement of the grounds for the revocation and the time period allowed for the employer's rebuttal. The employer may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 calendar days of receipt of the notice. The OFLC Administrator must consider all relevant evidence presented in deciding whether to revoke the permanent labor certification.
(2) If rebuttal evidence is not filed by the employer, the
Notice of Intent to Revoke
becomes the final decision of the Secretary.
(3) If the employer files rebuttal evidence and the OFLC Administrator determines the approved permanent labor certification should be revoked, the employer may file an appeal under § 656.26.
(4) The OFLC Administrator will inform the employer within 30 calendar days of receiving any rebuttal evidence whether or not the approved permanent labor certification will be revoked.
(5) If the approved permanent labor certification is revoked, the OFLC Administrator will also send a copy of the notification to DHS and DOS.
(c)
DHS or DOS invalidation of labor certifications.
Either DHS or a Consul of the DOS may invalidate a permanent labor certification approved under this part upon a determination, made in accordance with those agencies'
(
printed page 74020)
procedures or by a court, of fraud or willful misrepresentation of a material fact involving the permanent labor certification application. If evidence of such fraud or willful misrepresentation becomes known to the OFLC Administrator, the OFLC Administrator will notify DHS or DOS, in writing. The OFLC Administrator will also send a copy of the notification to the regional or national office, as appropriate, of the DOL-OIG.

Revise subpart D to read as follows:
Subpart D—Determination of Prevailing Wage

Determination of prevailing wage for labor certification purposes.

§ 656.40
Determination of prevailing wage for labor certification purposes.
(a)
Application filing requirements.
Except as otherwise permitted by this part, an employer who desires to file an
Application for Permanent Employment Certification
to hire an alien for permanent employment in the United States must obtain a PWD from the NPC designated by the OFLC Administrator. This section provides the procedures employers must follow when filing.
(1)
What to file.
(i) An employer that desires to apply for permanent labor certification of an immigrant worker must file a completed
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination,
including any relevant appendices and supporting documentation, to obtain a PWD from the NPC.
(ii) The
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
must include the employer's legal name, trade name(s), and a valid FEIN as well as a valid place of business (physical location) in the United States.
(iii) If an employer is requesting a PWD based on a CBA covering the job opportunity, the employer must concurrently submit with its
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
at the time of filing the following:
(A) A copy of the relevant sections of the CBA, which must include the validity dates of the agreement; the position(s) and description of the job(s) covered; the wage section, including tables and explanations; and the signature page with effective dates of the agreement;
(B) A letter on letterhead from the employer or employer's representative that states the relevant portions of the agreement with effective dates; the title of the position in the agreement appropriate to the job duties, requirements, and location; and wage value appropriate to the job duties, requirements, and location; and
(C) A letter on letterhead from the CBA authorized representative that states the relevant portions of the agreement with effective dates; the title of the position in the agreement appropriate to the job duties, requirements, and location; and wage value appropriate to the job duties, requirements, and location.
(iv) If an employer is requesting a PWD for a job opportunity for a professional athlete or professional sports team coach covered by professional sports league rules or regulations with wage provisions, the employer must concurrently submit with its
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
at the time of filing a copy of the applicable league rules or regulations.
(v) If an employer is requesting a PWD based on an employer-provided survey under paragraph (f) of this section, the employer must concurrently submit with its
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
at the time of filing a copy of the survey containing specific information about the survey methodology, including sample size and source, sample selection procedures, survey job descriptions, job and wage leveling chart, and list of participants surveyed, to allow a determination of whether the survey meets all the requirements of this section.
(2)
Location and method of filing.
(i)
Electronic filing.
The employer must file the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination,
including any relevant appendices, with the NPC using the electronic method(s) designated by the OFLC Administrator. The NPC will return without review any application submitted using a method other than the designated electronic method(s), unless the employer submits the application in accordance with paragraph (a)(2)(ii) of this section.
(ii)
Filing by mail.
Employers that lack adequate access to electronic filing may file the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
by mail in accordance with the procedures set forth in § 656.10(c)(2) and (3).
(b)
NPC review.
(1) The CO will review the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
for compliance with all applicable program requirements and make a decision to issue a Request for Information (RFI) under paragraph (c) of this section or a PWD.
(2) Any notice or request sent by the CO(s) to an employer requiring a response will be sent electronically, unless the employer was permitted to file by mail as set forth in § 656.10(c). For employers permitted to file by mail, the CO will send any notice or request via traditional methods to assure next day delivery. The CO will use the address, including electronic mail address, provided on the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
to send such notices or requests. The employer's response to such a notice or request must be filed electronically, except that an employer permitted to file by mail as set forth in § 656.10(c), may use traditional methods to assure next day delivery. The employer's response must be sent by the due date or the next business day if the due date falls on a Sunday or Federal holiday.
(3) The CO will return without review any
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
where a valid PWD has been issued for the same employer covering the same job opportunity and AIE(s) for the same wage year, including applications where the employer has requested review of a PWD under § 656.41.
(c)
Request for Information.
(1) If the CO determines the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
is incomplete, contains errors or inaccuracies, or otherwise contains information that is not sufficient to issue a PWD, the CO will issue an RFI to the employer and to the employer's attorney or agent (if applicable). The CO may issue one or more additional RFIs before issuing a final decision.
(2) The RFI will:
(i) State the reason(s) the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
does not meet the criteria for issuing a PWD;
(ii) Offer the employer an opportunity to respond to the RFI within 7 calendar days from the date the RFI was issued by CO;
(iii) State that the CO's determination on whether to issue a PWD will be made based on a review of the employer's response and the CO will make the necessary amendments to the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
to issue a PWD, as applicable; and
(iv) State that if the employer does not respond to the RFI within 7 calendar days from the date the RFI was issued by the CO, the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
will be deemed abandoned, the CO will return the application to the employer without issuing a PWD, and the employer may file a new
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
with the NPC.
(d)
Determinations.
Prevailing wages will be determined as follows:
(
printed page 74021)
(1) If the job opportunity is covered by CBA that was negotiated at arms-length between the union and the employer or by professional sports league rules or regulations with wage provisions, the wage rate set forth in the CBA agreement or professional sports league rules or regulations is considered as not adversely affecting the wages of U.S. workers similarly employed, that is, it is considered the “prevailing wage” for labor certification purposes.
(2) If the job opportunity is not covered by a CBA or professional sports league rules or regulations, the prevailing wage for labor certification purposes will be the arithmetic mean, of the wages of workers similarly employed in the AIE, except as provided in paragraph (e) or (f) of this section. The wage component of the Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics Survey will be used to determine the arithmetic mean, unless the employer provides an acceptable survey under paragraph (f) of this section.
(3) If the employer provides a survey acceptable under paragraph (f) of this section, the survey must provide an arithmetic mean of the wages of workers similarly employed in the AIE.
(4) The employer may utilize a current wage determination in the area under the Davis-Bacon Act,
40 U.S.C. 276a
et seq.,
29 CFR part 1
, or the McNamara-O'Hara Service Contract Act,
41 U.S.C. 351
et seq.
(e)
Institutions of higher education and research entities.
In computing the prevailing wage for a job opportunity in an occupational classification in an AIE for an employee of an institution of higher education, or an affiliated or related nonprofit entity, a nonprofit research organization, or a Governmental research organization, the prevailing wage level takes into account the wage levels of employees only at such institutions and organizations in the AIE.
(1) The organizations listed in this paragraph (e) are defined by DHS at
8 CFR 214.2(h)(19)(iii)
as follows:
(i) Institution of higher education means an institution of higher education as defined in section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965;
(ii) Affiliated or related nonprofit entity means a nonprofit entity that is related or affiliated with an institution of higher education, if it satisfies any of the following conditions:
(A) The nonprofit entity is connected to or associated with an institution of higher education through shared ownership or control by the same board or federation;
(B) The nonprofit entity is operated by an institution of higher education;
(C) The nonprofit entity is attached to an institution of higher education as a member, branch, cooperative, or subsidiary; or
(D) The nonprofit entity has entered into a formal written affiliation agreement with an institution of higher education that establishes an active working relationship between the nonprofit entity and the institution of higher education for the purposes of research or education, and a fundamental activity of the nonprofit entity is to directly contribute to the research or education mission of the institution of higher education. A nonprofit entity may engage in more than one fundamental activity.
(iii) Nonprofit research organization or Governmental research organization. When a fundamental activity of a nonprofit organization is engaging in basic research and/or applied research, that organization is a nonprofit research organization. When a fundamental activity of a Governmental organization is the performance or promotion of basic research and/or applied research, that organization is a government research organization. A Governmental research organization may be a Federal, State, or local entity. A nonprofit research organization or governmental research organization may perform or promote more than one fundamental activity. Basic research is general research to gain more comprehensive knowledge or understanding of the subject under study, without specific applications in mind. Basic research is also research that advances scientific knowledge but does not have specific immediate commercial objectives although it may be in fields of present or potential commercial interest. Applied research is research to gain knowledge or understanding to determine the means by which a specific, recognized need may be met. Applied research includes investigations oriented to discovering new scientific knowledge that has specific commercial objectives with respect to products, processes, or services. Both basic research and applied research may include research and investigation in the sciences, social sciences, or humanities and may include designing, analyzing, and directing the research of others if on an ongoing basis and throughout the research cycle.
(2) Nonprofit organization or entity, for the purpose of this paragraph (e), means an organization qualified as a tax exempt organization under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, section 501(c)(3), (c)(4), or (c)(6) (
26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3)
, (c)(4) or (c)(6)), and which has received approval as a tax exempt organization from the Internal Revenue Service, as it relates to research or educational purposes.
(f)
Employer-provided wage information.
(1) If the job opportunity is not covered by a CBA, or by a professional sports league's rules or regulations, the CO will consider wage information provided by the employer in making a PWD.
(2) The survey submitted to the NPC must be based upon recently collected data.
(i) A published survey must have been published within 24 months of the date of submission to the NPC, must be the most current edition of the survey, and the data upon which the survey is based must have been collected within 24 months of the publication date of the survey.
(ii) A survey conducted by the employer must be based on data collected within 24 months of the date it is submitted to the NPC.
(g)
Similarly employed.
For purposes of this section, similarly employed means having substantially comparable jobs in the occupational category in the AIE, except that, if a representative sample of workers in the occupational category cannot be obtained in the AIE, similarly employed means:
(1) Having jobs requiring a substantially similar level of skills within the AIE; or
(2) If there are no substantially comparable jobs in the AIE, having substantially comparable jobs with employers outside of the AIE.
(h)
Validity of the PWD.
(1) The CO must specify the validity period of the prevailing wage, which in no event may be less than 90 calendar days or more than 365 calendar days from the determination date. A request for review under § 656.41 renders the PWD invalid until the CO issues an affirmed or modified PWD.
(2) An employer must begin the recruitment of U.S. workers required by §§ 656.17, 656.18, or 656.21 within the validity period specified on the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination.
(3) Where the
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
contains multiple AIEs covering the same job opportunity, the PWD issued by the CO on such an application may be used in connection with the filing of multiple
Applications for Permanent Employment Certification
under § 656.10.
(i)
Withdrawal of an Application for Prevailing Wage Determination.
The
(
printed page 74022)
employer may withdraw an
Application for Prevailing Wage Determination
before the CO issues a PWD under this section by submitting a request in writing, electronically or, if permitted to file by mail, via mail, to the NPC that identifies the unique application number and states the reason(s) for the withdrawal.
§ 656.41
Review of prevailing wage determinations.
(a)
Review of NPC PWD.
Any employer desiring review of a PWD made by a CO must make a request for such review within 30 calendar days of the date from when the PWD was issued. The request for review must be sent to the director of the NPC that issued the PWD within 30 calendar days of the date of the PWD; clearly identify the PWD from which review is sought; set forth the particular grounds for the request; and include all the materials pertaining to the PWD submitted to the NPC up to the date of the PWD received from the NPC.
(b)
Processing of request by NPC.
Upon the receipt of a request for review, the NPC will review the employer's request and accompanying documentation and add any material that may have been omitted by the employer, including any material the NPC sent the employer up to the date of the PWD.
(c)
Review on the record.
The director will review the PWD solely on the basis upon which the PWD was made and, upon the request for review, may either affirm or modify the PWD.
(d)
Request for review by BALCA.
Any employer desiring review of the director's determination must make a request for review by BALCA within 30 calendar days of the date of the Director's decision.
(1) The request for review, statements, briefs, and other submissions of the parties and amicus curiae must contain only legal arguments and only such evidence that was within the record upon which the director made his/her affirmation of the PWD.
(2) The request for review must be in writing and addressed to the director of the NPC making the determination. Upon receipt of a request for a review, the director will assemble an indexed appeal file in reverse chronological order, with the index on top followed by the most recent document.
(3) The director will send the Appeal File to the Office of Administrative Law Judges, BALCA. BALCA handles the appeals in accordance with §§ 656.26 and 656.27.

[Office of Management and Budget #: 0970-0382]
AGENCY:
Office of Community Services, Administration for Children and Families, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.
ACTION:
Request for public comments.
SUMMARY:
The Office of Community Services (OCS), Administration for Children and Families (ACF) requests a 3-year extension of the Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) State Plan, CSBG Eligible Entity Master List, and the American Customer Survey Index (ACSI) forms (Office of Management and Budget (OMB) #: 0970-0382, expiration August 31, 2027). There are changes requested to these information collections to reduce burden.
DATES:
Comments due January 19, 2027.
ADDRESSES:
In compliance with the requirements of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, ACF is soliciting public comment on the specific aspects of the information collection described above. You can obtain copies of the proposed collection of information and submit comments by emailing
infocollection@acf.hhs.gov
.
Identify all requests by the title of the information collection.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Description:
Section 676 of the CSBG Act requires states, including the District of Columbia and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and U.S. territories applying for CSBG funds to submit an application and plan (CSBG State Plan). The CSBG State Plan must meet statutory requirements prior to OCS awarding CSBG grant recipients (states and territories) with CSBG funds. Grant recipients have the option to submit a detailed plan annually or biannually. Grant recipients that submit a biannual plan must provide an abbreviated plan the following year if substantial changes to the initial plan occur. OCS is requesting revisions to this form to reduce burden.
OCS is also requesting to extend approval of the following information collections, with minimal changes proposed:
CSBG Eligible Entity List.
In alignment with federal requirements, OCS requests that all grant recipients continue to keep their CSBG Eligible Entity List current, to include maintaining an accurate listing of the CSBG sub-grant recipients (CSBG eligible entities) and current Unique Entity Identifier for each recipient listed. With the revisions proposed this year, OCS is also requesting that states include satellite offices, as applicable, for all CSBG sub-grant recipients.
Optional survey for the sub-grant recipients (or CSBG-eligible entities).
ACSI is administered biennially. OCS uses the ACSI survey for eligible entities as part of the CSBG performance management framework. The survey focuses on the customer service that the CSBG sub-grant recipients receive from the CSBG grant recipients. The survey is optional, and this will be the eighth time that CSBG sub-grant recipients have the option to complete the survey. There were minimal revisions to the survey.
Respondents:
State governments, including the District of Columbia and
(
printed page 73757)
the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico and U.S. territories, and local level sub-grant recipients.

AGENCY:
Bureau of Land Management, Interior.
ACTION:
Notice of intent.
SUMMARY:
In compliance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) of 1969, as amended, the Mineral Leasing Act (MLA) of 1920, as amended, and the Federal Land Policy and Management Act (FLPMA) of 1976, as amended, the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Arizona State Director intends to prepare an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) to consider the effects of the construction, operation, maintenance, and eventual decommissioning of a new 20-inch-diameter liquid petroleum product pipeline from Borger, Texas, to El Paso, Texas, and a 24-inch diameter pipeline from El Paso, Texas, to Buckeye, Arizona, and by this notice is announcing the beginning of the scoping process to solicit public comments and identify issues, and is providing the criteria for public review.
DATES:
This notice initiates the public scoping process for the EIS. The BLM requests that the public submit comments concerning the scope of the analysis, potential alternatives, and identification of relevant information and studies by December 17, 2026. To afford the BLM the opportunity to consider comments and address them in the EIS, please ensure your comments are received prior to the close of the 30-day scoping period or 15 days after the last public meeting, whichever is later. Comments received outside this window will not be considered.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments related to the Western Gateway Pipeline Project (Project) by any of the following methods:
Project Website:
https://eplanning.blm.gov/​project-home/​?id=​95c62a3a-75be-f111-aaae-001dd8029bbb
.
Mail:
Bureau of Land Management, Arizona State Office, ATTN: Western Gateway Pipeline Project, One North Central Avenue, Suite 800, Phoenix, AZ 85004.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This document provides notice that the BLM Arizona State Director intends to prepare an EIS to consider the effects of the Project, announces the beginning of the scoping process, and seeks public input on issues. The BLM is evaluating whether to grant a right-of-way (ROW) for the Project which consists of a new build 20-inch diameter pipeline from Borger, Texas, to El Paso, Texas, and a 24-inch diameter pipeline from El Paso, Texas, to Buckeye, Arizona, to transport refined liquid petroleum products (
i.e.,
gasoline, diesel, jet fuel). The Project would be developed by Phillips 66 across approximately 887 miles of Federal, state, county, and private lands between Borger, Texas, and Buckeye, Arizona. The Project would also include pipeline-related facilities, such as, but not limited to, access roads, pump stations, mainline valve stations, and breakout facilities.
If approved, the new construction would tie into Kinder Morgan's existing Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline, L.P. from Colton, California, to Buckeye, Arizona, which would be reversed to enable east-to-west product flows. The Project would also tie into the Gold Pipeline, operated by Phillips 66, which runs from Borger, Texas, to St. Louis, Missouri. This section of pipeline would also be reversed for an east-to-west product flow. The Project, along with the connections to the existing Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline and the Gold Pipeline, would result in a total 1,300-mile pipeline system that would transport refined liquid petroleum products from Illinois refineries to California. The Project's proposed construction activities would occur only along the 887-mile portion of the route from Borger, Texas, to Buckeye, Arizona.
Purpose and Need for the Proposed Action
The purpose for BLM's action is to respond to Phillips 66's ROW application filed with the BLM on February 11, 2026, under the MLA. Phillips 66's goal is to obtain authorization across Federal lands to construct, operate, maintain, and decommission a refined petroleum pipeline, access roads, and related facilities in Arizona and New Mexico.
The BLM is the lead Federal agency responsible for issuing the ROW grant and associated temporary use permits (TUPs) for the Western Gateway Pipeline Project under Section 28 of the MLA of 1920 (
30 U.S.C. 185
). Because the proposed petroleum pipeline would cross lands administered by two or more Federal agencies, the BLM serves as the designated lead Federal agency for authorization of the pipeline ROW. Issuance of a ROW or TUP by the BLM will occur with the concurrence of each respective land-managing agency whose lands are crossed by the Project.
The need for the Project comes from the Federal responsibilities under Section 28 of the MLA of 1920 (
30 U.S.C. 185
), 43 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) part 2880 as amended, Title V of the FLPMA,
43 CFR part 2800
, as amended, and other applicable Federal laws, regulations, and policies.
Preliminary Proposed Action and Alternatives
BLM is currently considering one alternative (proposed action) and the no action alternative. Additional alternatives may be identified by cooperators, Federal agencies, tribes, state and local agencies, and the public during the scoping process or by the BLM during its NEPA review.
Under the Proposed Action, the BLM would issue a 30-year ROW grant and any necessary temporary use permits for the construction, operation, maintenance, and eventual decommissioning of a 20-inch, or 24-inch diameter refined liquid petroleum product pipeline on Federal lands, consistent with BLM's jurisdiction as lead Federal agency under Section 28 of
(
printed page 73794)
the MLA. Other Federal land-managing agencies whose lands are crossed by the Project would provide concurrence to the BLM for issuance of these authorizations.
The proposed project consists of a total of 887 miles of pipeline. Approximately 170 miles of underground pipeline would be constructed and operated on BLM-administered land that includes approximately 31 miles administered by the Carlsbad Field Office, 16 miles administered by the Roswell Field Office, 101 miles administered by the Las Cruces District Office in New Mexico, 9 miles administered by the Safford Field Office, 4 miles administered by the Tucson Field Office, and 9 miles administered by the Lower Sonoran Field Office in Arizona. The proposed action would result in the construction and operation of underground pipeline crossing approximately 16 miles of Department of War land in Texas (Fort Bliss), 0.3 mile of Bureau of Reclamation (USBR) land in Arizona (Central Arizona Project Canal), and 0.25 mile of U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) land in Arizona (Gila River Waterfowl Management Area). It would also cross the Rio Grande, under the jurisdiction of the International Boundary and Water Commission. In addition, the proposed action would result in the construction and operation of underground pipeline crossing approximately 228 miles of state and county lands and 472 miles of private lands. In addition to the new pipelines, the proposed action would involve the construction of other ancillary facilities required to be authorized by the appropriate federal agency with jurisdiction for non-pipeline project elements such as electric powerlines.
The long-term corridor for the pipeline would typically be 30 feet wide with an additional 60-foot-wide temporary construction corridor for a combined width of 90 feet, resulting in impacts to approximately 2,033 acres of Federal lands, 2,496 acres of state and county lands, and 5,149 acres of private/unknown lands where the surface owner has not been determined, for a total of 9,768 acres. Temporary and long-term workspaces for facilities outside of the pipeline corridor would affect approximately 1,189 acres on Federal lands, 1,364 acres on state and county lands, and 2,971 acres on private/unknown lands, for a total of 5,523 acres. However, the specific locations and dimensions of the pipeline corridor and additional workspaces would be further established based on site-specific construction requirements, resource avoidance measures, or other location-specific considerations.
Under the No Action Alternative, the BLM would deny the ROW application and the Project would not be constructed on Federal lands. Under this alternative, the Project would not be constructed, and existing land uses on the Project site would continue.
The BLM welcomes comments on all preliminary alternatives as well as suggestions for additional alternatives. The BLM also welcomes comments providing relevant information, studies, or analyses with respect to the proposed action.
Summary of Expected Impacts
The EIS will analyze environmental effects sufficient to support the BLM's ROW and TUP decisions and the concurrences required from other Federal land-managing agencies. The BLM's decision will be the primary Federal authorization for the pipeline across all Federal lands.
The EIS will evaluate potential environmental effects of the proposed action and alternatives, and the reasonably foreseeable effects on resources and issues such as caves and karst; playas; native plants; national historic or scenic trails; and sensitive, rare, threatened and endangered species, such as the lesser prairie-chicken, Sonoran Desert tortoise, southwestern willow flycatcher, yellow-billed cuckoo, dunes sagebrush lizard, and cactus ferruginous pygmy-owl. Additionally, the EIS will evaluate potential environmental effects on air quality, noise, geology, agriculture, water resources (including aquatic resources, water quality, groundwater, water supplies and wells, and floodplains), biological resources (including vegetation; noxious weeds and invasive plants; raptors, eagles, and migratory birds), cultural resources, paleontological resources, visual resources, special land use designations, recreation, transportation, public health and safety, and socioeconomics.
Permits and Authorizations Anticipated at This Time
ROW grant and TUP:
BLM;
Section 404 of Clean Water Act:
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers;
Endangered Species Act (ESA):
USFWS;
Section 401 permit:
Texas Commission of Environmental Quality (TCEQ), New Mexico Environment Department (NMED), and Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ);
Outgrant (for crossing waters in the Northern International Boundary zone):
International Boundary and Water Commission;
Air quality permits:
TCEQ, NMED, and ADEQ;
General national pollutant discharge elimination system permit:
TCEQ, NMED, and ADEQ;
U.S. and State Highway utility encroachment permit:
Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT), New Mexico Department of Transportation (NMDOT), and Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT);
Interstate permitting:
TxDOT, NMDOT, ADOT, and Federal Highway Administration; and,
All other state and county required permits (
e.g.,
road use, load, zoning, conditional use, crossing/encroachment, noxious weed management).
Further details of these permitting requirements may be found in the Plan of Development for the Project, will be available on the ePlanning Project page (see
ADDRESSES
).
Schedule for the Decision-Making Process
The BLM may provide additional opportunities for public participation consistent with the NEPA process. The Final EIS is anticipated to be released in February 2028, with a Record of Decision in May 2028.
Public Scoping Process
This notice of intent initiates the scoping period. The BLM will hold up to three virtual scoping meetings on Zoom. The specific dates of these scoping meetings will be announced in advance through postcards, letters to interested parties, and the ePlanning Project page (see
ADDRESSES
).
Responsible Official
The BLM Arizona State Director is the deciding official for this project. The other affected Federal agencies would issue separate decisions for lands under their jurisdiction based on the analysis contained in the EIS.
Nature of Decision To Be Made
The BLM will use the analysis in the EIS to inform its decision about whether to grant, grant with conditions, or deny the application for a ROW on Federal lands. If the BLM issues a ROW, the BLM decision maker may include terms, conditions, and stipulations determined to be in the public interest, which may include modifying the proposed use or changing the location or route of the proposed facilities. The BLM's resource management goals, objectives, opportunities, and/or conflicts will be
(
printed page 73795)
considered in the decision process for the proposed ROW application.
The USBR, USFWS, and the Department of War may use the analysis in the EIS to inform federal decision-making, as appropriate.
Additional Information
The BLM will utilize and coordinate the NEPA process to help support compliance with applicable procedural requirements under the ESA (
16 U.S.C. 1536
) and Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act (
54 U.S.C. 306108
) as provided in
36 CFR 800.2(d)(3)
, including public involvement requirements of Section 106. The information about historic and cultural resources and threatened and endangered species within the area potentially affected by the proposed project will assist the BLM in identifying and evaluating impacts on such resources.
In July 2026, the BLM invited 31 Indian tribal nations to participate in government-to-government consultation in accordance with
Executive Order 13175
, BLM Manual Section 1780, and other Departmental policies. The BLM will provide additional opportunities for government-to-government consultation during the NEPA process. Tribal concerns, including impacts on Indian trust assets and potential impacts to cultural resources, will be given due consideration.
Federal, state, and local agencies, along with Indian tribal nations, and other stakeholders that may be interested in or affected by the proposed Project that the BLM is evaluating, are invited to participate in the scoping process and, if eligible, may request or be requested by the BLM to participate in the development of the environmental analysis as a cooperating agency.
Before including your address, phone number, email address, or other personal identifying information in your comment, you should be aware that your entire comment—including your personal identifying information—may be made publicly available at any time. While you can request in your comment that BLM withhold your personal identifying information from public review, BLM cannot guarantee that it will be able to do so.

42 U.S.C. 4336a(c)
,

,

)

ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA, Agency, or we) has determined that M.V.I. PEDIATRIC (ascorbic acid 80 milligrams (mg)/vial; biotin 0.02 mg/vial; cyanocobalamin 0.001 mg/vial; dexpanthenol 5 mg/vial; ergocalciferol 0.01 mg/vial; folic acid 0.14 mg/vial; niacinamide 17 mg/vial; phytonadione 0.2 mg/vial; pyridoxine hydrochloride 1 mg/vial; riboflavin 5′-phosphate sodium 1.4 mg/vial; thiamine hydrochloride equivalent (EQ) 1.2 mg base/vial; vitamin A 0.7 mg/vial; vitamin E 7 mg/vial), for injection, was not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness. This determination will allow FDA to approve abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs) for ascorbic acid 80 mg/vial; biotin 0.02 mg/vial; cyanocobalamin 0.001 mg/vial; dexpanthenol 5 mg/vial; ergocalciferol 0.01 mg/vial; folic acid 0.14 mg/vial; niacinamide 17 mg/vial; phytonadione 0.2 mg/vial; pyridoxine hydrochloride 1 mg/vial; riboflavin 5′-phosphate sodium 1.4 mg/vial; thiamine hydrochloride EQ 1.2 mg base/vial; vitamin A 0.7 mg/vial; vitamin E 7 mg/vial, for injection, if all other legal and regulatory requirements are met.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Molly Arndt, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Food and Drug Administration, 10903 New Hampshire Ave., Bldg. 51, Rm. 6281, Silver Spring, MD 20993-0002,
