Department of Veterans Affairs
38 CFR Part 8
[Docket No. VA-2026-VBA-0430]
RIN 2900-AS98
AGENCY:
Department of Veterans Affairs.
ACTION:
Proposed rule.
SUMMARY:
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is proposing to amend its National Service Life Insurance (NSLI) regulations to cease collecting premiums from veterans with NSLI policies identified by the prefixes “V,” “J,” and “JR.” VA has determined there are sufficient financial resources to cover the remaining active policies, enabling veterans to benefit from continued coverage without having to pay future premiums. These programs cover predominantly World War II-era veterans.
DATES:
Comments must be received by December 17, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments through
www.regulations.gov
under RIN 2900-AS98. That website includes a plain language summary of this rulemaking. Comments will be posted for viewing by the public on
www.regulations.gov
,
including any personally identifiable information (
e.g.,
a social security number or address) within a comment and its supporting materials. However, VA retains discretion to redact personal or sensitive information, including but not limited to personal or sensitive information pertaining to third parties. Additionally, VA will not post public comments that make threats to individuals or institutions or suggest that the commenter will take actions to harm an individual. Instructions for accessing
(
printed page 73727)
agency documents, submitting comments, and viewing the rulemaking docket, are available on
www.regulations.gov
under “FAQ.” Any public comment received after the comment period's closing date is considered late and will not be considered in the final rulemaking.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Ethan Parker, Supervisory Insurance Specialist, Veterans Benefits Administration,
ethan.parker2@va.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
NSLI was created by Congress on October 8, 1940, to handle the insurance needs of World War II service personnel. National Life Insurance Act of 1940, 54 Stat. 1008 (1940) (currently located at
38 U.S.C. 1901
et seq.
). Policies were issued from 1940 until April 24, 1951, under a variety of plans and as renewable term insurance, including policies issued under the “V” prefix (hereinafter, NSLI-V). Congress later authorized a limited reopening of NSLI to certain eligible World War II and Korean War veterans under Public Law (Pub. L.) 88-664, 78 Stat. 1094, 1096 (1964) (currently located at
38 U.S.C. 1925
). During this time, policies were issued under the “J,” “JR,” and “JS” prefixes and are collectively referred to as the Veterans' Reopened Insurance (VRI) program. There are no longer any active reopened policies with the prefix “JS.”
VA has determined that it is no longer necessary to collect premiums from veterans for NSLI-V policies and the VRI-J and VRI-JR policies. These policies cover predominantly World War II-era veterans and have been closed to new issues for decades. There are approximately 16,000 current policyholders under NSLI-V, VRI-J, and VRI-JR, ranging in age from 87 to 101 years. The funds that cover these policies are in strong financial position, and VA concludes there are sufficient financial resources to cover future liabilities and cost, while providing adequate margin to guard against adverse experience and allow for the payment of dividends.
The NSLI-V, VRI-J, and VRI-JR programs are self-supporting (that is, operating without any appropriations). They are supported exclusively by premium income, accumulated reserves, and investment income generated within their dedicated insurance funds. As noted above, these programs are in a strong financial position and possess sufficient resources to meet all projected future liabilities. Because no appropriated dollars are used to administer or sustain these programs, placing NSLI-V, VRI-J, and VRI-JR premium paying policies into paid-up status would not result in any cost to the Federal Government. Rather, this proposed rule would adjust the internal operation of a mature, closed insurance program whose financial condition would allow VA to discontinue premium collection while continuing to honor all policy obligations without taxpayer funding.
VA notes that declaring an insurance program paid-up when there are sufficient financial resources to cover the remaining active policies is consistent with past VA action. In 1983, VA previously declared the United States Government Life Insurance (USGLI) program paid-up via regulatory revisions. See
48 FR 1959
(Jan. 17, 1983). A paid-up declaration for NSLI-V, VRI-J, and VRI-JR would benefit veteran policyholders in multiple ways. First, approximately 65% of current policyholders are required to pay premiums and a paid-up declaration would discontinue premium obligations for eligible veterans. Additionally, because premium obligations would cease prospectively, policyholders would no longer face potential lapses for nonpayment or a need to establish good health to reinstate a lapsed policy. VA and the veteran policyholders VA serves would also benefit from this rule inasmuch as VA projects administrative savings due to reduced billing, check collections, dividends, and lapse-related activities.
I. Authority To Regulate
NSLI is established under
chapter 19 of title 38, United States Code
(U.S.C.), and implemented in
part 8 of title 38, Code of Federal Regulations
(CFR). Sections 1906 and 1908 authorize the Secretary to prescribe regulations regarding premium payments and general program policy provisions. Additionally, under
38 U.S.C. 501
, “[t]he Secretary has authority to prescribe all rules and regulations which are necessary or appropriate to carry out the laws administered by the Department.” Based on these authorities, VA is proposing to amend
38 CFR part 8
to establish paid-up status for NSLI policies with certain prefixes, which would cease premium payment collections for existing veteran policyholders of such policies.
II. Discussion of Proposed Changes
A. New § 8.37
VA proposes to add a new
38 CFR 8.37
, titled “Paid-up status of National Service Life Insurance.” Paragraph (a) of this new section, under the paragraph heading “Paid-up declaration and effective date,” would provide that effective 30 days after publication of a final rule, all NSLI-V, VRI-J, and VRI-JR policies that are not already paid-up, terminated, or in force under the extended term insurance provision would be considered paid-up such that no further premiums would be required to maintain these policies in force.
Under proposed paragraph (a), VA would include in its paid-up declaration NSLI-V, VRI-J, and VRI-JR policies for which premium payments may be outstanding but for which VA has not completed the final lapse action to extend the plan as term insurance pursuant to
38 CFR 8.14
. In such cases, these veterans would not have to repay the missed premiums, and their insurance policies would continue without interruption. VA considered several factors in deciding to include these policies in the paid-up declaration: these late-payment cases are less than 3% of all current policies, the average amount owed is less than $60 per policy, these veterans are advanced in age, the fund is in strong financial health, and collecting these small payments would cost both the veterans and VA more time and money than what is owed. Allowing these policies to remain in force and declared paid-up without requiring payment of a limited number of overdue premiums is therefore considered the most compassionate and cost-effective approach.
For any lapsed policy for which VA has taken final action, VA notes that such policy could be declared paid-up under this proposed rule if the veteran applies and is approved for policy reinstatement within the eligibility period provided by
38 CFR 8.7
.
Proposed paragraph (b) would include the heading “Continuation of policy provisions” and would specify that policies described in paragraph (a) would remain in effect subject to all contract provisions and applicable regulations, despite VA not collecting premiums from policyholders.
Proposed paragraph (c) would state, under the paragraph heading “Advance premiums,” that any premiums paid in advance for months subsequent to the effective month of the paid-up declaration shall be held on deposit on the policy to accrue interest until the insured requests a refund. VA considered automatically refunding any advance premiums to the veteran but opted to let the veteran decide due to potential unforeseen consequences associated with a lump-sum refund. VA would further outline in paragraph (c) that in the event a refund is requested, VA would remit to the veteran the
(
printed page 73728)
advance premiums and any accrued interest.
Proposed paragraph (d) would outline, under the paragraph heading “Effect of paid-up status on other provisions,” how other provisions within part 8 would or would not apply as a result of VA's paid-up declaration. Because multiple sections within part 8 refer to or assume ongoing premium obligations, this paragraph would assist readers in understanding how a paid-up declaration affects those sections.
VA proposes to clarify in paragraph (d)(1) that VA would not bill, collect, remit, deduct, or otherwise require premiums for policies described in § 8.37(a). As previously discussed, this would include policies for which premiums may be owed but VA has not completed the final lapse action to extend the plan as term insurance pursuant to § 8.14. For example, consider a policy for which a premium is due on June 1, but the veteran does not pay the premium during the 31-day grace period, which expires on July 2. Under current § 8.2(d)(2), VA would treat a premium paid after the 31-day grace period as timely if the veteran pays the premium within 61 days of its due date and the veteran is alive when the payment is mailed. In this case, because the 61-day period extends through July 31, the policy is outside the grace period but still within the period during which a late premium would still be considered timely. Also, VA would not have taken final lapse action and placed the policy on extended term insurance until after expiration of the 61-day period. If the paid-up declaration becomes effective July 10, the policy would qualify for the paid-up declaration under proposed § 8.37(a). Further, under proposed § 8.37(d)(1), VA would not require payment of the unpaid June premium, the policy would remain in force and paid-up as of July 10, and no further premiums would be billed or collected. The unpaid June premium becomes irrelevant with respect to maintaining coverage.
VA proposes to clarify in paragraph (d)(2) that the paid-up declaration does not alter, forgive, or extinguish any policy loans (see § 8.13) or lien amounts (see §§ 8.3(a)(6) and (b)(2) and 8.13) that arose prior to the paid-up declaration effective date. Such indebtedness would remain fully enforceable in accordance with the policy contract and applicable regulations.
Veterans would continue to be eligible to earn annual dividends based on the program's investment performance and experience. Because the declaration of paid-up status would mean that premiums would no longer be due after the effective date, certain dividend options—namely those that involve applying dividends to reduce or pay future premiums—would no longer function in practice because no premiums would exist to be reduced or offset. To provide clarity for veterans, proposed paragraph (d)(3) would specify that dividends would be held on deposit to accrue interest unless the insured elects an option available under § 8.10(e) through (g).
Finally, veterans are able to pay premiums through pre-authorized debit, allotment, or other deduction authorization. See,
e.g.,
38 CFR 8.4
and
8.5
. Proposed paragraph (d)(4) would specify that any such preauthorization related to premium payment would automatically terminate on the paid-up declaration effective date, ensuring that VA does not collect premiums that are no longer owed. This would include authorizations associated with policies that were not actively premium-paying at the time of the declaration but for which a deduction arrangement remains on file. It would not affect any authorizations for payment of any outstanding policy loans or liens, as described in proposed paragraph (d)(2).
B. Technical and Other Amendments
In addition to proposed new § 8.37, VA proposes to amend
38 CFR 8.2
, which discusses payment of premiums, by adding a new paragraph (f), under the heading “What effect does a paid-up declaration have upon the payment of premiums?” This paragraph would state that, notwithstanding paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section, no premiums would be due or payable for any policy described in § 8.37 on or after the effective date specified therein. While proposed § 8.37(d)(1) would state that premiums would not be required for policies VA has declared as paid-up, VA believes amending § 8.2 would provide additional clarity to readers looking for information about whether premiums would be owed on an NSLI policy.
Lastly, VA proposes to insert the undesignated heading “Other Provisions” before
38 CFR 8.31
. Part 8 includes undesignated headings to assist readers in finding relevant sections. Newer provisions have been added to the end of part 8 under the undesignated heading “Appeals” despite not being related to such topic. With the proposed addition of new § 8.37, VA is proposing a technical amendment to organize §§ 8.31 through 8.37 under this general heading to avoid confusion.
III. Explanation of Comment Period
VA is issuing this proposed rule with a 30-day comment period. The Administrative Procedure Act (APA) does not specify the length of the comment period, requiring only that an agency give the public an “opportunity to participate.” Agencies commonly allow 30 to 60 days for comment on a proposed rule. VA is limiting the comment period to 30 days because this rule would financially benefit an aged veteran population and, based on public feedback on past paid-up declarations via regulation, VA believes that a 30-day public comment period is sufficient to ensure VA can gather input from interested parties while accelerating the process toward a final rule to assist affected veterans.
Executive Orders 12866, 13563, and 14192
VA examined the impact of this rulemaking as required by Executive Orders 12866 (Sept. 30, 1993) and 13563 (Jan. 18, 2011), which direct agencies to assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives and, if regulation is necessary, to select regulatory approaches that maximize net benefits. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs has determined that this rulemaking is a significant regulatory action under section 3(f) of
Executive Order 12866
. This proposed rule is expected to be a deregulatory action under
Executive Order 14192
because this rule produces measurable savings by eliminating both Federal administrative activities and recurring burdens on insured veterans. These savings are outlined in the regulatory impact analysis associated with this rulemaking, which can be found as a supporting document at
www.regulations.gov
.
Regulatory Flexibility Act
The Secretary hereby certifies that this proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities as defined in the Regulatory Flexibility Act (
5 U.S.C. 601-612
). This certification is based on the fact that this rule would affect insured individuals and VA's administration of its insurance programs; it would impose no obligations on or impact small entities. Therefore, under
5 U.S.C. 605(b)
, the initial and final regulatory flexibility analysis requirements of
5 U.S.C. 603
and
604
do not apply.
Unfunded Mandates
This proposed rule would not result in the expenditure by State, local, and Tribal governments, in the aggregate, or
(
printed page 73729)
by the private sector, of $100 million or more (adjusted annually for inflation) in any one year.
Paperwork Reduction Act
This proposed rule contains no provisions constituting a collection of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3521
).
List of Subjects in
38 CFR Part 8
Insurance; Veterans
Signing Authority
Douglas A. Collins, Secretary of Veterans Affairs, approved this document on November 10, 2026, and authorized the undersigned to sign and submit the document to the Office of the Federal Register for publication electronically as an official document of the Department of Veterans Affairs.
Gabriela DeCuir,
Alternate Federal Register Liaison Officer, Department of Veterans Affairs.
For the reasons stated in the preamble, the Department of Veterans Affairs proposes to amend
38 CFR part 8
as set forth below:
PART 8—NATIONAL SERVICE LIFE INSURANCE
1.
The authority citation for part 8 continues to read as follows:
Authority:
38 U.S.C. 501
,
1901-1929
,
1981-1988
, unless otherwise noted.
2.
In § 8.2, add paragraph (f) to read as follows:
§ 8.2
Payment of premiums.
*
*
*
*
*
(f)
What effect does a paid-up declaration have upon the payment of premiums?
Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) through (e) of this section, no premiums shall be due or payable for any policy described in § 8.37 on and after the effective date specified therein.
3.
Add the undesignated center heading “Other Provisions” immediately before § 8.31.
4.
Add § 8.37 to read as follows:
§ 8.37
Paid-up status of National Service Life Insurance.
(a)
Paid-up declaration and effective date.
Effective [INSERT DATE 30 DAYS AFTER DATE OF PUBLICATION OF THE FINAL RULE IN THE
Federal Register
], all National Service Life Insurance policies issued under
38 U.S.C. 1904
with policy prefix V and policies issued under
38 U.S.C. 1925
with policy prefixes J and JR that are not paid-up, terminated, or in force under the extended term insurance provision (§ 8.14) are considered paid-up and no further premiums are required to maintain such policies in force. A policy that is in force under extended term insurance as of the paid-up declaration effective date and is later approved for reinstatement under § 8.7 shall be considered paid-up as of the paid-up declaration effective date, and no premiums shall be required to maintain such policy in force for any period beginning on or after that date.
(b)
Continuation of policy provisions.
Upon entering into non-premium-paying status following the paid-up declaration under paragraph (a), such policies shall remain in effect subject to all contract provisions and applicable regulations except for the premium-payment requirements.
(c)
Advance premiums.
Any premiums paid in advance but not yet applied as of the paid-up declaration effective date shall be held on deposit on the policy of the insured to accrue interest until the insured requests a refund or until the policy matures. If the insured requests a refund, or if the policy matures before the insured requests a refund, VA will remit the advance premiums plus any accrued interest.
(d)
Effect of paid-up status on other provisions.
Notwithstanding any other provision of this part, for any policy described in § 8.37(a):
(1) No premiums may be billed, collected, remitted, deducted, or otherwise required under §§ 8.2 through 8.5 as of the paid-up declaration date.
(2) Any lien or policy loan existing on a policy as of the paid-up declaration date shall remain in effect and shall continue to be subject to the terms of the policy and to §§ 8.11 through 8.15, as applicable. Nothing in this section shall be construed to cancel, forgive, or otherwise alter any such indebtedness or lien.
(3) Dividends shall be held on deposit on the policy of the insured to accrue interest in accordance with § 8.10(g), unless the insured elects another option under § 8.10(e)-(g).
(4) Any pre-authorized debit, allotment, or deduction authorization related to premium payment shall automatically terminate on the paid-up declaration effective date.

[Docket No. RM2027-3; Order No. 9796]
AGENCY:
Postal Regulatory Commission.
ACTION:
Notice of proposed rulemaking.
SUMMARY:
The Commission is acknowledging a recent Postal Service filing requesting the Commission initiate a rulemaking proceeding to consider changes to analytical principles relating to periodic reports. This document informs the public of the filing, invites public comment, and takes other administrative steps.
DATES:
Comments are due November 27, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Submit comments electronically via the Commission's Filing Online system at
https://www.prc.gov
.
Those who cannot submit comments electronically should contact the person identified in the
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT
section by telephone for advice on filing alternatives.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
David A. Trissell, General Counsel, at 202-789-6820.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Table of Contents
I. Introduction
II. Proposal
III. Notice and Comment
IV. Ordering Paragraphs
I. Introduction
On November 6, 2026, the Postal Service filed a petition pursuant to
39 CFR 3050.11
requesting that the Commission initiate a rulemaking proceeding to consider changes to analytical principles relating to the Postal Service's Priority Mail transportation model.
[
1
]
The Petition proposes replacing sample data from the Origin-Destination Information System—Revenue, Pieces, and Weight (ODIS-RPW) with Product Tracking and Reporting (PTR)
[
2
]
data to measure
(
printed page 73730)
Priority Mail weight and volume by origin-destination ZIP Code pair. Petition, Proposal at 1. The Postal Service states that it is not seeking to change the underlying conceptual methodology of the current Priority Mail model but only looking to change one data source.
Id.
The Postal Service also filed a supporting folder under seal containing model outputs and the proposed change's effect on unit costs by zone.
[
3
]
The Postal Service states that the folder contains commercially sensitive information similar to information reported in Library Reference USPS-LR-NP27 in its
Annual Compliance Report.
Petition at 1. The Postal Service therefore adopts by reference its application for non-public treatment filed in Docket No. ACR2025.
[
4
]
II. Proposal
Background.
The Postal Service contends that PTR should replace ODIS-RPW because PTR provides more complete data, considering the ODIS-RPW sample reduction approved in Commission Order No. 9449 took effect in FY 2026, Quarter 4.
[
5
]
The Postal Service notes that, in Docket No. RM2021-3, it identified PTR as a potential alternative source for determining the percentages of mail transported by air “to and from the offshore location.”
[
6
]
Following approval of the changes proposed in that docket, the Postal Service now considers it appropriate to use PTR for the relevant portions of the Priority Mail transportation model.” Petition, Proposal at 4.
The current model uses ODIS-RPW sample data for two principal purposes.
[
7
]
First, it distributes Alaska, Hawaii, and Air Taxi costs by zone. Second, it estimates the portions of Priority Mail involving ground-air or air-ground connections and the portion of Zone 1 mail classified as Intra-SCF. Petition, Proposal at 2. The Postal Service states that the current model pulls ODIS-RPW data from the origin-destination ZIP (ODZIP) file which identifies the origin-destination ZIP3 pairs in the sample and reports the corresponding Priority Mail weight and volume for the fiscal year.
Id.
Although the Postal Service considers the existing sample large, it states that reducing the sample size will increase statistical variance.
Id.
Proposal and rationale.
The Postal Service proposes replacing the ODIS-RPW-based ODZIP dataset with a more complete PTR dataset because PTR covers the relevant population-level census data, rather than a statistical sample, thereby eliminating sampling variance in the reported weights and volumes.
Id.
at 3. The Postal Service asserts that PTR data will be more representative of all Priority Mail, providing mail piece data for more ODZIP3 pairs.
Id.
Impact.
The Postal Service asserts that it sees changes in the weights by zone for Alaska, Hawaii, and Air Taxi networks because they rely on inputs from the ODIS-RPW sample data.
Id.
at 4. For highway-related inputs to the Transportation Cost Model workbook, the Postal Service reports a 0.87-percentage-point increase in the share of distance-related ground transportation costs associated with ground-to-air or air-to-ground connections.
Id.
It also reports a 7.41-percentage-point increase in the share of Local and Zone 1 weight attributable to Intra-SCF mail.
[
8
]
The Postal Service asserts that “[t]hese shifts are a result of the PTR data having more complete coverage of all ZIP3 combinations relative to the ODIS-RPW sample data.” Petition, Proposal at 4.
The Postal Service concludes that replacing ODIS-RPW sample data with census data from PTR results in an improvement in the quality, accuracy, and completeness of the Priority Mail transportation model and has minimal impact on the final unit cost by zone.
Id.
at 5.
III. Notice and Comment
The Commission establishes Docket No. RM2027-3 for consideration of matters raised by the Petition. More information on the Petition may be accessed via the Commission's website at
https://www.prc.gov
.
Interested persons may submit comments on the Petition and the Proposal no later than November 27, 2026. Pursuant to
39 U.S.C. 505
, Annette Morin is designated as an officer of the Commission (Public Representative) to represent the interests of the general public in this proceeding. The Public Representative does not represent any individual person, entity or particular point of view, and, when Commission attorneys are appointed, no attorney-client relationship is established.
IV. Ordering Paragraphs
It is ordered:
1. The Commission establishes Docket No. RM2027-3 for consideration of the matters raised by the Petition of the United States Postal Service to Initiate a Proceeding to Change Analytical Principles, filed November 6, 2026.
2. Comments by interested persons in this proceeding are due no later than November 27, 2026.
3. Pursuant to
39 U.S.C. 505
, the Commission appoints Annette Morin to serve as an officer of the Commission (Public Representative) to represent the interests of the general public in this docket.
4. This Order, or abstract thereof, will be published in the
Federal Register
.
By the Commission.
Danielle LeFlore,
Legal Assistant.

full_text:

Department of Energy
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
[Docket No. CP26-585-000]
The staff of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC or Commission) will prepare an environmental document that will discuss the environmental impacts of the DELMAR Regional Enhancement Project involving construction and operation of facilities by Eastern Shore Natural Gas Company (Eastern Shore) in Chester County, Pennsylvania; Cecil County, Maryland; New Castle, Kent, and Sussex Counties, Delaware. The Commission will use this environmental document in its decision-making process to determine whether the project is in the public convenience and necessity.
This notice announces the opening of the scoping process the Commission will use to gather input from the public and interested agencies regarding the project. As part of the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review process, the Commission takes into account concerns the public may have about proposals and the environmental impacts that could result from its action whenever it considers the issuance of a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity. This gathering of public input is referred to as “scoping.” The main goal of the scoping process is to focus the analysis in the environmental document on the important environmental issues. Additional information about the Commission's NEPA process is described below in the
NEPA Process and Environmental Document
section of this notice.
By this notice, the Commission requests public comments on the scope of issues to address in the environmental document. To ensure that your comments are timely and properly recorded, please submit your comments so that the Commission receives them in Washington, DC on or before 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 14, 2026. Comments may be submitted in written form. Further details on how to submit comments are provided in the
Public Participation
section of this notice.
Your comments should focus on the potential environmental effects, reasonable alternatives, and measures to avoid or lessen environmental impacts. Your input will help the Commission staff determine what issues they need to evaluate in the environmental document. Commission staff will consider all written comments during the preparation of the environmental document.
If you submitted comments on this project to the Commission before the opening of this docket on September 24, 2026, you will need to file those comments in Docket No. CP26-585-000 to ensure they are considered as part of this proceeding.
This notice is being sent to the Commission's current environmental mailing list for this project. State and local government representatives should notify their constituents of this proposed project and encourage them to comment on their areas of concern.
If you are a landowner receiving this notice, a pipeline company representative may contact you about the acquisition of an easement to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed facilities. The company would seek to negotiate a mutually acceptable easement agreement. You are not required to enter into an agreement. However, if the Commission approves the project, the Natural Gas Act conveys the right of eminent domain to the company. Therefore, if you and the company do not reach an easement agreement, the pipeline company could initiate condemnation proceedings in court. In such instances, compensation would be determined by a judge in accordance with state law. The Commission does not subsequently grant, exercise, or oversee the exercise of that eminent domain authority. The courts have exclusive authority to handle eminent domain cases; the Commission has no jurisdiction over these matters.
Eastern Shore provided landowners with a fact sheet prepared by the FERC entitled “An Interstate Natural Gas Facility On My Land? What Do I Need To Know?” which addresses typically asked questions, including the use of eminent domain and how to participate in the Commission's proceedings. This fact sheet along with other landowner topics of interest are available for viewing on the FERC website (
www.ferc.gov
) under the Natural Gas, Landowner Topics link.
Public Participation
There are three methods you can use to submit your comments to the Commission. Please carefully follow these instructions so that your comments are properly recorded. The Commission encourages electronic filing of comments and has staff available to assist you at (866) 208-3676 or
FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
.
(
printed page 73750)
(1) You can file your comments electronically using the
eComment
feature, which is located on the Commission's website (
www.ferc.gov
) under the link to FERC Online. Using eComment is an easy method for submitting brief, text-only comments on a project;
(2) You can file your comments electronically by using the
eFiling
feature, which is located on the Commission's website (
www.ferc.gov
) under the link to FERC Online. With eFiling, you can provide comments in a variety of formats by attaching them as a file with your submission. New eFiling users must first create an account by clicking on “
eRegister.”
You will be asked to select the type of filing you are making; a comment on a particular project is considered a “Comment on a Filing”; or
(3) You can file a paper copy of your comments by mailing them to the Commission. Be sure to reference the project docket number (CP26-585-000) on your letter. Submissions sent via the U.S. Postal Service must be addressed to: Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Room 1A, Washington, DC 20426. Submissions sent via any other carrier must be addressed to: Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 12225 Wilkins Avenue, Rockville, MD 20852.
Additionally, the Commission offers a free service called eSubscription which makes it easy to stay informed of all issuances and submittals regarding the dockets/projects to which you subscribe. These instant email notifications are the fastest way to receive notification and provide a link to the document files which can reduce the amount of time you spend researching proceedings. Go to
https://www.ferc.gov/​ferc-online/​overview
to register for eSubscription.
For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact the Office of Public Participation at (202) 502-6595 or
OPP@ferc.gov
.
Summary of the Proposed Project
The DELMAR Regional Enhancement Project would consist of the following facilities:
Chester County, Pennsylvania
Construct 2.55 miles of new 24-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline collocated within existing Eastern Shore pipelines (Parkesburg-Daleville Loop).
[
1
]
Associated aboveground facilities including the new Gum Tree remote monitoring valve (RMV) station and a new RMV at the existing Daleville Compressor Station.
Abandon the existing connection between the Daleville metering and regulation (M&R) station and the 8-inch-diameter Parkesburg Line and reconfigure belowground station piping at the Daleville Compressor Station.
Cecil County, Maryland
Construct 1.85 miles of 24-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline loop collocated with existing Eastern Shore pipelines (Barksdale Loop).
[
2
]
Associated aboveground facilities including the new Telegraph Road RMV Station and the new Barksdale Road RMV Station.
Abandon approximately 120 feet of belowground interconnect piping at the proposed Telegraph Road RMV Station.
New Castle, Kent, and Sussex Counties, Delaware
Replace 0.32 mile of existing 6-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline with 16-inch-diameter transmission pipeline (Tidewater Upgrade Segment 1).
Replace 1.28 miles of existing 6-inch-diameter transmission pipeline with 16-inch-diameter transmission pipeline (Tidewater Upgrade Segment 2) and a new manual shutoff valve at the existing Delaware City Compressor Station.
Abandon approximately 2.0 miles of existing 6-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline and miscellaneous reconfigurations (Tidewater 6-inch Line).
Construct 5.05 miles of new 16-inch-diameter natural gas transmission pipeline loop (16” Harrington Loop).
[
3
]
and associated aboveground facilities including a new RMV, and a new pipeline tie-in at the existing Felton Loop South RMV Station.
Abandon by-removal the existing North Bridgeville M&R station and construct a new M&R station adjacent to the abandoned M&R station.
The general locations of the project facilities are shown in appendix 1.
[
4
]
The DELMAR Regional Enhancement Project would provide a total of about 15,800 dekatherms per day (Dth/d) of natural gas per day to local distribution companies servicing residential and commercial customers. According to Eastern Shore, its project would allow the shippers to connect new customers and continue to service existing customers reliably under peak demand conditions.
Land Requirements for Construction
Construction of the proposed facilities would disturb about 135.61 acres of land for the pipelines, above-ground facilities, access roads, and temporary workspaces. Following construction, Eastern Shore would permanently maintain about 33.16 acres of land to operate the proposed facilities; the remaining acreage would be restored and revert to former uses. About 14 percent of the proposed pipeline and aboveground facilities parallels or uses existing utility easements.
NEPA Process and the Environmental Document
Any environmental document issued by the Commission will discuss impacts that could occur as a result of the construction and operation of the proposed project under the relevant general resource areas:
geology and soils;
water resources and wetlands;
vegetation and wildlife;
threatened and endangered species;
cultural resources;
land use;
visual resources;
air quality and noise; and
reliability and safety.
Commission staff have already identified several issues that deserve attention based on a preliminary review of the proposed facilities and the environmental information provided by Eastern Shore. This preliminary list of issues may change based on your comments and our analysis:
agricultural land use;
bald eagles and other birds of prey habitat;
mature tree clearing;
traffic; and
existing and planned land use conflicts (residential development and recreation).
Commission staff will also evaluate reasonable alternatives to the proposed project or portions of the project and make recommendations on how to lessen or avoid impacts on the various resource areas. Your comments will help Commission staff identify and focus on the issues that might have an effect on the human environment and
(
printed page 73751)
potentially eliminate others from further study and discussion in the environmental document.
Following this scoping period, Commission staff will determine whether to prepare an Environmental Assessment (EA) or an Environmental Impact Statement (EIS). The EA or the EIS will present Commission staff's independent analysis of the issues. If Commission staff prepares an EA, a
Notice of Schedule for the Preparation of an Environmental Assessment
will be issued. The EA may be issued for an allotted public comment period. The Commission would consider timely comments on the EA before making its decision regarding the proposed project. If Commission staff prepares an EIS, a
Notice of Intent to Prepare an EIS/Notice of Schedule
will be issued, which will open up an additional comment period. Staff will then prepare a draft EIS which will be issued for public comment. Commission staff will consider all timely comments received during the comment period on the draft EIS and revise the document, as necessary, before issuing a final EIS. Any EA or draft and final EIS will be available in electronic format in the public record through eLibrary
[
5
]
and the Commission's natural gas environmental documents web page (
https://www.ferc.gov/​industries-data/​natural-gas/​environment/​environmental-documents
). If eSubscribed, you will receive instant email notification when the environmental document is issued.
With this notice, the Commission is asking agencies with jurisdiction by law and/or special expertise with respect to the environmental issues of this project to formally cooperate in the preparation of the environmental document.
[
6
]
Agencies that would like to request cooperating agency status should follow the instructions for filing comments provided under the
Public Participation
section of this notice.
Consultation Under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act
In accordance with the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation's implementing regulations for section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, the Commission is using this notice to initiate consultation with the applicable State Historic Preservation Office(s), and to solicit their views and those of other government agencies, interested Indian tribes, and the public on the project's potential effects on historic properties.
[
7
]
The environmental document for this project will document findings on the impacts on historic properties and summarize the status of consultations under section 106.
Environmental Mailing List
The environmental mailing list includes federal, state, and local government representatives and agencies; elected officials; Native American Tribes; environmental and public interest groups; other interested parties; and local libraries and media outlets. This list also includes all affected landowners (as defined in the Commission's regulations) who are potential right-of-way grantors, whose property may be used temporarily for project purposes, or who own homes within certain distances of aboveground facilities, and anyone who submits comments on the project and includes a mailing address with their comments. Commission staff will update the environmental mailing list as the analysis proceeds to ensure that Commission notices related to this environmental review are sent to all individuals, organizations, and government entities interested in and/or potentially affected by the proposed project.
If you need to make changes to your name/address, or if you would like to remove your name from the mailing list, please complete one of the following steps:
(1) Send an email to
GasProjectAddressChange@ferc.gov
stating your request. You must include the docket number CP26-585-000 in your request. If you are requesting a change to your address, please be sure to include your name and the correct address. If you are requesting to delete your address from the mailing list, please include your name and address as it appeared on this notice. This email address is unable to accept comments.
OR
(2) Return the attached “Mailing List Update Form” (appendix 2).
Additional Information
Additional information about the project is available from the FERC website at
www.ferc.gov
using the eLibrary link. Click on the eLibrary link, click on “General Search” and enter the docket number in the “Docket Number” field. Be sure you have selected an appropriate date range. For assistance, please contact FERC Online Support at
FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
or (866) 208-3676, or for TTY, contact (202) 502-8659. The eLibrary link also provides access to the texts of all formal documents issued by the Commission, such as orders, notices, and rulemakings.
Public sessions or site visits will be posted on the Commission's calendar located at
https://www.ferc.gov/​news-events/​events
along with other related information.
(Authority:
18 CFR 2.1
)
Dated: November 12, 2026.

SUMMARY:
The U.S. Small Business Administration (“SBA” or “Agency”) is publishing this interim final rule (“IFR”) amending the U.S. Small Business Administration's loan guarantee regulations applicable to the Small Business Investment Company (“SBIC”) program to implement the
(
printed page 73666)
provisions of the Investing in All of America Act of 2025 (“the Investing Act”). These provisions increase the maximum amount of leverage available to SBICs issuing standard debentures in ratios of up to two-to-one against private capital, update the private capital definition to include certain government-sponsored corporations and college/university trusts or endowments, and grant Small Business Investment Companies access to additional “bonus” leverage for investments in critical technology areas, small manufacturers, rural areas, and low-income geographic areas, all in conformance with the Investing Act.

I. Background Information
A. Small Business Investment Company Program
SBA's small business investment company (“SBIC”) program is designed to enhance small business access to capital by stimulating and supplementing “the flow of private equity capital and long-term loan funds which small-business concerns need for the sound financing of their business operations and for their growth, expansion, and modernization, and which are not available in adequate supply.” Small Business Investment Act of 1958, as amended,
15 U.S.C. 661
,
et seq.
(the “SBIC Act”). SBA licenses SBICs to issue SBA-guaranteed loans (“Leverage”), typically with a ten-year term, the repayment of which is guaranteed by SBA using the full faith and credit of the United States. SBICs are privately owned and managed investment funds, licensed and regulated by SBA, that use capital raised from private investors and SBA-guaranteed loans to make equity and debt investments in qualifying small businesses. Recently, SBA has also entered into partnerships with the Department of War, National Aeronautics and Space Administration, and Department of Energy, to license SBICs that make investments in critical technology areas applicable to those agencies.
II. Justification for Publication as Interim Final Rule
The Administrative Procedure Act (“APA”) exempts rulemakings that involve matters relating to public property, loans, grants, benefits, or contracts from the APA's notice and comment procedures.
5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2)
. SBA notes that the provisions of the Investing Act being implemented by this interim final rule relate specifically to increasing the Leverage (
i.e.,
government-guaranteed loan) limits, increasing private capital inclusions for purposes of calculating Leverage, and granting additional “bonus” Leverage. Accordingly, as a rulemaking relating to the issuance of loans, SBA has determined that prior public notice and comment or delay in effective date is not required for this IFR's amendments to part 107. While SBA has determined that prior public notice and comment is not required for this IFR's amendments to part 107, SBA has nevertheless voluntarily elected to solicit comment. SBA will accept comments regarding this IFR on or before the date provided in the
DATES
section at the beginning of this IFR. Interested parties may submit comments and other information using any of the methods described in the
ADDRESSES
section at the beginning of this document. SBA will issue a final rule at a later date considering comments submitted during this period. Thus, SBA issues this interim final rule without prior public notice and comment or a delayed effective date under
5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2)
.
III. Section by Section Analysis
A. Section 107.50—Definitions
SBA is amending
13 CFR 107.50
to add the four definitions applicable to requests for “bonus” Leverage that are expressly identified in the Investing Act. SBA is adding the definition of Covered Technology Category to have the meaning set forth at
10 U.S.C. 149(h)
. SBA is adding the definition of Low-Income Geographic Area to have the meaning set forth in sec. 351 of the SBIC Act. In addition, SBA is adding the definition of Rural Area to have the meaning set forth in sec. 343(a)(13) of the Agricultural Act of 1961. Finally, SBA is adding the definition of Small Manufacturer to have the meaning set forth in sec. 501(e)(6) of the SBIC Act.
B. Section 107.230
SBA is amending
13 CFR 107.230
to implement changes set forth in the Investing Act to the statutory definition of private capital. SBA is revising this section to expressly include, as private capital, funds invested in a Licensee by (i) a foundation, endowment, or trust of any college or university and (ii) business revenues from a Federally chartered or Government-sponsored corporation, thereby removing the “Qualified Non-private Funds” limitations that were previously applicable to such funds.
C. Section 107.1120(d)
SBA is making a modification to
13 CFR 107.1120(d)
by removing the outdated reference to the $175 million
(
printed page 73667)
individual Leverage limitation set forth in this section and updating this section to reflect the appropriate limitations applicable under sec. 303(b)(2)(A)(ii) of the SBIC Act. SBA notes that this change is necessary to reflect the appropriate Leverage limitation increases set forth in the Investing Act.
D. Section 107.1150
This section identifies the Leverage limitations applicable to those SBICs approved to operate as a Leveraged Licensee. SBA is revising § 107.1150 by amending the introductory paragraph and paragraphs (a), (b), (d), and (e) to align with the applicable provisions set forth in the Investing Act.
First, SBA is removing the last sentence of the first paragraph set forth in § 107.1150 permitting SBICs to have a Leverage ratio exceeding 200 percent if the SBIC is able to demonstrate certain conditions that are satisfactory to SBA. SBA is removing this sentence in compliance with the update to sec. 303(b)(2) of the SBIC Act, which provides that an SBIC may not have a Leverage ratio exceeding 200 percent of its private capital. Similarly, SBA is amending § 107.1150(a)(1) by revising the applicable Leverage ratios for SBICs from 300 percent to 200 percent in accordance with the changes to sec. 303(b)(2) of the SBIC Act.
SBA is also amending the language set forth in § 107.1150(a)(3) to make clear that those SBICs already licensed in the program may apply for additional increases in Leverage following an increase to the outstanding Leverage maximum under the SBIC Act. This change will permit SBICs that were underwritten and approved for the maximum amount of Leverage under the SBIC Act at the time of licensure to apply for additional increases in Leverage following updates to the statutory maximum and provides transparency into SBA's credit policies by identifying the factors that SBA considers when evaluating requests to increase maximum Leverage amounts.
In addition, SBA is revising § 107.1150(b) to reflect that the total outstanding Leverage limit for multiple SBICs under common control shall be the amount set forth in the Investing Act (
i.e.,
$475,000,000 for SBICs that issue standard Debentures), while the total outstanding Leverage limit for other types of SBICs, including Accrual SBICs that are under common control with other Leveraged Licensees, will remain the amount set forth in sec. 303(b)(2)(B)(ii) of the SBIC Act (
i.e.,
$350,000,000).
Finally, SBA is revising § 107.1150(d) by removing provisions that referred to outdated Leverage maximums (
i.e.,
$150 million) and replacing that language with the appropriate procedures for SBICs to apply for additional “bonus” Leverage in connection with investments made in covered technology areas, small manufacturers, low-income geographic areas, and/or rural areas. SBA is also removing the sentence set forth in current § 107.1150(d) stating that any investment that an SBIC uses as a basis for seeking additional Leverage under § 107.1150(d) may not be used as a basis for seeking additional Leverage under § 107.1150(e). As a result, an SBIC that makes an investment that would qualify for both Leverage “bonuses” identified in §§ 107.1150(d) and 107.1150(e) may apply the full cost basis of the qualifying investment (subject to the applicable limits specified in each section) to each of §§ 107.1150(d) and 107.1150(e) for purposes of determining bonus Leverage eligibility. SBA believes that removing this sentence will incentivize investment into these critical areas while maintaining appropriate credit protection under the program.
IV. Compliance With Executive Orders 12866, 12988, 13132, 13563, and 14192; the Paperwork Reduction Act (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3520
); the Congressional Review Act (
5 U.S.C. 801-808
); and the Regulatory Flexibility Act (
5 U.S.C. 601-612
)
A. Executive Orders 12866 and 13563
Executive Orders (E.O.s) 12866 and 13563 direct agencies to assess costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives and, if regulation is necessary, to select regulatory approaches that maximize net benefits (including potential economic, environmental, public health and safety effects, distributive impacts, and equity).
E.O. 13563
emphasizes the importance of quantifying both costs and benefits, of reducing costs, of harmonizing rules, and of promoting flexibility. The Office of Management and Budget (“OMB”) has determined that this rule is a significant regulatory action under section 3(f)(1) of
Executive Order 12866
. SBA has prepared the below Regulatory Impact Analysis.
Regulatory Impact Analysis
1. Need for this Regulatory Action
This interim final rule makes non-discretionary modifications to part 107 to incorporate the provisions of the Investing Act. The current provisions of
13 CFR part 107
reference outdated statutory Leverage maxima, do not permit “bonus” Leverage for qualifying investments under the Investing Act, and include an outdated definition of private capital (as amended by the Investing Act). Without this rule, SBICs (and their limited partners) will not have certainty into what constitutes private capital (given the conflicting definition between the Investing Act and
13 CFR part 107
) and will not have access to “bonus” Leverage as contemplated by the Investing Act. In addition, SBA would lack a regulatory basis for processing “bonus” Leverage requests without this rulemaking.
2. Baseline and Proposed Changes
This rule incorporates programmatic changes implemented by the Investing Act, which is the baseline that necessitated this update to the regulations. The regulations are being updated to reflect changes to the Small Business Investment Act of 1958, as amended by the Investing Act. These primary changes include the following:
The Investing Act increases the individual Leverage maximum from $175 million to $250 million for eligible SBICs issuing standard Debentures and the common control Leverage maximum from $350 million to $475 million for eligible SBICs issuing standard Debentures. This rule clarifies that the SBICs currently licensed in the program will be eligible to apply for this additional Leverage amount. SBA estimates that of the approximately 368 active SBIC licensed funds, 72 SBIC licensees are potentially eligible to increase their Leverage limit. Currently, SBA has already received approximately 60 requests from SBICs to increase SBA guaranteed Leverage.
The Investing Act also clarifies that the maximum amount of Leverage that an SBIC may have outstanding at any time may not exceed 200% of its private capital, bringing the statute in line with current practices of the SBIC program. This rule conforms the provisions of part 107 to the Investing Act. As this provision of the Investing Act is already consistent with existing SBA practices, this change will not have any adverse impact on SBICs.
The Investing Act expands the definition of “private capital” to include certain governmental funds (including public university and college foundations, trusts, and endowments) that were previously subject to limitations and restrictions for inclusion as private capital. This rule updates the definition of private capital by codifying the text of the Investing Act expanding the definition of private capital.
The Investing Act authorizes additional “bonus” Leverage for SBICs in connection with investments made in
(
printed page 73668)
covered technology areas, small manufacturers, low-income geographic areas, and/or rural areas. This rule incorporates the “bonus” Leverage provisions of the Investing Act and provides eligibility for this bonus Leverage for investments made after May 19, 2026, by existing or future SBICs.
3. Benefits and Costs of the Rule
The Investing Act increases the limit on Leverage provided by SBA funds, expands the definition of private capital and authorizes additional “bonus” Leverage for eligible SBICs investing in covered technology areas, small manufacturers, low-income geographic areas, and/or rural areas. SBA anticipates that these regulations, which directly implement statutory provisions of the Investing Act, will result in approximately $815.7 million of average annual additional capital available for investment in the U.S. economy in eligible small businesses. In order to determine this amount, SBA first calculated the aggregate amount of additional Leverage anticipated to be available to SBICs under the provisions of the Investing Act increasing the Leverage threshold applicable to SBICs issuing standard Debentures. Based on Leverage increase requests already received by SBA, SBA estimates that approximately $3.297 billion will be made available across approximately sixty (60) SBICs over a five-year period. Additionally, SBA estimated the anticipated amount of Leverage expected to be made available to SBICs pursuant to the provisions of the Investing Act permitting access to “bonus” Leverage for investments in low-income or rural areas, covered technology categories, and small manufacturers, subject to an aggregate cap of the lesser of 50 percent of private capital or $125 million. SBA conducted a review of anticipated “bonus” Leverage availability based on a review of its current portfolio for SBICs in their current investment period that would also be eligible for Leverage based on their current private capital ratios (for SBICs with Leverage, SBA anticipates that 60 percent of the investments made by critical technology SBICs will qualify for bonus Leverage, whereas 20 percent of the investments made by other Leveraged licensees will qualify for bonus Leverage availability). As a result of its analysis, SBA estimates that approximately $2.141 billion in “bonus” Leverage would be made available across approximately forty (40) SBICs over a five-year period. SBA then reduced the aggregate additional Leverage amounts (
i.e.,
increased Leverage and “bonus” Leverage) by 25 percent to account for funds that may not avail themselves of the available additional Leverage and anticipated operating expenses of SBIC licensees, which would total $4.079 billion. This amount is estimated to be invested over a five-year time horizon, equaling approximately $815.7 million, on average, invested in small businesses annually. Therefore, based on these assumptions, SBA estimates that this interim final rule will result in just over $815.7 million in average annual additional capital being invested into small businesses.
The rule imposes no compliance costs to the public. It creates no new information collection within the meaning of the Paperwork Reduction Act, and this rulemaking neither imposes new recordkeeping or reporting requirements nor mandates any action by any Licensees, applicants, investors, or small business concerns. Participation is entirely voluntary, and a Licensee seeking additional Leverage does so at its own election. Further, implementing the Investing Act will not have an effect on direct spending or revenues,
[
1
]
and the Committee Report applicable to this legislation indicated that Congress does not believe that there will be any new or increased costs attributable to the Investing Act.
[
2
]
In addition, this rule will result in a minimal increase in administrative costs. SBA anticipates that the annual average cost to the U.S. government of analyzing requests for additional Leverage will be $29,442, based on a GS-12, Step 1 located at SBA's Washington, DC headquarters, working approximately two (2) hours per Leverage request, which would take 600 hours based on an estimated 300 requests. This rulemaking is expected to support, on average, approximately $815.7 million annually in additional investments to small businesses as a result the increased Leverage available to SBICs and a total average administrative cost of $29,442 annually for SBA to grant these additional Leverage requests.
4. Alternatives Considered
This IFR implements changes made by the Investing Act. There were no feasible alternatives available.
B.
Executive Order 14192
This interim final rule is not an
Executive Order 14192
regulatory action, because it does not impose any more than de minimis regulatory costs. This interim final rule implements the provisions of the Investing Act. Specifically, the defined terms changes set forth in
13 CFR 107.50
and
107.230
codify exactly the definitions outlined in the Investing Act. The changes to
13 CFR 107.1120
codify the Investing Act's changes to common control Leverage maxima, and the changes to § 107.1150 codify the increase to maximum Leverage for individual SBICs and permits and outline the applicable limitations of the Investing Act relating to “bonus” Leverage. SBA notes that it made a minor change not directly expressed in the Investing Act by removing a sentence in current § 107.1150(d) stating that any investment used as a basis for seeking additional Leverage under § 107.1150(d) may not be used to seek additional Leverage under § 107.1150(e); however, SBA notes that the removal of this language removes an unnecessary regulatory restraint on an SBIC's access to capital and is consistent with both the Investing Act and the SBIC Act.
Accordingly, this interim final rule does not impose any additional obligations or operational constraints beyond those specified in the Investing Act, does not create any new reporting or recordkeeping requirements, and does not impose any additional mandatory obligations on SBICs participating in the program. Requests for “bonus” Leverage under this interim final rulemaking are purely voluntary, and there are not any budgetary impacts attributable to this rulemaking. Any costs attributable to this interim final rule are purely administrative in nature and as noted above, are expected to be de minimis costs of processing additional Leverage.
C.
Executive Order 12988
This action meets applicable standards set forth in Sections 3(a) and 3(b)(2) of
Executive Order 12988
, Civil Justice Reform, to minimize litigation, eliminate ambiguity, and reduce burden. The action does not have a retroactive or preemptive effect.
D.
Executive Order 13132
This interim final rule does not have federalism implications as defined in
Executive Order 13132
. It would not have substantial direct effects on the States, on the relationship between the national government and the States, or on the distribution of power and
(
printed page 73669)
responsibilities among the various levels of government, as specified in the Executive Order. As such it does not warrant the preparation of a Federalism Assessment. Additionally, the rule will not require new compliance activities or reporting by state, local, or tribal governments.
E. Paperwork Reduction Act,
44 U.S.C. 3501-3520
SBA has determined that this interim final rule does not affect any existing collection of information and does not propose any new collection of information.
F. Congressional Review Act,
5 U.S.C. 801-808
Subtitle E of the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996, also known as the Congressional Review Act,
5 U.S.C. 801
et seq.,
provides that before a rule may take effect, the agency promulgating the rule must submit a rule report, which includes a copy of the rule, to each House of the Congress and to the Comptroller General of the United States. SBA will submit a report containing this rulemaking and other required information to the U.S. Senate, the U.S. House of Representatives, and the Comptroller General of the United States. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA) in the Office of Management and Budget has determined that this is a major rule under
5 U.S.C. 804
. If a rule is deemed major, the CRA generally provides that the rule may not take effect until at least 60 days following its publication unless the agency for good cause finds that notice and public procedure are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest.
5 U.S.C. 808(2)
. As this IFR amends regulations concerning loan guarantees, it is exempt from the notice-and-comment and effective date delay requirements in the Administrative Procedure Act, thereby rendering notice and public procedure unnecessary.
See
5 U.S.C. 553(a)(2)
. In addition, this IFR is narrowly tailored to implement the Investing Act, including provisions which are already in effect. For these reasons, SBA for good cause finds that notice and public procedure is unnecessary, and in accordance with
5 U.S.C. 808(2)
, this IFR will be effective upon publication.
G. Regulatory Flexibility Act,
5 U.S.C. 601-612
The Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA),
5 U.S.C. 601
, requires administrative agencies to consider the effect of their actions on small entities, small nonprofit enterprises, and small local governments. Pursuant to the RFA, when an agency issues a rulemaking, the agency must prepare a regulatory flexibility analysis which describes the impact of the rule on small entities. However, the RFA requires such analysis only where notice and comment rulemaking is required. As discussed above, SBA is not required to publish a general notice of proposed rulemaking pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act. Accordingly, SBA is not required to conduct a regulatory flexibility analysis.

§ 107.1150
Maximum amount of Leverage.
A Leveraged Licensee, other than an Early Stage SBIC, may have maximum outstanding Leverage as set forth in paragraphs (a), (b), (d), and (e) of this section. An Early Stage SBIC may have maximum outstanding Leverage as set forth in paragraph (c) of this section.
(a)
Individual Licensee.
Subject to SBA's credit policies, if you are a Leveraged Licensee and not an Accrual SBIC or Reinvestor SBIC, the maximum amount of Leverage you may have outstanding at any time is the Individual Maximum. If you are an Accrual SBIC or Reinvestor SBIC, the maximum amount of Leverage and accrued interest you may have outstanding at any time is the Individual Maximum. The Individual Maximum means the lesser of:
(1) 200 percent of your Leverageable Capital;
(2) 100 percent of your Leverageable Capital if you have less than $5 million in Regulatory Capital and you were Licensed because you are headquartered in an Underlicensed State; or
(3) The maximum Leverage available to a single Licensee under section 303(b)
(
printed page 73670)
of the Act, as applicable to you at the time of licensure. (b)
Multiple Licensees Under Common Control.
Subject to SBA's credit policies, two or more Licensees under Common Control may have maximum aggregate outstanding Leverage as permitted under the Act, provided, however, that if you are an Accrual SBIC, the maximum outstanding Leverage which you and other Licensees under Common Control may have may not exceed the amount specified in section 303(b)(2)(B)(ii) of the Act. (d)
Additional Leverage Based on Investments in Covered Technology Categories, Small Manufacturers, Low-Income Geographic Areas, and Rural Areas.
You may submit a request for one or more additional Leverage commitments, in excess of the amounts otherwise available under paragraphs (a)(3) and (b) of this section, and, upon SBA's approval of such additional Leverage commitment(s), a request to draw such additional Leverage, for an investment made after May 19, 2026, in a Small Business which is located in either a Low-Income Geographic Area or a Rural Area, is a Small Manufacturer, or operates primarily in a Covered Technology Category in the amount specified in paragraphs (d)(1) and (2) of this section.
(1) Subject to SBA's credit policies, you may have outstanding Leverage in excess of the amounts permitted by paragraph (a)(3) of this section in an amount equal to the lesser of paragraphs (d)(1)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) of this section, where:
(i) The amount determined under paragraph (a)(1) of this section (as set forth in your Total Intended Leverage Commitment, as applicable) minus the amount determined under paragraph (a)(3) of this section;
(ii) The total cost basis, as reported on your most recent filing of SBA Form 468, of any investments made on or after May 19, 2026, in any Small Business which is located in either a Low-Income Geographic Area or a Rural Area, is a Small Manufacturer, or operates primarily in a Covered Technology Category;
(iii) 50 percent of your Private Capital; and
(iv) $125,000,000.
(2) Subject to SBA's credit policies, you and other Licensees under Common Control may have outstanding Leverage in excess of the amount otherwise available under paragraph (b) of this section in an amount equal to the lesser of paragraphs (d)(2)(i), (ii), and (iii) of this section, where:
(i) The total cost basis, as reported on the most recently filed SBA Forms 468, of any investments made on or after May 19, 2026, by you and by other Licensees under Common Control in any Small Business which is located in a Low-Income Geographic Area or a Rural Area, which is a Small Manufacturer, or which operates primarily in a Covered Technology Category;
(ii) The amount that equals 50 percent of the sum of your Private Capital and the Private Capital of all Licensees that are under Common Control with you; and
(iii) $125,000,000.
(3) The amount calculated in paragraph (d)(2) of this section equals the additional Leverage availability for you and other Licensees under Common Control under paragraph (b) of this section, provided, however, that additional Leverage made available under paragraph (d)(2) of this section may not:
(i) Cause your total drawn and committed Leverage to exceed 200 percent of your Leverageable Capital or any lower amount or ratio approved by SBA at licensure; or
(ii) Exceed the lesser of:
(A) 50 percent of the total Private Capital of the Licensees under Common Control; or
(B) $125,000,000.

SUMMARY:
Notice is hereby given, pursuant to the provisions of the rules and regulations of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), the Office of Tribal Relations is announcing a meeting of the Tribal Advisory Committee. The committee is authorized under the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 (the 2018 Farm Bill) and operates in compliance with the Federal Advisory Committee Act. The purpose of the committee is to provide advice and guidance to USDA on matters related to Tribal and Indian affairs.
DATES:
An in-person meeting with a virtual webinar with a call-in option will be held on Monday, December 7, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to approximately 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time (PT). The meeting will be held during the Intertribal Agriculture Council's Annual Conference at the Virgin Hotels; 4455 Paradise Rd., Las Vegas, NV 89169. Updates to the location, such as the meeting room, will be published on the Tribal Advisory Committee web page at
https://www.usda.gov/​about-usda/​general-information/​staff-offices/​office-tribal-relations/​tribal-advisory-committee
.

https://www.zoomgov.com/​webinar/​register/​WN_​l7clY6nWSNmO1uh3LXaOCA#/​registration
.

The public may file written comments to the Tribal Advisory Committee by Thursday, December 3, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET via email at
Tribal.Relations@usda.gov
.

.

.

.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Discussion
On September 30, 2026, SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades SMR, LLC (Palisades SMR), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Holtec International, filed with the NRC, the second part (Part 2) of a phased construction permit application (CPA) for a utilization facility pursuant to Section 103 of the Atomic Energy Act and part 50 of title 10 of the
Code of Federal Regulations
(10 CFR), “Domestic Licensing of Production and Utilization Facilities.” Part 2 of the application consists of a complete preliminary safety analysis report. Palisades SMR also provided an updated version of the Quality Assurance Topical Report that was previously approved by the NRC and is seeking review of these revisions. Part 2 also contains a set of exemption requests which address aspects of the CPA that require exemption from the existing rules. The general and financial information submitted with the Part 1 of the application is incorporated by reference into the Part 2 CPA.
(
printed page 73818)
Part 1 of the application was submitted on December 31, 2025, and consisted of a limited work authorization request pursuant to
10 CFR 50.10(d)
, “Request for limited work authorization,” three exemption requests, and a comprehensive environmental report. In Part 1, Palisade SMR was seeking NRC approval to conduct certain early construction activities of a dual-unit SMR-300 plant at the PEC in Covert, Michigan. In Part 2, Palisades SMR is seeking NRC approval to complete construction activities of the dual-unit SMR-300 plant site.
Palisades SMR submitted Part 2 of its application as part of a phased application approach for a construction permit for a utilization facility, as described in
10 CFR 2.101(a)(9)
and
10 CFR 2.600(d)
.
The NRC staff is currently undertaking its acceptance review of the application. If the application is accepted for docketing, subsequent
Federal Register
notices will be issued that address the acceptability of the tendered construction permit application for docketing and provisions for participation of the public in the permitting process. These weekly notices of receipt and availability of the application are being provided in accordance with the requirements in
10 CFR 50.43(a)(3)
.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Jason Latona, Assistant Director, Loan Guaranty Service, Veterans Benefits Administration, (202) 461-9201.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
In accordance with
38 U.S.C. 2102(e)
,
38 U.S.C. 2102A(b)(2)
,
38 U.S.C. 2102B(b)(2)
, and
38 CFR 36.4411
, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs announces for FY 2027 the aggregate amounts of assistance available to veterans and service members eligible for SAH program grants.
Section 2102(e)(2) authorizes the Secretary to increase the aggregate amounts of SAH assistance annually based on a residential home cost-of construction index. Consistent with
38 CFR 36.4411(a)
, VA uses the Turner Building Cost Index for this purpose. Such an increase will be equal to the percentage by which the Turner Building Cost Index for the most recent calendar year exceeds that of the next preceding calendar year. If, however, the Turner Building Cost Index for the most recent full calendar year is equal to or less than the next preceding calendar year, the percentage increase will be zero. See
38 CFR 36.4411(b)
.
In the most recent quarter for which the Turner Building Cost Index is available, second quarter 2026, the index showed 5.15 percent over the index value listed for second quarter 2025. Turner Construction Company,
https://www.turnerconstruction.com/​cost-index
.
Pursuant to
38 CFR 36.4411(a)
, therefore, the aggregate amounts of assistance for SAH grants made pursuant to
38 U.S.C. 2101(a)
and
2101(b)
will increase by 5.15 percent for FY 2027.
Sections 2102A(b)(2) and 2102B(b)(2) require the Secretary to apply the same percentage calculated pursuant to section 2102(e) to grants authorized pursuant to sections 2102A and 2102B. As such, the maximum amount of assistance available under these grants will also increase by 5.15 percent for FY 2027.
The increases are effective as of October 1, 2026.
