Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106891; File No. SR-CCUS-2026-01]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 4, 2026, Cboe Clear U.S., LLC (“CCUS” or the “Clearinghouse”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared primarily by CCUS. CCUS filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
3
]
and paragraph (f)(2) of Rule 19b-4
[
4
]
thereunder, such that the proposed rule change was immediately effective upon filing with the Commission. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
CCUS proposes to amend its Fee Schedule to adopt a Broker-Dealer Clearing Member Incentive Program (the “BD Program”) in connection with CCUS's issuance and clearance of securities listed on a national securities exchange (“Securities Contracts”),
[
5
]
and to reduce the clearing fee for Securities Contracts from $0.002 to $0.001 per cleared contract.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), CCUS's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​solutions/​clearing/​us/​notices/​ccus-sec-filings/​
), and at the principal office of CCUS.
II. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the clearing agency included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The clearing agency has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
CCUS proposes to amend its Fee Schedule to adopt the BD Program in connection with its issuance and clearance of Securities Contracts, and to reduce the clearing fee for Securities Contracts.
[
6
]
Market Makers and other broker-dealers trading for their own proprietary accounts are critical for options to have liquid and active markets. These market participants generally clear securities options transactions through separate clearing firms, including, in the case of broker-dealers, transactions for proprietary accounts of broker-dealers (“PAB” transactions). Therefore, for Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts issued by CCUS to be cleared, CCUS Clearing Members must be able and eligible to clear Securities Contracts.
Before a clearing firm can clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts at CCUS, CCUS understands a clearing firm must complete significant back-office development work, including system development, connectivity to CCUS, risk and margin integration, testing and certification, and operational readiness. Clearing firms have many competing items in their development queues. To incentivize clearing firms to prioritize in the near term the work needed to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts at CCUS, CCUS proposes to adopt the BD Program.
(
printed page 73839)
Eligibility and Selection
CCUS may select BD Clearing Members
[
7
]
(or prospective BD Clearing Members) to participate in the BD Program. To be eligible, a firm must: (1) notify CCUS of its intent to participate in the BD Program no later than November 11, 2026, in a form and manner prescribed by CCUS; and (2) be a BD Clearing Member or a prospective BD Clearing Member at the time it provides such notice.
CCUS will select BD Program participants from among eligible firms by considering the following factors: (1) adequacy of capital, (2) operational capacity, (3) clearing experience, (4) regulatory history, and (5) other relevant factors CCUS believes demonstrate the firm's capacity to engage in the clearing of Securities Contracts. CCUS believes it is reasonable to limit participation in the BD Program to clearing firms that can demonstrate they possess the resources to be operationally ready to clear Securities Contracts at CCUS in a compressed time period (as early as the open of regular trading hours on November 16, 2026, as discussed below). Regardless of participation in the BD Program, any BD Clearing Member (or prospective BD Clearing Member, once approved) may clear Securities Contracts through CCUS at any time those contracts are trading on a national securities exchange.
Standards and Payments
If, by the open of regular trading hours on November 16, 2026, a BD Program participant (1) is a BD Clearing Member in good standing with CCUS that has satisfied applicable documentation and operational requirements prescribed by CCUS and completed connectivity and certification testing for clearing Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts cleared by CCUS,
[
8
]
and (2) submits written documentation evidencing readiness to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts cleared by CCUS, each in a manner prescribed by CCUS, the BD Program participant will receive a one-time payment of $1,250,000. If a BD Program participant does not satisfy the above criteria by the open of regular trading hours on November 16, 2026, but does so by November 25, 2026, the BD Program participant will instead receive a one-time payment of $750,000. If a BD Program participant does not satisfy the above criteria by November 25, 2026, but does so by November 30, 2026, the BD Program participant will instead receive a one-time payment of $500,000.
Clearing Fee Reduction
CCUS also proposes to reduce the clearing fee for Securities Contracts set forth in the clearing fees table on the Fee Schedule from $0.002 per cleared contract to $0.001 per cleared contract. The reduced fee will apply equally to all transactions. CCUS proposes the reduction to lower the cost of clearing transactions at CCUS.
2. Statutory Basis
CCUS believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a registered clearing agency and, in particular, Section 17A(b)(3) of the Act.
[
9
]
Specifically, CCUS believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(D) of the Act,
[
10
]
which requires that the rules of a clearing agency provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its participants.
CCUS also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act,
[
11
]
which requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a national system for the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and that they not be designed to permit unfair discrimination in the admission of participants or among participants in the use of the clearing agency.
CCUS believes the BD Program is reasonably designed to encourage clearing firms to prioritize the significant back-office development work CCUS understands they would need to undertake to enable them to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts that will clear through CCUS in a compressed timeline. CCUS believes this will support liquid and active markets in listed options issued and cleared by CCUS, which facilitates tighter spreads, increased trading opportunities, and enhanced market quality to the benefit of all market participants that trade those options. CCUS believes the fixed amounts are reasonable in light of the internal resources, system development, and opportunity costs CCUS would expect a clearing firm to incur to complete this work by the proposed deadlines.
While CCUS has no way of predicting with certainty how many BD Clearing Members or prospective BD Clearing Members will notify CCUS of their intent to participate in the BD Program, CCUS anticipates that at least one prospective BD Clearing Member will do so. CCUS believes the different payment amounts for BD Program participants are reasonable because the higher payment amounts reflect the greater value to the market of having BD Clearing Members able to clear Securities Contracts at CCUS by an earlier date. CCUS believes the proposed deadlines are reasonable based on its assessment that they provide clearing firms with sufficient time to satisfy the proposed program standards while incentivizing clearing firms to complete the work in an expeditious manner to justify the payment amounts.
CCUS notes the proposed BD Program, including the proposed payment amounts, is comparable to other participant incentive programs designed to promote liquidity in listed options. For example, CCUS currently offers the FCM Clearing Member Incentive Program, which provides up to $500,000 for completing the work required to become and actively clear as a CCUS Clearing Member.
[
12
]
Similar to the BD Program, the CCUS FCM Clearing Member Incentive Program was designed to incentivize certain clearing firms to become Clearing Members given regulatory and operational costs associated with becoming Clearing Members. Additionally, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe Options”) currently offers several Lead Market-Maker (“LMM”) Incentive Programs designed to incentivize quoting in certain products to provide significant liquidity, which would, in turn, provide greater trading opportunities, market transparency, and enhanced price discovery for all market
(
printed page 73840)
participants, in the applicable options, including during trading hours outside of regular trading hours for certain products when liquidity may otherwise be lower.
[
13
]
Additionally, CCUS believes the BD Program is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory. The BD Program is open to any securities clearing firm that meets the objective eligibility criteria. CCUS will select BD Program participants by considering objective factors and applying them consistently to all firms that notify CCUS of their intent to participate, which factors bear directly on whether a firm can reasonably be expected to satisfy the BD Program standards by the proposed deadlines. The standards that a BD Program participant must satisfy to receive any payment (including the specified deadlines), and the fixed payment amounts, will apply equally to all BD Program participants. Participation in the BD Program is voluntary and within the discretion of a clearing firm, as is the determination by a clearing firm to commit its own resources to complete development work to clear Securities Contracts at CCUS. If a clearing firm participates in the BD Program but does not satisfy a payment standard, it simply does not receive the payment. Similarly, if a clearing firm does not participate in the BD Program but wishes to be a BD Clearing Member and clear Securities Contracts at CCUS, it may do so within its own discretion.
CCUS believes it is not unfairly discriminatory to offer payments only to BD Clearing Members (and prospective BD Clearing Members) that satisfy the BD Program standards, because BD Program participants will undertake development obligations and costs that other Clearing Members do not to be in a position to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts cleared at CCUS in a compressed timeframe to the benefit of all market participants.
CCUS further believes the proposed reduction of the clearing fee for Securities Contracts from $0.002 to $0.001 per cleared contract is reasonable because it lowers the cost of clearing for all Clearing Members that clear those contracts, which CCUS believes may encourage additional clearing activity in Securities Contracts at CCUS to the benefit of all market participants. CCUS believes the reduced fee is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply uniformly to all transactions.
CCUS further believes the proposed rule change will be implemented consistently with the safeguarding of securities and funds in its custody or control or for which it is responsible. The BD Program establishes one-time incentive payments and does not amend CCUS's margin methodology, Guaranty Fund requirements, default management procedures, or other risk management rules or procedures. To receive any payment, a BD Program participant must be a BD Clearing Member in good standing that has satisfied all applicable documentation and operational requirements prescribed by CCUS, including conformance testing, deposit of the Minimum Guaranty Fund requirement, and account activation, and has completed connectivity and certification testing. The BD Program does not waive or modify any CCUS membership, financial, or risk management requirement applicable to BD Clearing Members. Payments under the BD Program will be funded from CCUS's general corporate resources.
B. Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
CCUS does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
[
14
]
All clearing firms that are BD Clearing Members or prospective BD Clearing Members may notify CCUS of their intent to participate in the BD Program. CCUS will select participants in the BD Program based on the same objective factors. The terms of the BD Program, including the standards necessary to be met for payments and the amounts of payments, will apply uniformly to all participants. Participation in the BD Program is voluntary and within the discretion of a clearing firm, as is the determination by a clearing firm to commit its own resources to complete development work to clear Securities Contracts at CCUS. If a clearing firm participates in the BD Program but does not satisfy a payment standard, it simply does not receive the payment. Similarly, if a clearing firm does not participate in the BD Program but wishes to be a BD Clearing Member and clear Securities Contracts at CCUS, it may do so within its own discretion.
CCUS believes the BD Program will promote competition by increasing the number of clearing firms able to clear Market Maker or PAB transactions in Securities Contracts through CCUS, which may promote liquid and active markets in these securities, which may facilitate tighter spreads and trading opportunities to the benefit of all market participants. Similarly, the reduced clearing fee for Securities Contracts will apply equally to all Clearing Members and does not impose any burden on competition; rather, CCUS believes the lower fee may promote competition by reducing the cost of clearing those contracts.
C. Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
CCUS has not solicited, and does not intend to solicit, written comments on the proposed rule change, and has not received any written comments from Clearing Members or other interested parties.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106890; File No. SR-NYSEAMER-2026-100]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 30, 2026, NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Section 341 (“Acquisition of a Listed Issuer by an Unlisted Entity”) of the NYSE American Company Guide (“Company Guide”) to address the application of Section 341 to multi-step transactions. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
(
printed page 73836)
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
Section 341 (“Acquisition of a Listed Issuer by an Unlisted Entity”) of the Company Guide provides that, if a listed issuer engages in a Reverse Merger,
[
3
]
it will be eligible for continued listing on the Exchange only if the post-transaction entity meets the standards for initial listing. Section 341 provides that the Exchange will refuse to list additional securities of a listed issuer in connection with a Reverse Merger unless the post-transaction entity meets the standards for initial listing and the listed issuer obtains shareholder approval of the issuance of such securities as required by Section 713(b) of the Company Guide.
In recent times, a small number of companies listed on the Exchange have structured a Reverse Merger as a multi-step transaction. In a multi-step reverse merger, in connection with the consummation of a merger with the unlisted entity, the listed company issues to the owner of the unlisted entity (i) a number of shares of the listed company's common stock that would not require shareholder approval under Section 713(b) or give rise to a change of control and (ii) additional consideration in the form of contingently convertible securities that will become convertible into common stock upon subsequent receipt of approval of the listed company's shareholders. The owners of the unlisted entity obtain control of the post-merger entity only upon the later conversion of the contingently convertible securities into common stock. The Exchange notes that the definition of “Reverse Merger” for purposes of Section 341 and the requirements of the rule only apply when the change of control occurs. As such, under Section 341 as currently drafted, a listed issuer may consummate the merger in a multi-step reverse merger transaction even if the combined entity would not meet the Exchange's initial listing standards. In such a case, the Exchange would have no choice but to permit the consummation of the merger and then delist the company in the event that the shareholders approve the conversion of the contingently convertible securities and the combined entity proceeds with conversion and does not meet the initial listing standards at the time of that conversion. In some cases, a company may refrain from converting the contingently convertible securities in order to avoid delisting, leaving the company in the unusual position of having completed a merger without effectuating the change of control that was anticipated when the merger agreement was reached.
The Exchange wishes to address the effect under Section 341 of structuring a Reverse Merger using the multi-step reverse merger structure. The Exchange proposes to amend Section 341 to define a Multi-Step Reverse Merger for purposes of that rule as a transaction in which a listed issuer engages in a Reverse Merger through a series of transactions, where the listed issuer enters into an agreement with an unlisted entity that provides for an initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer, along with the anticipated future issuance of additional shares of the listed issuer upon conversion, exchange or exercise of securities of another type of the listed issuer when the future issuance of the shares would result in a change of control of the listed issuer. The Exchange proposes to amend Section 341 to provide that in a Multi-Step Reverse Merger, the listed issuer will be eligible for continued listing on the Exchange only if, at the time of the initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer, the contemplated post-transaction entity meets initial listing standards. The revised rule will specify that, in determining the post-transaction entity's compliance with initial listing standards in a Multi-Step Reverse Merger, the Exchange will assume the issuance of all shares anticipated to be issued upon conversion, exchange or exercise of securities as part of the Multi-Step Reverse Merger.
Section 341 provides that the Exchange should be consulted whenever a listed issuer is contemplating a transaction or series of transactions that could constitute a Reverse Merger. If the Exchange determines that a transaction or series of transactions constitute a Reverse Merger, the listed issuer must submit an initial listing application for the post-transaction entity with sufficient time to allow the Exchange to complete its review before the effective date of the Reverse Merger. The proposed amended form of Section 341 will provide that the listed issuer must submit the required initial listing application prior to the Reverse Merger or the initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer in the Multi-Step Reverse Merger, as the case may be.
In its current form, Section 341 states that “in determining whether a change of control constitutes a Reverse Merger, the Exchange will consider all relevant factors, including, but not limited to, changes in the management, board of directors, voting power, ownership, and financial structure of the listed issuer.” The Exchange proposes to clarify this statement by modifying it to state that the Exchange will undertake this analysis of all relevant factors “in considering whether a change of control has occurred in the context of a Reverse Merger.”
Section 341 contains a sentence providing that if the initial listing application has not been approved prior to the effective date of the Reverse Merger, the Exchange will issue a Staff Determination Letter as set forth in Section 1202 and begin delisting proceedings pursuant to Part 12. The Exchange proposes to amend this sentence to state that if the initial listing application has not been approved prior to the effective date of the Reverse Merger or the initial issuance of shares of the listed issuer in the Multi-Step Reverse Merger, as the case may be, the Exchange will issue a Staff Determination Letter and begin delisting proceedings.
The Exchange believes the proposed amendment to Section 341 is appropriate as it would prevent a listed company from entering into a Multi-Step Reverse Merger where the ownership structure upon completion of all of the intended steps could result in a Reverse Merger that would require the listed company to be delisted for failing to meet initial listing standards. As such, the proposed amendment is consistent with the purpose of Section 341 in its current form, which is to prevent entities that do not qualify for initial listing from achieving listing status by undertaking a Reverse Merger with a listed issuer.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
4
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
5
]
in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove
(
printed page 73837)
impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange believes the proposed amendment to Section 341 is appropriate as it would prevent a listed issuer from entering into a Multi-Step Reverse Merger where the ownership structure upon completion of all of the intended steps could result in a Reverse Merger that would require the listed issuer to be delisted. As such, the proposed amendment is consistent with the purpose of Section 341 in its current form, which is to prevent entities that do not qualify for initial listing from achieving listing status by undertaking a Reverse Merger with a listed issuer.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule amendment will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule amendment would be applied in a nondiscriminatory manner to all listed companies that seek to consummate a transaction. In addition, any company wishing to undertake a Multi-Step Reverse Merger could seek to list on another national securities exchange that does not have a similar rule.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Within 45 days of the date of publication of this notice in the
Federal Register
or within such longer period up to 90 days (i) as the Commission may designate if it finds such longer period to be appropriate and publishes its reasons for so finding or (ii) as to which the self-regulatory organization consents, the Commission will:
(A) by order approve or disapprove the proposed rule change, or
(B) institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-100  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-100. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-100 and should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
5
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

3.
    
                         For the purposes of Section 341, a “Reverse Merger” is a transaction or series of transactions whereby a listed issuer combines with, or into, an entity not listed on the Exchange, resulting in a change of control of the listed issuer and potentially allowing such unlisted entity to obtain an Exchange listing. In determining whether a change of control constitutes a Reverse Merger, the Exchange will consider all relevant factors, including, but not limited to, changes in the management, board of directors, voting power, ownership, and financial structure of the listed issuer. The Exchange will also consider the nature of the businesses and the relative size of both the listed issuer and the unlisted entity.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106889; File No. SR-SAPPHIRE-2026-38]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 30, 2026, MIAX Sapphire, LLC (“MIAX Sapphire” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) a proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the MIAX Sapphire Options Exchange Fee Schedule (“Fee Schedule”) to clarify that the Exchange will exclude options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://www.miaxglobal.com/​markets/​us-options/​miax-sapphire/​rule-filings
,
and at the Exchange's principal office.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month.
Exchange Rule 501 describes the Exchange's hours of operation. In particular, the hours during which option transactions may be made on the Exchange shall be from 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time except for option contracts on Exchange Traded Fund Shares, as defined in Rule 402(i), and Index-Linked Securities, as
(
printed page 73866)
defined in Rule 402(k)(1), which may remain open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time, as designated by the Exchange. The Exchange does not offer options trading outside of the hours described in Exchange Rule 501.
Currently, the Exchange assesses monthly Trading Permit
[
3
]
fees and MEO Port fees to Market Makers based on the lesser of either the per class basis or percentage of total national average daily volume measurement.
[
4
]
The amount of monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and MEO Port fee is based upon the number of classes in which the Market Maker was assigned to quote on any given day within the calendar month, or upon the class volume percentages set forth in the tables in Sections 3)b) and 5)d)ii) of the Fee Schedule.
[
5
]
The Exchange assesses Market Makers the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and MEO Port fee based on the greatest number of classes listed on MIAX Sapphire that the Market Maker was assigned to quote in on any given day within a calendar month.
[
6
]
The class volume percentage is based on the total national average daily volume in classes listed on MIAX Sapphire in the prior calendar quarter.
[
7
]
Newly listed option classes are excluded from the calculation of the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and MEO Port fee until the calendar quarter following their listing, at which time the newly listed option classes will be included in both the per class count and the percentage of total national average daily volume.
[
8
]
The Exchange notes that the Exchange's transactional fees and rebates currently are base rates with no tiers. The Exchange may, in the future, amend transactional fees and rebates to be determined by volume in a particular segment, which may be calculated as a percentage of total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types.
[
9
]
The Exchange's affiliated options markets calculate certain of their transaction fees and rebates using various volume calculations in certain segments;
[
10
]
however, the Exchange does not do so at this time. If the Exchange decides to amend transactional fees and rebates to establish tiers utilizing volume calculations in particular segments, it will file a separate Rule 19b-4 filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) to amend the Fee Schedule.
On May 28, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe”) received approval from the Commission to amend the Cboe rules to provide for extended trading sessions for multi-listed equity options that meet certain eligibility criteria.
[
11
]
Pursuant to the Cboe Approval Order, Cboe may offer an extended morning trading session (from 7:30 a.m. to 9:25 a.m. Eastern Time) and an extended afternoon session (from 4:00 p.m. to 4:15 p.m.) for equity options that are not exchange-traded product options that already trade until 4:15 p.m.
[
12
]
Cboe launched the extended trading sessions on October 19, 2026, with the initial listings of select multi-listed equity and exchange-traded fund options.
[
13
]
Other exchanges have filed rule proposals with the Commission to offer the same extended trading sessions for multi-listed equity options, which proposals were also approved by the Commission.
[
14
]
The Exchange now proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to add a section titled “Notes” before Section 1 of the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. In particular, the Exchange proposes to exclude the following from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month: (1) total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types in multiply-listed equity options classes that occur outside of the hours of 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time; and (2) total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types in option classes in Exchange Traded Fund Shares (as defined in Rule 402(i)) and Index-Linked Securities (as defined in Rule 402(k)(1)) that occur outside of the hours of 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time, except for options on such Exchange Traded Fund Shares or Index-Linked Securities which have been designated by the Exchange as remaining open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time. The Exchange further proposes to clarify that the exclusions noted above are separate from volume the Exchange excludes in the event that it experiences an Exchange System Disruption,
[
15
]
as described in the Fee Schedule.
The purpose of the proposed change is to add clarity to the Fee Schedule. The Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions at this time. The Exchange proposes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. If the Exchange were to not exclude multi-listed equity options volume executed during other exchanges' extended trading sessions, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's
(
printed page 73867)
various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations.
Implementation Date
The proposed rule change is effective beginning November 1, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act,
[
16
]
in general, and with Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
17
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed change to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month is reasonable, equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory. This is because the change will provide greater clarity to Members regarding volume in multi-list equity options that the Exchange will exclude from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts. The Exchange believes it is reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory to ensure that the Fee Schedule is clear and concise to all market participants.
The Exchange believes it is reasonable to exclude volume executed during the extended trading sessions of other exchanges because, if the Exchange were to not exclude such volume, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed each month. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange believes its proposal is reasonable.
Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply to all Members uniformly, in that each Member's volume for purposes of pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives would continue to be calculated in a uniform manner and would now exclude multi-list equity options volume executed during extended trading sessions.
For the reasons discussed above, the Exchange submits that the proposal satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
18
]
in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as described above, the proposed rule change is designed to provide greater clarity regarding volume that the exchange will exclude in its volume calculations to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month.
Inter-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe the proposal would impose any burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, as the Exchange believes the proposal is not concerned with competitive issues, but rather relates to calculation methodologies applicable to its pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives.
Intra-Market Competition
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposal would not impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because, as described above, the proposed change will apply to all Members uniformly and in the same manner.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others

III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106888; File No. SR-EMERALD-2026-24]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act” or “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 30, 2026, MIAX Emerald, LLC (“MIAX Emerald” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the MIAX Emerald Options Exchange Fee Schedule (“Fee Schedule”) to clarify that the Exchange will exclude options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. The Exchange also proposes to amend the last paragraph in the Definitions section of the Fee Schedule to add the name of the Exchange's other affiliate.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://www.miaxglobal.com/​markets/​us-options/​emerald-options/​rule-filings
, and at the Exchange's principal office.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. The Exchange also proposes to amend the last paragraph in the Definitions section of the Fee Schedule to add the name of the Exchange's other affiliate, MIAX Sapphire, LLC (“MIAX Sapphire”).
Exchange Rule 501 describes the Exchange's hours of operation. In particular, the hours during which option transactions may be made on the Exchange shall be from 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time except for option contracts on Exchange Traded Fund Shares, as defined in Rule 402(j), and Index-Linked Securities, as defined in Rule 402(k)(1), which may remain open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time, as designated by the Exchange. The Exchange does not offer options trading outside of the hours described in Exchange Rule 501.
Currently, certain of the Exchange's transactional and non-transactional fees, rebates and tiers are determined by volume in a particular segment calculated as a percentage of total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types. For example, the Exchanges calculates transaction fees (or rebates) to Priority Customers,
[
3
]
Market Makers,
[
4
]
and professional origins (
i.e.,
referred to in the Fee Schedule under the origin Non-Priority Customer, Firm Proprietary/Broker-Dealer, and Non-MIAX Emerald Market Makers)
[
5
]
based on the total monthly sides executed by the Member
[
6
]
in all options classes on MIAX Emerald in the relevant origin type and/or applicable liquidity, not including Excluded Contracts,
[
7
]
(as the numerator) expressed as a percentage of (divided by) CTCV
[
8
]
(as the denominator).
Additionally, the Exchange assesses monthly Trading Permit
[
9
]
fees and MEI Port fees to Market Makers based on the lesser of either the per class basis or percentage of total national average daily volume measurement.
[
10
]
The amount of the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and MEI Port fee is based upon the number of classes in which the Market Maker was assigned to quote on any given day within the calendar month, or upon the class volume percentages set forth in the tables in Sections 3)b) and 5)d)ii) of the Fee Schedule.
[
11
]
The Exchange assesses MIAX Emerald Market Makers the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and MEI Port fee based on the greatest number of classes listed on MIAX Emerald that the MIAX Emerald Market Maker was assigned to quote in on any given day within a calendar
(
printed page 73830)
month.
[
12
]
The class volume percentage is based on the total national average daily volume in classes listed on MIAX Emerald in the prior calendar quarter.
[
13
]
Newly listed option classes are excluded from the calculation of the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and MEI Port fee until the calendar quarter following their listing, at which time the newly listed option classes will be included in both the per class count and the percentage of total national average daily volume.
[
14
]
The Exchange notes there are other examples in the Fee Schedule where fees or rebates are determined by certain volume calculations in particular segments calculated as a percentage of national volume in each segment.
On May 28, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe”) received approval from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) to amend the Cboe rules to provide for extended trading sessions for multi-listed equity options that meet certain eligibility criteria.
[
15
]
Pursuant to the Cboe Approval Order, Cboe may offer an extended morning trading session (from 7:30 a.m. to 9:25 a.m. Eastern Time) and an extended afternoon session (from 4:00 p.m. to 4:15 p.m.) for equity options that are not exchange-traded product options that already trade until 4:15 p.m.
[
16
]
Cboe launched the extended trading sessions on October 19, 2026, with the initial listings of select multi-listed equity and exchange-traded fund options.
[
17
]
Other exchanges have filed rule proposals with the Commission to offer the same extended trading sessions for multi-listed equity options, which proposals were also approved by the Commission.
[
18
]
The Exchange now proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to add a section titled “Notes” before Section 1 of the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. In particular, the Exchange proposes to exclude the following from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month: (1) total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types in multiply-listed equity options classes that occur outside of the hours of 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time; and (2) total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types in option classes in Exchange Traded Fund Shares (as defined in Rule 402(j)) and Index-Linked Securities (as defined in Rule 402(k)(1)) that occur outside of the hours of 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time, except for options on such Exchange Traded Fund Shares or Index-Linked Securities which have been designated by the Exchange as remaining open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time. The Exchange further proposes to clarify that the exclusions noted above are separate from volume the Exchange excludes in the event that it experiences an Exchange System Disruption,
[
19
]
as described in the Fee Schedule.
The purpose of the proposed changes is to add clarity to the Fee Schedule. The Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions at this time. The Exchange proposes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. If the Exchange were to not exclude multi-listed equity options volume executed during other exchanges' extended trading sessions, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations.
The Exchange also proposes to amend the last paragraph in the Definitions section of the Fee Schedule to add the name of the Exchange's other affiliate. Currently, the last paragraph provides as follows:
Except as otherwise provided in this Fee Schedule as described below, all fees set forth in this Fee Schedule are specific to and assessed exclusively for use of MIAX Emerald and do not include access to and/or use of MIAX
[
20
]
or MIAX Pearl.
[
21
]
Since this language was originally established, the Exchange's affiliate, MIAX Sapphire launched operations. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to amend this paragraph to insert MIAX Sapphire. The purpose of this change is to provide consistency and clarity in the Fee Schedule and to align the Fee Schedule with that of the Exchange's affiliates, MIAX, MIAX Pearl, and MIAX Sapphire, to specify that the fees described in the Fee Schedule apply exclusively to the Exchange, within limited exceptions noted.
Implementation Date
The proposed rule changes are effective beginning November 1, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act,
[
22
]
in general, and with Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
23
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from
(
printed page 73831)
its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month is reasonable, equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory. This is because the changes will provide greater clarity to Members regarding volume in multi-list equity options that the Exchange will exclude from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts. The Exchange believes it is reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory to ensure that the Fee Schedule is clear and concise to all market participants.
The Exchange believes it is reasonable to exclude volume executed during the extended trading sessions of other exchanges because, if the Exchange were to not exclude such volume, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed each month. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange believes its proposal is reasonable.
Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply to all Members uniformly, in that each Member's volume for purposes of pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives would continue to be calculated in a uniform manner and would now exclude multi-list equity options volume executed during extended trading sessions.
The Exchange believes its proposal to add clarifying text at the end of the newly proposed Notes section to specify how the fees described in the Fee Schedule are exclusive to MIAX Emerald, with limited exceptions, is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory. This is because the proposed change is to align with text in the fee schedules of the Exchange's affiliates and to provide consistency and clarity in the Fee Schedule.
For the reasons discussed above, the Exchange submits that the proposal satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
24
]
in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as described above, the proposed rule change is designed to provide greater clarity regarding volume that the exchange will exclude in its volume calculations to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month.
Inter-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe the proposal would impose any burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, as the Exchange believes the proposal is not concerned with competitive issues, but rather relates to calculation methodologies applicable to its pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives. The Exchange's proposal to add clarifying text at the end of the newly proposed Notes section to specify how the fees described in the Fee Schedule are exclusive to MIAX Emerald, with limited exceptions, also does not raise any competitive issues and is solely to provide clarity in the Fee Schedule.
Intra-Market Competition
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposal would not impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because, as described above, the proposed changes will apply to all Members uniformly and in the same manner.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act,
[
25
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
26
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-EMERALD-2026-24 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-EMERALD-2026-24. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-EMERALD-2026-24 and
(
printed page 73832)
should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.

]

Assistant Secretary.

A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. The Exchange also proposes to amend the last paragraph in the Definitions section of the Fee Schedule to add the names of the Exchange's other affiliates, MIAX Emerald, LLC (“MIAX Emerald”), and MIAX Sapphire, LLC (“MIAX Sapphire”).
Exchange Rule 501 describes the Exchange's hours of operation. In particular, the hours during which option transactions may be made on the Exchange shall be from 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time
(
printed page 73869)
except for option contracts on Exchange Traded Fund Shares, as defined in Rule 402(i), and Index-Linked Securities, as defined in Rule 402(k)(1), which may remain open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time, as designated by the Exchange. The Exchange does not offer options trading outside of the hours described in Exchange Rule 501.
Currently, certain of the Exchange's transactional and non-transactional fees, rebates and tiers are determined by volume in a particular segment calculated as a percentage of total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types. For example, the Exchanges calculates transaction fees (or rebates) to Priority Customers,
[
3
]
Market Makers,
[
4
]
and professional origins (
i.e.,
referred to in the Fee Schedule under the origin Non-Priority Customer, Firm, BD, and Non-MIAX Pearl Market Makers)
[
5
]
based on the total monthly volume executed by the Member
[
6
]
in all options classes on MIAX Pearl in the relevant origin type, not including Excluded Contracts,
[
7
]
(as the numerator) expressed as a percentage of (divided by) TCV
[
8
]
(as the denominator).
Additionally, the Exchange assesses monthly Trading Permit
[
9
]
and Full Service MEO Port fees to Market Makers based on the lesser of either the per class basis or percentage of total national average daily volume measurement.
[
10
]
The amount of monthly Market Maker Trading Permit fee and Full Service MEO Port fees is based upon the number of classes in which the Market Maker was assigned to quote on any given day within the calendar month, or upon the class volume percentages set forth in the tables in Sections 3)b) and 5)d) of the Fee Schedule.
[
11
]
The Exchange assesses Market Makers the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit Fee based on the greatest number of classes listed on MIAX Pearl that the Market Maker was assigned to quote in on any given day within a calendar month.
[
12
]
The class volume percentage is based on the total national average daily volume in classes listed on MIAX Pearl in the prior calendar quarter.
[
13
]
Newly listed option classes are excluded from the calculation of the monthly Market Maker Trading Permit Fee until the calendar quarter following their listing, at which time the newly listed option classes will be included in both the per class count and the percentage of total national average daily volume.
[
14
]
The Exchange notes there are other examples in the Fee Schedule where fees or rebates are determined by certain volume calculations in particular segments calculated as a percentage of national volume in each segment. For example, the Exchange also calculates certain alternative thresholds in certain classes like SPY, QQQ, and IWM to reach certain Market Maker tiers.
On May 28, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe”) received approval from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) to amend the Cboe rules to provide for extended trading sessions for multi-listed equity options that meet certain eligibility criteria.
[
15
]
Pursuant to the Cboe Approval Order, Cboe may offer an extended morning trading session (from 7:30 a.m. to 9:25 a.m. Eastern Time) and an extended afternoon session (from 4:00 p.m. to 4:15 p.m.) for equity options that are not exchange-traded product options that already trade until 4:15 p.m.
[
16
]
Cboe launched the extended trading sessions on October 19, 2026, with the initial listings of select multi-listed equity and exchange-traded fund options.
[
17
]
Other exchanges have filed rule proposals with the Commission to offer the same extended trading sessions for multi-listed equity options, which proposals were also approved by the Commission.
[
18
]
The Exchange now proposes to amend the Fee Schedule to add a section titled “Notes” before Section 1 of the Fee Schedule to clarify that the Exchange will exclude multi-listed options volume executed during extended trading hours from the Exchange's volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. In particular, the Exchange proposes to exclude the following from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month: (1) total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types in multiply-listed equity options classes that occur outside of the hours of 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time; and (2) total national volume cleared at the Options Clearing Corporation in the relevant account types in option classes in Exchange Traded Fund Shares (as defined in Rule 402(i)) and Index-Linked Securities (as defined in Rule 402(k)(1)) that occur outside of the hours of 9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time, except for options on such Exchange Traded Fund Shares or Index-Linked Securities which have been designated by the Exchange as remaining open for trading beyond 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time but in no case later than 4:15 p.m. Eastern Time. The Exchange further proposes to clarify that the exclusions noted above are separate from volume the Exchange excludes in the event that it experiences a System outage, as described in the Fee Schedule.
The purpose of the proposed changes is to add clarity to the Fee Schedule. The Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions at this time. The Exchange proposes to exclude volume
(
printed page 73870)
in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month. If the Exchange were to not exclude multi-listed equity options volume executed during other exchanges' extended trading sessions, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations.
The Exchange also proposes to amend the last paragraph in the Definitions section of the Fee Schedule to add the names of the Exchange's other affiliates. Currently, the last paragraph provides as follows:
Except as otherwise provided in this Fee Schedule with regard to network connectivity, including network testing and certification, all fees set forth in this Fee Schedule are specific to and assessed exclusively for use of MIAX Pearl and do not include access to and/or use of MIAX or any other facilities of the Exchange.
Since this language was originally established, the Exchange's affiliates, MIAX Emerald and MIAX Sapphire launched operations. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to amend this paragraph to insert MIAX Emerald and MIAX Sapphire. The purpose of this change is to provide consistency and clarity in the Fee Schedule and to align the Fee Schedule with that of the Exchange's affiliates, MIAX Pearl, MIAX Emerald and MIAX Sapphire, to specify that the fees described in the Fee Schedule apply exclusively to the Exchange, within limited exceptions noted.
Implementation Date
The proposed rule changes are effective beginning November 1, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposal is consistent with the provisions of Section 6 of the Act,
[
19
]
in general, and with Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
20
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes to exclude volume in multi-listed equity options executed during extended trading sessions from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month is reasonable, equitably allocated and not unfairly discriminatory. This is because the changes will provide greater clarity to Members regarding volume in multi-list equity options that the Exchange will exclude from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts. The Exchange believes it is reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory to ensure that the Fee Schedule is clear and concise to all market participants.
The Exchange believes it is reasonable to exclude volume executed during the extended trading sessions of other exchanges because, if the Exchange were to not exclude such volume, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed each month. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange believes its proposal is reasonable.
Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply to all Members uniformly, in that each Member's volume for purposes of pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives would continue to be calculated in a uniform manner and would now exclude multi-list equity options volume executed during extended trading sessions.
The Exchange believes its proposal to add clarifying text at the end of the newly proposed Notes section to specify how the fees described in the Fee Schedule are exclusive to MIAX Pearl, with limited exceptions, is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory. This is because the proposed change is to align with text in the fee schedules of the Exchange's affiliates and to provide consistency and clarity in the Fee Schedule.
For the reasons discussed above, the Exchange submits that the proposal satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
21
]
in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as described above, the proposed rule change is designed to provide greater clarity regarding volume that the exchange will exclude in its volume calculations to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month.
Inter-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe the proposal would impose any burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, as the Exchange believes the proposal is not concerned with competitive issues, but rather relates to calculation methodologies applicable to its pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives. The Exchange's proposal to add clarifying text at the end of the newly proposed Notes section to specify how the fees described in the Fee Schedule are exclusive to MIAX Pearl, with limited exceptions, also does not raise any competitive issues and is
(
printed page 73871)
solely to provide clarity in the Fee Schedule.
Intra-Market Competition
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposal would not impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because, as described above, the proposed changes will apply to all Members uniformly and in the same manner.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act,
[
22
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
23
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-PEARL-2026-44  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-PEARL-2026-44. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-PEARL-2026-44 and should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
24
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.
