This is because the changes will provide greater clarity to Members regarding volume in multi-list equity options that the Exchange will exclude from its volume calculations that determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts. The Exchange believes it is reasonable and not unfairly discriminatory to ensure that the Fee Schedule is clear and concise to all market participants.
The Exchange believes it is reasonable to exclude volume executed during the extended trading sessions of other exchanges because, if the Exchange were to not exclude such volume, then the volume calculations used by the Exchange to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month are likely to be skewed each month. This is because the extended trading sessions would increase the denominator used by the Exchange for its relevant volume calculations across various segments without the corresponding available increase in volume used in the numerator since the Exchange does not offer extended trading sessions. This has the potential to negatively impact market participants who may receive lower fees or higher rebates working through the Exchange's various tiers, which are based on increasing volume in each segment. Accordingly, the Exchange believes its proposal is reasonable.
Additionally, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will apply to all Members uniformly, in that each Member's volume for purposes of pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives would continue to be calculated in a uniform manner and would now exclude multi-list equity options volume executed during extended trading sessions.
The Exchange believes its proposal to add clarifying text at the end of the newly proposed Notes section to specify how the fees described in the Fee Schedule are exclusive to MIAX, with limited exceptions, is reasonable, equitable and not unfairly discriminatory. This is because the proposed change is to align with text in the fee schedules of the Exchange's affiliates and to provide consistency and clarity in the Fee Schedule.
For the reasons discussed above, the Exchange submits that the proposal satisfies the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
24
]
in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities and is not designed to unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. Rather, as described above, the proposed rule change is designed to provide greater clarity regarding volume that the exchange will exclude in its volume calculations to determine applicable thresholds and tiers for transactions and non-transactional fees, rebates, and discounts each month.
Inter-Market Competition
The Exchange does not believe the proposal would impose any burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, as the Exchange believes the proposal is not concerned with competitive issues, but rather relates to calculation methodologies applicable to its pricing tiers, non-transaction fees and other incentives. The Exchange's proposal to
(
printed page 73863)
add clarifying text at the end of the newly proposed Notes section to specify how the fees described in the Fee Schedule are exclusive to MIAX, with limited exceptions, also does not raise any competitive issues and is solely to provide clarity in the Fee Schedule.
Intra-Market Competition
Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposal would not impose any burden on intra-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because, as described above, the proposed changes will apply to all Members uniformly and in the same manner.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act,
[
25
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(2)
[
26
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments

https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-MIAX-2026-43 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-MIAX-2026-43. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. [Release No. 34-106885; File No. SR-ISE-2026-59]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 2, 2026, Nasdaq ISE, LLC (“ISE” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the Exchange's Rules at Options 7, Section 6 (Other Options Fees and Rebates).
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​ise/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend its Pricing Schedule at Options 7, Section 6 (Other Options Fees and Rebates).
Currently, the Exchange offers a PIM
[
3
]
rebate of $0.105 per contract to Electronic Access Members
[
4
]
that utilize PIM to execute more than 0.75% of Priority Customer volume in Regular Orders,
[
5
]
calculated as a percentage of Customer Total Consolidated Volume per day in a given month.
[
6
]
As used in the Pricing Schedule, “Priority Customer” includes “Retail,” as defined in Options 7, Section 1(c), and Customer Total Consolidated Volume means the total national volume cleared at The Options Clearing Corporation in the Customer range in equity and ETF
(
printed page 73864)
options in that month. The rebate is paid for Priority Customer Regular Orders under 250 contracts that are submitted to PIM.
[
7
]
The Exchange proposes to modify the amount of this rebate, from $0.105 per contract, to $0.10 per contract. The Exchange is not otherwise modifying the eligibility, calculation, payment, aggregation, or exclusion provisions applicable to this rebate. The Exchange believes the revised rebate will continue to encourage qualifying Electronic Access Members to submit smaller-sized Priority Customer Regular Orders to PIM for price improvement while allowing the Exchange to periodically adjust its incentive programs.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
8
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
9
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Commission and the courts have repeatedly expressed their preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, while adopting a series of steps to improve the current market model, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
10
]
Likewise, in
NetCoalition
v.
Securities and Exchange Commission
[
11
]
(“NetCoalition”) the D.C. Circuit upheld the Commission's use of a market-based approach in evaluating the fairness of market data fees against a challenge claiming that Congress mandated a cost-based approach.
[
12
]
As the court emphasized, the Commission “intended in Regulation NMS that `market forces, rather than regulatory requirements' play a role in determining the market data . . .  to be made available to investors and at what cost.”
[
13
]
Further, “[n]o one disputes that competition for order flow is `fierce.' . . . As the SEC explained, `[i]n the U.S. national market system, buyers and sellers of securities, and the broker-dealers that act as their order-routing agents, have a wide range of choices of where to route orders for execution'; [and] `no exchange can afford to take its market share percentages for granted' because `no exchange possesses a monopoly, regulatory or otherwise, in the execution of order flow from broker dealers'. . . .”
[
14
]
Although the court and the SEC were discussing the cash equities markets, the Exchange believes that these views apply with equal force to the options markets.
The Exchange believes that its proposal to reduce the PIM rebate in Options 7, Section 6.C from $0.105 per contract to $0.10 per contract is reasonable. The Exchange has limited resources to allocate to its incentive programs and periodically assesses its fee structure to ensure that its rebates continue to attract order flow while remaining sustainable. The proposed rebate of $0.10 per contract represents only a modest reduction from the current $0.105 per contract level, and the Exchange believes that this rebate remains attractive and will continue to incentivize qualifying Electronic Access Members to submit smaller-sized Priority Customer Regular Orders to PIM for price improvement, which benefits all market participants.
The Exchange believes that its proposal to reduce the PIM rebate is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the modified rebate will apply uniformly to all Electronic Access Members that satisfy the objective volume qualification (utilizing PIM to execute more than 0.75% of Priority Customer volume in Regular Orders, calculated as a percentage of Customer Total Consolidated Volume per day in a given month) with respect to all Priority Customer Regular Orders under 250 contracts submitted to PIM. Any Electronic Access Member is able to qualify for the rebate by meeting the applicable volume threshold, and all qualifying Members will receive the same $0.10 per contract rebate on such orders. Any Electronic Access Member may participate in PIM, and Market Makers may respond to a PIM. While the rebate is targeted at Priority Customer Regular Orders, this does not render the proposal unfairly discriminatory because Priority Customers pay no Fees for PIM Orders and Priority Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers, and increased Market Maker activity facilitates tighter spreads that may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Inter-Market Competition
The proposal does not impose an undue burden on inter-market competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange believes its proposal remains competitive with other options markets and will offer market participants another choice of where to transact options. The Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily favor competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive, or rebate opportunities available at other venues to be more favorable. In such an environment, the Exchange must continually adjust its fees to remain competitive with other exchanges. Because competitors are free to modify their own fees in response, and because market participants may readily adjust their order routing practices, the Exchange believes that the degree to which fee changes in this market may impose any burden on competition is extremely limited. In sum, if the proposed rebate level is unattractive to market participants, it is likely that the Exchange will lose market share as a result. Accordingly, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed change will impair the ability of Members or competing order execution venues to maintain their competitive standing in the financial markets.
Intra-Market Competition
The Exchange's proposal to reduce the PIM rebate in Options 7, Section 6.C from $0.105 per contract to $0.10 per contract will not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition.
(
printed page 73865)
The modified rebate will apply uniformly to all Electronic Access Members that satisfy the same objective volume qualification, with respect to all Priority Customer Regular Orders under 250 contracts submitted to PIM. Any Electronic Access Member is able to qualify for the rebate by meeting the applicable volume threshold. Any Electronic Access Member may participate in PIM, and Market Makers may respond to a PIM. While the rebate is targeted at Priority Customer Regular Orders, this does not impose an undue burden on intra-market competition because Priority Customers pay no Fees for PIM Orders and Priority Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which attracts Market Makers, and increased Market Maker activity facilitates tighter spreads that may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from other market participants.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
15
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-ISE-2026-59  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-ISE-2026-59. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-ISE-2026-59 and should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
16
]

Assistant Secretary.

November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[

[

]
notice is hereby given that on November 2, 2026, Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “C2”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe C2 Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “C2”) proposes to amend its Fees Schedule to clarify that Fee Codes BC, BM, BN and BO apply to the Russell 2000 Index (“RUT”). The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​options/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​ctwo/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
(
printed page 73828)
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule, effective November 2, 2026, to clarify that fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO apply to options on the Russell 2000 Index (“RUT”).
Currently, fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the “Fee Codes and Associated Fees” table do not expressly reference RUT. The Exchange proposes to amend the Fees Schedule to add RUT to fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the “Fee Codes and Associated Fees” table to clarify that these are the fees specifically charged for RUT. The Exchange notes that these fee codes (BC, BM, BN and BO) are already used in a prior table that expressly calls out the applicable fees for executions in RUT. This proposed change is only intended to provide clarity in the second instance where these fee codes are used within the Fee Schedule. The proposed change does not make any substantive changes to the amount of any fee or rebate set forth in the Fees Schedule, nor does it change how any fee or rebate is assessed. Rather, the proposed change is non-substantive and clarifying in nature and is intended to make the Fees Schedule more accurate and transparent.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”) and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
3
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
4
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination. The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
5
]
which requires that Exchange rules provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Trading Permit Holders and other persons using its facilities.
The Exchange believes the proposed amendment to add RUT to fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the “Fee Codes and Associated Fees” table of the Fees Schedule is reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory, and promotes just and equitable principles of trade, because it is a clarifying change that makes no substantive change to any fee amount. The proposed change will provide greater clarity and transparency in the Fees Schedule regarding the fee codes applicable to RUT transactions, thereby reducing potential confusion among market participants, which removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protects investors and the public interest. The proposed change applies equally to all Trading Permit Holders.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe the proposed change will impose any burden on intramarket competition. The proposed change is a clarifying, non-substantive change that adds “RUT” to the description for fee codes BC, BM, BN and BO in the Fees Schedule, does not change any fee amount, and applies equally to all Trading Permit Holders.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106883; File No. SR-OCC-2026-013]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Exchange Act” or “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, The Options Clearing Corporation (“OCC” or “Corporation”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared primarily by OCC. OCC filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
3
]
of the Act and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4
[
4
]
thereunder, such that the proposed rule change was immediately effective upon filing with the Commission. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
This proposed rule change would update OCC's cash settlement process to provide Clearing Members with the ability to satisfy daily margin deficit amounts with non-cash collateral prior to the daily Settlement Time.
The proposed changes to OCC's Rules are contained in Exhibit 5 to SR-OCC-2026-013. Material proposed to be added is marked by underlining and material proposed to be deleted is marked with strikethrough text. All terms with initial capitalization that are
(
printed page 73848)
not otherwise defined herein have the same meaning as set forth in the OCC By-Laws and Rules.
[
5
]
II. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, OCC included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. OCC has prepared summaries, set forth in sections (A), (B), and (C) below, of the most significant aspects of these statements.
(A) Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
OCC conducts a daily cash settlement process in which OCC drafts cash from Clearing Member bank accounts to offset any deficit in margin assets pledged by the Clearing Member as compared to the total required margin as of Settlement Time.
[
6
]
Currently, prior to Settlement Time (8:00 a.m. CT), OCC makes a Daily Margin Report available to each Clearing Member showing, among other things, the Clearing Member's margin requirements and margin previously deposited by the Clearing Member, as well as any surplus over the margin amount required or margin deficit to be satisfied. For all Clearing Members who are reported to have a margin deficit, OCC authorizes cash withdrawals from the Clearing Members' bank accounts in order to satisfy the deficit. Clearing Members currently do not have the opportunity to deposit additional collateral after receipt of the Daily Margin Report to offset any start-of-day margin deficit identified on the report before OCC drafts cash from the Clearing Members' bank accounts.
OCC proposes to replace the Daily Margin Report with a Daily Account Summary.
[
7
]
OCC proposes to offer Clearing Members an opportunity, after receiving the Daily Account Summary and prior to Settlement Time, to deposit collateral in order to reduce or eliminate their Start-of-Day Margin Deficit. Any such collateral deposit would correspondingly reduce or eliminate the necessary cash withdrawal from the Clearing Member's bank account. OCC's Rules already provide Clearing Members a similar opportunity to offset deficits in their Clearing Fund allocations prior to OCC withdrawing cash from Clearing Member bank accounts, as described in Rule 1005.
[
8
]
OCC seeks to give Clearing Members this ability with respect to margin deficits.
1. Purpose
OCC proposes to change its Rules to provide Clearing Members with an opportunity to reduce or eliminate any margin deficit identified in the Daily Account Summary to avoid OCC's cash draw prior to Settlement Time.
This change is expected to have positive effects on both OCC and Clearing Members. The current start-of-day margin cash settlement process often requires multiple inefficient transfers of collateral and cash during the trading day, resulting in temporary double-collateralization for Clearing Members. Presently, after OCC drafts cash from a Clearing Member's bank account prior to Settlement Time to satisfy a start-of-day-margin deficit, the Clearing Member often deposits non-cash collateral with OCC and requests that OCC return some or all of the cash back to the Clearing Member's bank account. OCC allows this intraday deposit of margin and returns the cash, but the process is inefficient for all parties. Under the current process, OCC must often make multiple cash transactions, drafting cash from Clearing Member accounts and then returning the cash to the Clearing Member on the same day. And because the cash transfer is not instantaneous, this series of events leaves Clearing Members double-collateralized for a period. Clearing Members may not receive their returned cash until hours after they deposited additional collateral, meaning that they are double-collateralized (through the newly deposited collateral and the cash that has not yet been returned) from the time when they deposit additional collateral until the previously drafted cash is returned to their bank accounts.
This process increases cash liquidity demands on Clearing Members, causes Clearing Members to hold excess collateral to attempt to avoid daily deficit cash drafts, and increases instances of same-day double-collateralization. For OCC, this process increases transactional cash flows, causing unnecessary inefficiency and increased operational risk. These issues could be alleviated or eliminated if Clearing Members had the opportunity to deposit collateral to satisfy any identified margin deficit before OCC withdraws cash to satisfy the deficit. And regardless of whether a Clearing Member chooses to deposit additional margin, the ultimate Start-of-Day Margin Deficit and the corresponding deficit cash draft would be no greater than the deficit originally identified in the Daily Account Summary.
A hypothetical example may demonstrate how the updated daily settlement process would work in practice. If OCC were to report on a Clearing Member's Daily Account Summary that the Clearing Member faced a margin deficit, the Clearing Member would be afforded the choice whether to offset that deficit, in whole or in part, by depositing collateral prior to OCC issuing cash settlement instructions to the Clearing Member's bank. If the Clearing Member were to choose not to deposit additional collateral, OCC would issue cash settlement instructions to the Clearing Member's bank to satisfy the deficit with cash from the Clearing Member's account. But if the Clearing Member were to deposit additional collateral before OCC issued cash settlement instructions to the bank, the newly deposited collateral would reduce or eliminate the amount that OCC would withdraw from the Clearing Member's bank account.
If the proposed change is adopted, OCC will no longer immediately draft the full margin deficit from the Clearing Member's account in cash, but instead will give the Clearing Member the opportunity to satisfy or reduce the deficit with non-cash collateral before OCC conducts any cash draw from Clearing Member bank accounts. This reduces Clearing Members' need for cash liquidity, double-collateralization, and OCC's transactional cash flows and any attendant operational risk.
OCC does not anticipate that this proposed change would negatively affect its liquidity. Start of day liquidity is unaffected because OCC will continue to withdraw cash from Clearing Member bank accounts by Settlement Time each
(
printed page 73849)
day to satisfy any remaining margin deficits, just as it does in the current model. And intraday liquidity will be only minimally affected. In the current model when OCC withdraws cash to satisfy a margin deficit, most of the cash is returned to Clearing Members that same day after the Clearing Members deposit additional non-cash collateral. Finally, the proposed change affects only margin deficits; it will not affect how OCC handles money that flows daily through it from one party to another or how OCC collects mandatory margin cash requirements from time to time. For example, the settlement system by which OCC collects cash from one Clearing Member and passes it along to another Clearing Member would remain unchanged, as would the process for when a Clearing Member defaults. OCC will have qualified liquidity resources supported by all eligible forms of collateral both at the start of the day and intraday under the proposed change.
Description of Change
In order to provide Clearing Members with the opportunity to satisfy daily margin deficits with collateral prior to OCC initiating a cash draw from their bank accounts, OCC proposes to amend its Rules.
[
9
]
In particular OCC proposes amendments to Rule 605 and the creation of a new Rule 605A to implement this change.
OCC proposes to amend Rule 605 to change the name of the report Clearing Members receive identifying their margin deficit from “Daily Margin Report” to “Daily Account Summary.” This change is proposed to more accurately reflect the document that Clearing Members receive on a daily basis that identifies their margin deficit. OCC also proposes shortening and simplifying the rule by simply stating that the Daily Account Summary will show the margin required by the Clearing Member's “margined positions,” rather than listing each type of position that could require margin; however, the types of positions covered in the report will not change. Additionally, OCC proposes to move the sentences requiring that any margin deficit be satisfied by Settlement Time and authorizing OCC to withdraw cash from the Clearing Member's bank account to obtain satisfaction from current Rule 605 to proposed Rule 605A and to make conforming changes, as discussed below.
Rule 605A creates a new term, the “Start-of-Day Margin Deficit,” to represent any remaining margin deficit after a Clearing Member has had the opportunity to deposit collateral to offset the margin deficit identified in the Daily Account Summary. New Rule 605A states that Clearing Members are permitted to deposit such collateral to reduce any margin deficit identified in the Daily Account Summary. Under the new Rule, when OCC receives and recognizes the newly deposited collateral before OCC has issued withdrawal instructions to the Clearing Member's bank, the outstanding margin deficit will be reduced. The margin deficit identified in the Daily Account Summary minus the value of the collateral deposited thereafter is the Start-of-Day Margin Deficit, and subject to the provisions of Rule 606 OCC may withdraw cash from the Clearing Member's bank account to satisfy this deficit.
Finally, the changes to Rule 605 and the creation of Rule 605A will require ancillary changes in Rule 606 to add the term Start-of-Day Margin Deficit and in Rules 606 and 607 to change the term Daily Margin Report to Daily Account Summary.
Implementation Timeframe
OCC expects to implement the proposed changes following receipt of all necessary approvals and within approximately 270 days after the launch of Ovation
[
10
]
as OCC's system of record in light of the technical system changes that are required to implement this change. OCC will announce the implementation date of the proposed changes by an Information Memorandum posted to its public website at least two weeks prior to implementation.
2. Statutory Basis
OCC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 17A of the Exchange Act
[
11
]
and Rules 17ad-22(e)(17) and (21)
[
12
]
thereunder. Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act
[
13
]
requires, among other things, that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in the clearance and settlement of securities transactions and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The proposed change would provide Clearing Members with the option to provide non-cash collateral to satisfy any start-of-day margin deficit rather than requiring a cash draw, fostering OCC's cooperation and coordination with Clearing Members regarding the form of eligible collateral they wish to deposit. The change would also protect investors and the public interest by ensuring that margin deficits are satisfied while also affording Clearing Members the opportunity to select for themselves the collateral to be deposited, maximizing their capital and liquidity efficiency. For these reasons, the proposed changes to OCC's rules are reasonably designed to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in the clearance and settlement of securities transactions and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest in accordance with Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act.
[
14
]
Rule 17ad-22(e)(17)(i)
[
15
]
requires OCC to establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to manage OCC's operational risks by, among other things, identifying the plausible sources of operational risk and mitigating their impact through the use of appropriate systems, policies, procedures, and controls. The proposed change to the start-of-day margin deficit settlement process should reduce or eliminate Clearing Members' need to engage in same-day collateral substitution, thereby reducing or eliminating OCC's operational risk in conducting that process. If Clearing Members deposit collateral to satisfy any margin deficit during the proposed optional window, OCC will no longer need to make cash draws from Clearing Member bank accounts and then return the cash later in the day when the Clearing Member has deposited other collateral. Avoiding this inefficient process eliminates the risk that OCC might make an operational error in the same-day collateral substitution. For those reasons, OCC believes that the proposal is consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(17)(i).
[
16
]
Rule 17ad-22(e)(21)(i) requires OCC to establish, implement, maintain and enforce written policies and procedures reasonably designed to be efficient and effective in meeting the requirements of its participants and the markets it serves, and to regularly review the efficiency and effectiveness of its
(
printed page 73850)
settlement arrangements.
[
17
]
This proposed change promotes efficiency by reducing or eliminating the need for same-day collateral substitution for Clearing Members who wish to take advantage of the optional window to deposit collateral to offset their margin deficits. The change would enable Clearing Members to more efficiently allocate their assets for collateral purposes and avoid intraday double-collateralization. And as noted above, this change would reduce the number of cash draws and returns OCC is required to make to satisfy margin deficits, improving efficiency. For those reasons, OCC believes that the proposal is consistent with Rule 17ad-22(e)(21)(i).
[
18
]
(B) Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
Section 17A(b)(3)(I) of the Act
[
19
]
requires that the rules of a clearing agency not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. OCC does not believe that the proposed rule change would have any impact or impose a burden on competition. All Clearing Members would have the opportunity to deposit non-cash collateral during the optional window, if they so choose. The proposal would not advantage any particular Clearing Members at the expense of others.
(C) Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change  Received From Members, Participants or Others
Written comments were not and are not intended to be solicited with respect to the proposed change and none have been received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
20
]
and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4
[
21
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The proposal shall not take effect until all regulatory actions required with respect to the proposal are completed.
[
22
]
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-OCC-2026-013  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-OCC-2026-013. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of such filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of OCC and on OCC's website at
https://www.theocc.com/​Company-Information/​Documents-and-Archives/​By-Laws-and-Rules
.
Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-OCC-2026-013 and should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106882; File No. SR-Phlx-2026-73]
November 12, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, Nasdaq PHLX LLC (“Nasdaq Phlx” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule General 8, Section 1(b) to provide that the installation fee and ongoing monthly fee for interfirm cabinet connectivity will apply separately to each of the two customers connected through an interfirm cabinet connectivity order, as described further below.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​phlx/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule General 8, Section 1(b) to provide that the installation fee and ongoing monthly fee for interfirm cabinet connectivity will apply separately to each of the two customers connected through an interfirm cabinet connectivity connection, as described below. Currently, the Exchange assesses the applicable installation fee and ongoing monthly fee only to the customer that submits the order. The other customer that accepts and participates in the connection is not separately assessed those fees. Under the proposal, each customer participating in a new interfirm cabinet connectivity connection will be assessed the existing $550 installation fee and $385 ongoing monthly fee for its respective leg of the connectivity path. For interfirm cabinet connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date, the accepting customer will be assessed the ongoing monthly fee, but not the installation fee, for its respective leg, and the fees assessed to the ordering customer will not change.
Background
The Exchange's data center campus consists of the original data center (“NY11”), an initial expansion area (“NY11-4”), and a second expansion area (“NY11-5”) (collectively, the “Data Center” or “Data Center Campus”). Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is a fiber-based connectivity service that links cabinets used by two different colocation customers (“Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity”) throughout the Data Center Campus. The interfirm cabinet connection consists of two customer-side legs that meet at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point:
[
3
]
one leg extends from the first customer's cabinet to the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and the other extends from the Nasdaq-provided distribution point to the second customer's cabinet.
Before the Exchange implemented equalized connectivity
[
4
]
throughout its Data Center, a customer would order Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity through the Nasdaq customer portal and identify the customer to which the ordering customer wanted to connect, with the ordering customer being solely responsible for both the installation and the ongoing monthly fiber connectivity fees. No separate installation or ongoing monthly fees were assessed, or are currently assessed, to the non-ordering customer for its side of the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity.
With respect to provision and installation of the service, the fiber for the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity was provided and installed by a third-party provider or by the customer. The Exchange did not provide or install such fiber or manage such services.
Equalization places greater emphasis on the way Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is supervised and managed, with Nasdaq taking a more central role in those functions. While customers still request the interfirm cabinet connection through the Nasdaq Customer Portal, the pre-existing fiber in the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity has been replaced with Exchange-provided, equalized fiber. Under this structure, the Exchange supervises and audits the interfirm cabinet connection on an ongoing basis.
[
5
]
As discussed above, the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity consists of two customer-side legs that meet at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point: one leg extends from the first customer's cabinet to the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and the other extends from the Nasdaq-provided distribution point to the second customer's cabinet. The Exchange provides and manages the cabling and standardized demarcation points and performs inventory management, implementation support,
(
printed page 73833)
ongoing maintenance, monitoring, audit, and operational oversight for the connection.
Both customers must act before the connection is implemented: one customer initiates the Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity order through the Nasdaq Customer Portal, and the other customer accepts it. If the second customer does not accept the order, the connection is not implemented. Each participating customer consequently receives a distinct customer-side leg of a Nasdaq-provided, Nasdaq-managed, equalized connectivity path. Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is optional and is not required for a customer to obtain colocation services or to connect to the Exchange's trading systems.
Proposal
The Exchange proposes to retain the existing installation and ongoing monthly fees for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity and extend their application to the non-ordering, accepting customer side of the connection. Under the proposal, each customer participating in a new Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connection will be assessed the existing $550 installation fee and $385 ongoing monthly fee for its respective leg of the connectivity path. For Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date, the accepting customer will be assessed the ongoing monthly fee, but not the installation fee, for its respective leg, and the fees assessed to the ordering customer will not change.
The Exchange anticipates implementing the proposed rule change during the first quarter of 2027 and will announce that implementation date through an Equity Trader Alert or other customer communication.
The Exchange believes that assessing the existing fees separately to each customer appropriately reflects the Exchange's increased role in managing Data Center connectivity following Equalization. The Exchange now provides the fiber and manages, supervises, monitors, and audits the connection after installation. The proposal also aligns the allocation of fees with the structure of the service: two separately provided and managed customer-side legs join at the Nasdaq-provided distribution point, and each customer must authorize and receive the benefit of its own leg. The proposal therefore assesses each customer for the Nasdaq-provided and Nasdaq-managed connectivity furnished to that customer.
[
6
]
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
7
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
8
]
in particular, in that it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among members and issuers and other persons using any facility, and is not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed fees are reasonable because each customer receives a distinct leg of an equalized connectivity path that the Exchange actively provides and manages. Each customer-side leg is a defined, Exchange-managed component of that path. Following equalization, the Exchange provides the fiber connectivity and administers the cabling, standardized demarcation points, inventory, and ongoing operational support associated with each leg, and it supervises and audits the connection on an ongoing basis. Each customer's leg is a component the Exchange implements, administers, monitors, and supports. Applying the existing $550 installation fee and $385 monthly fee to each customer is reasonable because each customer receives, and the Exchange manages, a distinct leg of the equalized path.
[
9
]
The Exchange believes this approach equitably allocates the fees among the customers that receive and use each Exchange-managed leg of the connection. Each customer receives connectivity through its respective leg of the connectivity path, and each customer is accordingly responsible for the fees associated with the connectivity provided to it. The fact that the two connectivity paths collectively facilitate communication between the customers does not alter the fact that each customer receives a separately identifiable connectivity service. The Exchange further believes that assessing each customer for its respective connectivity leg avoids requiring one customer to pay for the leg that another customer receives. The Exchange therefore believes that its methodology represents an equitable allocation of fees among the customers using Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity.
The amount of each fee is also reasonable because it is unchanged from the Fiber connectivity fee amounts currently assessed to the ordering customer for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity and is the same amount charged for certain other Fiber connectivity offerings.
[
10
]
The Exchange also believes that the proposal is reasonable because it supports a uniformly administered and
(
printed page 73834)
auditable Interfirm Cabinet connectivity pathway within the Data Center. As the Exchange has explained, equalization is intended to enhance the integrity of the Data Center network by establishing standardized connectivity requirements for each component of the connectivity path and exercising greater management oversight over those components.
[
11
]
A standardized, Nasdaq-managed path in which the Exchange oversees the cabling, demarcation points, and supporting architecture enhances the Exchange's ability to monitor, maintain, and audit that connectivity.
[
12
]
Each customer-side leg of Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is a component of that path. Assessing the existing fees to each customer for its own leg allocates those fees among the customers that receive and use each Exchange-managed leg of the path and does not alter the path's availability or operation.
The Exchange further believes the proposal is reasonable because Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is an optional service. Customers are not required to purchase Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity to obtain colocation services or to connect to the Exchange's trading systems. Rather, a customer purchases the service only if it elects to establish a fiber connection between its cabinet and the cabinet of another colocation customer, and each customer may determine for itself whether the service, at the proposed fees, is appropriate for its business.
The Exchange believes that applying the fees separately to both customers is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because both customers receive a substantially similar customer-side service and both benefit from the Exchange's provision and ongoing management of the equalized path. Under the current billing model, only the ordering customer pays even though the accepting customer also receives a Nasdaq-provided and Nasdaq-managed leg of the connection. The proposal allocates the fees to both beneficiaries and treats the ordering and accepting customers alike. Each customer would pay the same, existing fee for the Exchange-provided and Exchange-managed leg that it receives, and no customer would be asked to bear the fees attributable to another customer's leg of the connection.
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory not to assess the installation fee to the accepting customer for Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity connections already in place as of the implementation date. The installation fee is a one-time charge assessed when a connection is ordered and established. For a connection already in place, the connection has been established and the installation fee has already been assessed to the ordering customer. The Exchange therefore believes that it would be inappropriate to assess a one-time installation charge for a connection that is not being newly established. Those accepting customers will, however, be assessed the ongoing monthly fee beginning on the implementation date, which is consistent with the Exchange's rationale for assessing each customer for the Exchange-managed leg of the connection that it receives and uses. The distinction is drawn by whether a connection is in place as of the implementation date, and not by the identity, size, or trading activity of any customer, and it applies uniformly to every accepting customer with an existing connection.
The Exchange will apply the same fee amounts and billing methodology to all similarly situated customers. The proposal does not distinguish among customers based on their identity, trading activity, or anticipated use of the connection. Rather, each new customer will pay the same installation fee and monthly fee for its own leg of the standardized, equalized connectivity path.
[
13
]
Because both parties must affirmatively participate in the Nasdaq Customer Portal order process before implementation, as described above, each customer will have notice of the fee treatment before the Exchange provisions the connection.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposal will impose an undue burden on intramarket competition because it will apply the same fees to each customer participating in an Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity order. The proposal will eliminate the current difference in the ongoing monthly fee treatment of the ordering and accepting customers, each of which receives a customer-side leg of the Exchange-provided and Exchange-managed connection, and, for new orders, the difference in their installation fee treatment.
The proposal therefore will treat similarly situated customers consistently. Each customer participating in an Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity arrangement through a new order will be assessed the same installation and recurring monthly fees for its respective connectivity leg. For connections already in place as of the implementation date, the Exchange will not assess a one-time installation fee to the accepting customer because the connection has already been established, but the accepting customer will be assessed the same ongoing monthly fee as the ordering customer. This distinction turns on whether a connection is in place as of the implementation date and applies uniformly to all such connections. It does not favor or disadvantage any customer relative to another. The fees do not distinguish among customers based on their identity, business model, trading activity, or the identity of the customer with which they establish connectivity.
The Exchange also does not believe that the proposal will impose an undue burden on intermarket competition. Interfirm Cabinet Connectivity is an optional service that customers are not required to purchase to obtain colocation services or connect to the Exchange's trading systems. The proposal does not alter the availability or technical operation of the service. Instead, it applies the existing fees separately to each customer that elects to participate in and receive a customer-side leg of the connection: for new orders, the existing installation fee and ongoing monthly fee, and for existing connections, the existing ongoing monthly fee.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(ii) of the Act.
[
14
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may
(
printed page 73835)
temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is: (i) necessary or appropriate in the public interest; (ii) for the protection of investors; or (iii) otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-Phlx-2026-73 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-Phlx-2026-73. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-Phlx-2026-73 and should be submitted on or before December 8, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.

15
]

Upon Written Request, Copies Available From:
Securities and Exchange Commission, Office of FOIA Services, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-2736
Notice is hereby given that, pursuant to the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (
44 U.S.C. 3501
et seq.
), the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC or “Commission”) is submitting to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) this request for revision of the proposed collection of information.
Section 4(g)(8) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act),
15 U.S.C. 78d(g)(8)
requires the SEC Ombuds to (i) act as a liaison between the Commission and any retail investor in resolving problems that retail investors may have with the Commission or with self-regulatory organizations (“SROs”); (ii) review and make recommendations regarding policies and procedures to encourage persons to present questions to the Investor Advocate regarding compliance with the securities laws; and (iii) establish safeguards to maintain the confidentiality of communications between the persons described in clause (ii) and the Ombuds. In addition, Section 4(g)(8) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act),
15 U.S.C. 78d(g)(8)
requires the Ombuds to submit a semi-annual report to the Investor Advocate describing the activities and evaluating the effectiveness of the Ombuds during the preceding year.
Each year, the Commission's Office of the Investor Advocate, Office of the Ombuds (“Ombuds”) receives over 2,500 contacts from investors who have complaints or questions about the SEC or any of the self-regulatory organizations that it oversees. To make it easier for the public to contact the Ombuds, the Ombuds created an electronic form (Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form) that provides drop down options to choose from in order to categorize the investor's complaint or question, and may also provide the investor with automated information about their issue. The Ombudsman Matter Management System (OMMS) Submission Form asks investors to provide information concerning, among other things, their names, how they can be reached, the names of the individuals or entities involved, the nature of their complaint or tip, what documents they can provide, and what, if any, actions they have taken. Use of the OMMS Submission Form is voluntary. Absent the forms, the public still has several ways to contact the Ombuds, including telephone, letters, and email. Investors can access the OMMS Submission Form through the Ombuds web page at the web address
https://www.sec.gov/​ombuds
or directly at the web address
https://omms.sec.gov
.
The dual purpose of the OMMS Submission Form is to make it easier for
(
printed page 73838)
the public to contact the agency with complaints, questions, tips, or other feedback and to streamline the workflow of Ombuds staff that record, process, and respond to investor contacts. Investors who submit complaints, ask questions, or provide tips do so voluntarily. Although the OMMS Submission Form provides a structured format for incoming investor correspondence, the Commission does not require that investors use any particular form or format when contacting the Ombuds. Investors who choose not to use the OMMS Submission Form will receive the same level of service as those who do.
The Ombuds receives approximately 1,500 contacts each year through the Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form. The Ombudsman uses the information that investors supply on the Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form to review and process the contact (which may, in turn, involve responding to questions, processing complaints, or, as appropriate, referring matters to enforcement or examinations for potential investigations), to maintain a record of contacts, to track the volume of investor complaints, and to analyze trends.
This proposed collection is a revision of the previously approved collection for OMMS. The OMMS Submission Form is being revised to include a new information type. Specifically, the user of the revised OMMS Submission Form will be asked to respond to a prepopulated list, which asks whether the submitter is a: Individual Investor; Registered Representative; Accountant; Other Financial Professional; Issuer/Attorney for an Issuer; Brokerage Firm Compliance Officer; Academic/Researcher/Student; Member of the Press.
The staff of the Commission estimates that the total reporting burden for using the Ombudsman Matter Management System Submission Form is 750 hours. The calculation of this estimate depends on the number of investors who use the forms each year and the estimated time it takes to complete the forms: 1,500 respondents × 30 minutes = 750 burden hours.
An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB Control Number.

https://www.reginfo.gov/​public/​do/​PRAViewICR?​ref_​nbr=​202608-3235-007
or email comment to
MBX.OMB.OIRA.SEC_desk_officer@omb.eop.gov
within 30 days of the day after publication of this notice, by December 18, 2026.
Dated: November 12, 2026.

Assistant Secretary.

An entity conducting an exempt cross-border business combination or rights offering is required to file a Form CB (
17 CFR 249.480
) to the extent the party would have had a filing obligation if the transaction were not eligible for the exemption. Form CB is intended to help the Commission determine whether a transaction meets the eligibility requirements of the exemptive rules. Form CB also helps to ensure that information about the transaction is publicly available in order to help security holders make informed investment decisions. The information required by Form CB is mandatory, and Form CB filings are publicly available on the Commission's Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval (“EDGAR”) system. We estimate that approximately 49 respondents make one Form CB filing per year, for a total of approximately 49 responses annually. We estimate that respondents incur approximately 0.12 burden hours per Form CB filing, for a total annual reporting burden of 6 hours (0.12 hours per response × 49 responses). We estimate that respondents incur $225 cost burden per Form CB filing, for a total annual cost burden of $11,025 ($225 cost per response × 49 responses).
